You are working in the repository of Yeah itself — an Emacs Lisp agent harness that lives in this directory. This is the first half of wave 42 of the owner's plan (docs/PLAN.md §18.2 — read that section, it is the specification of this task).

The defect, as the plan names it:

- The process of the ACP server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it. This half of the wave is about that life cycle. (The second half — a server that spins when the provider is silent — is NOT this task; do not register that claim and do not try to localize the spin here.)

The claim of this half, as the plan names it:

- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open. The control must break the subject, and the check must then fail by its own assertion: the control keeps the client sitting on an open pipe and takes out the way the server ends when its session is over, so the server survives and the check catches it.

The exit criterion of this half: a server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.

What to do:

1. Find out how the server process is started and how it is ended today. Do not guess: start real servers with the tools you have, look at the processes, and name the places you find (file and line). The places to look first are lib/yeah-service.el, lib/yeah-wire-socket.el, lib/yeah-acp.el and lib/yeah-emacs.el, but the truth is where it is.
2. Implement the way for the server to end that does not depend on the client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.
3. Write an end-to-end check `tests/checks/check-the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over.el` that starts a real server process, ends the session while the client keeps the pipe open, and asserts that the process is gone within ten seconds. The check must decide its verdict by construction: the same input gives the same verdict every time. Look at how the existing checks of this repository are written and at how the claims declare their controls (spec.json) — a control of a claim is a command that the method applies to a copy of the tree, and yours must break the subject.
4. Register the claim in spec.json with that control, and prove the control bites: apply the control to a copy of the tree and show that your check fails with the exit code 1 and with its own words.
5. Document the wave: `waves/wave-42.json` with the fields the other wave files have (intent, touches, checks, claims, commitment, objection, refuted_by, note), an execution note in `docs/PLAN.md` §18.2, and a bullet in `AGENTS.md` next to the bullets of the other waves. Say plainly what you did not prove.
6. Verify what you changed: `./scripts/dev byte-compile-all`, `./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el`, and your new check file. Do not run `./scripts/dev run` and do not run the whole suite `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*`.

One rule about the observation of this run: the journal of the run lives under `sessions/` in this repository. Never delete it and never delete anything else to make a check pass. If a check of yours deletes a file to prove something, that file must be a file the check itself created in a temporary directory.

# PLAN — the road to Yeah 1.0

> **Status: execution plan, not current capability.** The target and its
> rationale are in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; binding engineering rules are in
> `docs/ENGINEERING.md`. The machine-checked present is `spec.json` and
> `./scripts/dev map`.
>
> This plan introduces eight **stages**. Existing `waves/wave-01.json` …
> `wave-14.json` remain the historical math-coding units until corresponding
> new claims/waves are added. A stage is not considered closed here: closure
> requires the specification and its evidence to agree.

## 1. Current baseline

Verified on 2026-11-15 on `main` (the numbers of 2026-11-14 in the integration
branch were 319/319, 46 and 55):

- all 53 Elisp files under `lib/` byte-compile without warnings;
- 358/358 ERT unit tests pass;
- all 53 canaries pass when run directly (`./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*`);
- the installed math-coding v5 tool runs the standing specification: all 74
  claims hold, and every negative control changes its scoped subject and
  makes the verifier fail with an assertion;
- live provider behavior remains verified on 2026-11-12: the live coding task
  (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) reads the project, edits the file with a guarded edit,
  saves it, and the test of the project passes, and the interactive UI
  path (journal, cancel, quit, restart, resume, recover) works against a
  live provider.  The clean-Emacs install path is network-tested against the
  published repository (`tests/live/live-clean-install.el`).

The code contains a working kernel and a working wire, but not yet a usable
product:

- the stdio wire server answers one request at a time: a cancel that
  arrives while a prompt runs is read after that prompt settles.  The
  socket transport (`lib/yeah-wire-socket.el`) does not have this limit —
  a cancel arrives while the prompt is still running;
- the emacsclient bridge was checked against a live Emacs server (a real
  daemon) by `tests/checks/check-bridge-live-server.el`, but not yet against
  a person's Emacs in day-to-day use;
- concurrent sessions in one Emacs are isolated per run context: sessions,
  permissions, cancellation, budgets and the advertised tools are the run's
  own, and two sessions in one Emacs are checked for cross-talk;
- the PTC whitelist was experimentally bypassed with a permitted higher-order
  function and a quoted `delete-file` symbol. It is not a safe boundary.

payload:
## 18. The plan of the next waves

The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az), after the
report on the readiness of Yeah for self-development and after the
integration with the orchestrator Paseo.  The decision is recorded by the
method as the judgment claim `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`
(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

**The execution (2026-11-17).**  The wave was carried out by the harness
itself: a live model (`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`) worked on a copy of the repository
in a live run of Yeah, and the journals of the copy
(`sessions/wave41g.jsonl`, `sessions/wave41h.jsonl`) hold the run.  The model
wrote the check of the wave
(`tests/checks/check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el`) and
found three defects in it while it worked: the keys of a JSON object come as
symbols from Emacs 30 (so the control of the claim of the bridge was never
found and the check said "the claim of the bridge declares no control to
run"), `file-copy-file` does not create the directory of the target, and the
buffer of the words of a run was bound in a `let` that binds in parallel (the
filter of the process saw a void variable).  The model registered the new
claim in `spec.json` with a control that breaks the determinism of the check,
and it did not touch the claim of the bridge, whose control bit ten times of
ten.  The first run was killed by the machine after the changes were made and
verified; the second run picked the work up from the tree, checked the three
criteria of the exit and finished through the `finish` tool (the state of the
run was `completed`).  The evidence of the wave is in docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md,
the section "The self-development run that finished the wave 41".

**What the execution does not prove.**  The wave repairs the evidence of the
bridge; it does not repair the harness and it does not measure the parity of

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.

;;; yeah-service.el --- a service Emacs running the Yeah harness -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The primary placement: a dedicated Emacs process runs the harness, so
;; the editing Emacs never shares a thread with a long turn.  This module
;; starts such a service, connects to it and stops it.  The service
;; serves ACP on a Unix-domain socket, or on a loopback TCP port when the
;; platform has no Unix socket; a cancel is handled while a prompt is still
;; running.
;;
;; The service runs the same Emacs as the person: the program is resolved
;; when the service starts, and the running binary is the fallback, so a
;; service starts on a machine where `emacs' is not on PATH.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-client)
(require 'yeah-wire-socket)

(defgroup yeah-service nil
  "A service Emacs running the Yeah harness."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-service-emacs
  (or (executable-find "emacs")
      (and (file-executable-p (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
           (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
      invocation-name)
  "The Emacs program that runs the service."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-service)

(defvar yeah-service--processes (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map a service name to its process.")

(defun yeah-service--emacs-program ()
  "Return the program that runs the service Emacs.

The service runs the SAME Emacs as the person: the binary that is
running now, when the platform can name it.  A program name that the
PATH does not carry would make the service impossible to start on a
machine where Emacs lives in a profile, so the running binary is the
fallback, and `EMACS' comes before it."
  (let ((configured (or yeah-service-emacs "emacs")))
    (cond
     ((or (file-name-absolute-p configured)
          (file-directory-p configured))
      configured)
     ((executable-find configured) (executable-find configured))
     ((and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS")))
      (getenv "EMACS"))
     ((file-executable-p "/proc/self/exe") "/proc/self/exe")
     ((file-executable-p (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
     (t configured))))

(defun yeah-service--socket-directory ()
  "Return the user-private directory the service sockets live in.
Anyone who can connect to the socket drives the agent with the person's
permissions, so the socket never sits in a world-writable /tmp: it goes
under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR when there is one, else under a directory of this
user with mode 0700."
  (let ((dir (if-let ((runtime (getenv "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")))
                 (expand-file-name "yeah" runtime)
               (expand-file-name (format "yeah-%d" (user-uid))
                                 (or (getenv "TMPDIR") "/tmp")))))
    (unless (file-directory-p dir)
      (make-directory dir t)
      (set-file-modes dir #o700))
    dir))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-socket-path (name)
  "Return the socket path of the service NAME."
  (expand-file-name (format "yeah-service-%s.sock" name)
                    (yeah-service--socket-directory)))

(defun yeah-service--socket-path (name)
  "Return the socket path of the service NAME."
  (yeah-service-socket-path name))

(defun yeah-service--reserve-loopback-port ()
  "Return an unused loopback TCP port.
The probe binds the port briefly so the service child can bind the same
port without choosing a fixed, commonly occupied number."
  (let ((probe
         (make-network-process
          :name (format "yeah-service-port-%d" (random 1000000000))
          :server t
          :family 'ipv4
          :service 0
          :noquery t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((port (process-contact probe :service)))
          (unless (and (integerp port) (> port 0) (<= port 65535))
            (signal 'user-error
                    (list "yeah-service-start: could not reserve a TCP port")))
          port)
      (when (process-live-p probe)
        (delete-process probe)))))

(defun yeah-service--write-port-file (socket port)
  "Publish PORT for SOCKET in the port file next to its socket path.
The file contains the port number only; it is not a credential."
  (let ((file (yeah-client-port-file socket)))
    (with-temp-file file
      (insert (number-to-string port)))
    (set-file-modes file #o600)
    file))

(defun yeah-service--lib-directory ()
  "Return the directory holding Yeah's Elisp modules."
  (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-acp") "yeah-acp.el")))

(defun yeah-service--rules-eval (rules)
  "Return the Elisp that installs RULES in the service.
RULES is a list of permission rule plists, as `yeah-perm-rule-make'
builds them; the service adds each of them to its own ruleset."
  (if (null rules)
      ""
    (format "(dolist (rule '%S) (yeah-perm-rules-add rule))" rules)))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-start (name &optional extra-eval data-home transport clean rules)
  "Start a service Emacs named NAME and return its process.
The service serves ACP on a Unix-domain socket, or on a loopback TCP port
when `yeah-client-network-family' selects `ipv4'.  In the TCP case the port
number is published in a `.port' file next to the socket path.  EXTRA-EVAL
is evaluated in the service before the server starts (to configure the
model backend); DATA-HOME is the service's data directory; TRANSPORT is a
form evaluating to the model transport of the service (nil uses the
default).  A service with the same name is not started twice.
CLEAN (the default) starts the service without the user's init; nil lets
the service inherit the user's configuration, including the gptel backend.
RULES is a list of permission rule plists: the standing permissions the
person grants the service, which is how a headless service may edit at
all."
  (let ((existing (gethash name yeah-service--processes)))
    (when (and existing (process-live-p existing))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-service-start: %S is already running" name)))))
  (let* ((socket (yeah-service--socket-path name))
         (family (yeah-client-effective-network-family))
         (port (when (eq family 'ipv4)
                 (yeah-service--reserve-loopback-port)))
         (server-form
          (if (eq family 'local)
              (format "(yeah-acp-serve-socket %S %s)"
                      socket
                      (or transport "yeah-acp-default-transport"))
            (format "(yeah-acp-serve-socket %d %s nil 'ipv4)"
                    port
                    (or transport "yeah-acp-default-transport"))))
         (buffer (generate-new-buffer (format " *yeah service %s*" name)))
         (process
          (make-process
           :name (format "yeah-service-%s" name)
           :buffer buffer
           :command
           (append (list (yeah-service--emacs-program))
                   (if clean (list "-Q" "--batch") (list "--batch"))
                   (list "-L" (yeah-service--lib-directory)
                         "-l" "yeah-acp"
                         "--eval"
                         (format "(progn %s %s %s %s)"
                                 (or extra-eval "")
                                 (if data-home
                                     (format "(setq yeah-data-home %S)" data-home)
                                   "")
                                 (yeah-service--rules-eval rules)
                                 server-form)))
           :connection-type 'pipe
           :noquery t)))
    (when (eq family 'ipv4)
      (condition-case error
          (yeah-service--write-port-file socket port)
        (error
         (delete-process process)
         (signal (car error) (cdr error)))))
    (puthash name process yeah-service--processes)
    process))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-connect (name &optional timeout)
  "Connect to the service NAME and return the connection process.
Waits up to TIMEOUT seconds (default 10) for the socket to appear."
  (let ((socket (yeah-service-socket-path-internal name))
        (deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 10)))
        (connection nil))
    (while (and (null connection) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (setq connection (yeah-client--open-connection socket))

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## Current warnings for every agent

- This is a kernel prototype, not a usable coding product.
- The parity with other harnesses was piloted on 2026-11-15, and the
  difference the pilot found was a defect of the turn, not a difference of
  quality: after the results of the tool calls arrive, the model may answer
  with an empty message, and the turn took that as the end of the work and
  stopped without the effect (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot of the
  parity").  The defect is fixed (the claim
  `an-empty-answer-does-not-end-the-run'), and the pilot on the fixed turn
  moved one task of three; the nudge now carries the state of the work
  (the claim `a-silence-nudge-carries-the-state-of-the-work'), because the
  provider goes silent after every batch of tool results and the model was
  answering the nudge by starting the work over.  With that, Yeah passes
  two tasks of three and pi passes three.  The third task failed in the

;;; yeah-wire-socket.el --- the socket transport for Yeah's wire protocols -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The stdio transport of a wire protocol reads standard input with a
;; blocking read.  While that read blocks, the event loop of Emacs does
;; not run, so a notification that arrives while a request is being
;; answered is read only after the answer settled.  A reader thread does
;; not help: a thread blocked in `read-string' holds the interpreter lock,
;; and the whole Emacs stops until the read returns.
;;
;; A socket does help.  Emacs represents a connection as a process, so the
;; data of a connection arrives in a filter and the event loop keeps
;; running while the server waits.  A `session/cancel' that arrives during
;; a running prompt is therefore handled while the prompt is still
;; running, and two connections can be served at the same time.
;;
;; The transport is a local Unix socket by default; `ipv4' serves a
;; loopback TCP port instead.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire-socket nil
  "The socket transport of Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defvar yeah-wire-socket--pending (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "The part of the last line received on each connection.")

(defun yeah-wire-socket--lines (connection chunk)
  "Return the complete lines in CHUNK for CONNECTION and keep the rest.
The incomplete tail of CONNECTION is kept for the next chunk."
  (let* ((pending (gethash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending ""))
         (combined (concat pending chunk))
         (parts (split-string combined "\n"))
         (complete (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                        parts
                      (butlast parts)))
         (tail (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                    ""
                  (car (last parts)))))
    (puthash connection tail yeah-wire-socket--pending)
    complete))

(defun yeah-wire-socket--respond (connection text)
  "Send TEXT to CONNECTION as one line."
  (when (process-live-p connection)
    (process-send-string connection (concat text "\n"))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-server (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Listen on the local socket SERVICE and serve connections with HANDLER.
FAMILY is `local' for a Unix socket and `ipv4' for a loopback TCP port.
HANDLER is called with (LINE RESPOND CONNECTION) for every complete line
of input; RESPOND takes one message and sends it back to that connection.
ON-CLOSE, when given, is called with CONNECTION after it closed: a
question asked of a dead connection must not hang the server.
Return the server process."
  (make-network-process
   :name "yeah-wire-socket"
   :server t
   :family (or family 'local)
   :service service
   :noquery t
   :sentinel
   (when on-close
     (lambda (connection _event)
       (when (memq (process-status connection) '(closed failed exit))
         (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending)
         (funcall on-close connection))))
   :filter
   (lambda (connection chunk)
     (cond
      ((string= chunk "")
       (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending))
      (t
       (dolist (line (yeah-wire-socket--lines connection chunk))
         (unless (string-blank-p line)
           (funcall handler line
                    (lambda (text) (yeah-wire-socket--respond connection text))
                    connection))))))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-serve (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Serve connections on SERVICE with HANDLER until the server stops.
FAMILY, HANDLER and ON-CLOSE mean what they mean in
`yeah-wire-socket-server'."
  (let ((server (yeah-wire-socket-server service handler family on-close)))
    (while (process-live-p server)
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05))
    server))

(provide 'yeah-wire-socket)
;;; yeah-wire-socket.el ends here

found three defects in it while it worked: the keys of a JSON object come as
symbols from Emacs 30 (so the control of the claim of the bridge was never

filter of the process saw a void variable).  The model registered the new
claim in `spec.json` with a control that breaks the determinism of the check,
and it did not touch the claim of the bridge, whose control bit ten times of
ten.  The first run was killed by the machine after the changes were made and
verified; the second run picked the work up from the tree, checked the three
criteria of the exit and finished through the `finish` tool (the state of the
run was `completed`).  The evidence of the wave is in docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md,
the section "The self-development run that finished the wave 41".

**What the execution does not prove.**  The wave repairs the evidence of the
bridge; it does not repair the harness and it does not measure the parity of
the harnesses.  The second criterion of the exit (two consecutive runs of the
method that end in `green`) depends on the human review of the plan of the
owner being fresh at the time of the run: that review is a decision of the
owner and not a machine verifier (docs/PLAN.md 17.2), and any later edit of
this plan makes it stale again.  The runs, their verdicts and their dates are
in docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.
4. The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
   with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`, since wave 40), but
   no `kind`: a client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read,
   an edit, a shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The
   arguments of a call are positional, so a client that looks for named
   fields (`path`, `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.

**What changes.**  The gaps are closed in the order of what the live
integration needs today: the `cwd` first, because the agent must work in the
repository of the task; then the `kind` of the call and its named arguments,
because the client must be able to show what the agent did; then
`session/set_mode`; then the model of the session; then the `mcpServers` of
the session, whose tools do not reach the model today.

**The claims.**  Each gap is a claim of its own, and the name of the claim is
the name of the gap: `a-session-runs-in-its-own-directory`,
`a-tool-call-carries-its-kind`, `a-tool-call-carries-named-arguments`,
`a-session-changes-its-permission-profile-over-the-wire`,
`a-session-changes-its-model-over-the-wire`,
`the-mcp-servers-of-a-session-reach-the-model`.

**The exit criteria.**
1. The check of the `cwd` sends a session into a temporary directory, and the
   tool of that session sees the temporary directory and not the directory of
   the process.
2. The plugin of Paseo runs a turn in the repository of the task, and the
   timeline of the client shows the kind of the call of the tool.
3. The wire answers `session/set_mode` and no longer answers `-32601`.

**The estimate.**  Two to three days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The
wire of Yeah is ACP plus the one extension that was announced
(`yeah.queueEvents`); this wave adds no method that ACP does not have.

### 18.4 Wave 44 — parallel children in a live turn

**The defect.**  Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the
audit of wave 35 proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What
is not proven is a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live
provider.  No child of a live provider has run on a model other than the
model of its parent, and the live checks do not exercise the delegation at
all: the benchmark gives its runs a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is
not among them.

**What changes.**  The live check grows a second child in the same turn of
the parent, and the offline check with a fake model becomes the claim that
the map binds — the live check lives outside the map, because it needs a

**The claims.**

1. The offline check passes and its control bites.
2. The live check with a real provider shows two children in one turn of the

;;

;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Agent-side ACP v1 over newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0.  Sessions are real
;; Yeah sessions; prompt responses are sent when the run reaches a terminal
;; state; session/cancel is a notification; journal events become
;; session/update notifications through `yeah-events-write-functions'.
;;
;; A session is driven by a controller: the same one the attached path uses.
;; The controller owns the session's turn and its persistent pending queue,
;; so the wire can ask, steer, cancel, withdraw a pending input and recover
;; one.  There is no second queue in this module: the pending inputs of a
;; session are the ones the control keeps, and the queue the editor sees is
;; a projection of the journal -- the events that move an input in or out of
;; the queue reach the client as session/update notifications.
;;
;; `session/load' opens a session again and replays its journal: the records
;; of the session become session/update notifications, so that an editor can
;; rebuild the transcript of a session it opens a second time.
;;
;; An answer to a permission that arrives after the run that asked has ended
;; is not applied: the journal shows the question as deferred and the run as
;; ended, and the late answer changes nothing.
;;
;; The protocol is spoken over two transports.  On stdio the server reads
;; standard input with a blocking read, so a notification that arrives
;; while a prompt is running is read only after the prompt settled.  On a
;; socket the connection is a process, the data arrives in a filter and the
;; event loop keeps running, so a cancellation is handled while the prompt
;; is still running.  `yeah-acp-serve-socket' is the transport of the
;; primary deployment.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-acp-vocabulary)
(require 'yeah-control)
(require 'yeah-events)
(require 'yeah-product)
(require 'yeah-result)
(require 'yeah-turn)
(require 'yeah-wire)
(require 'yeah-wire-socket)

(defgroup yeah-acp nil
  "Yeah ACP v1 agent."
  :group 'yeah)

(defconst yeah-acp--agent-name "yeah")
(defconst yeah-acp--agent-version "0.1.0")

(defvar yeah-acp--sessions (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map ACP session ids to their Yeah session state.")

(defvar yeah-acp--pending-permissions (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map permission request ids to the question they ask.
The value names the session, the action and the resource, so that the
answer reaches the turn that asked and may be remembered for the
session.")

(defvar yeah-acp--connection nil
  "The connection being served, bound dynamically by the socket handler.
A session remembers which connection owns it, so the death of that
connection can cancel the work it started.")

(defvar yeah-acp--client-capabilities (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "Map every connection to the capabilities its client announced.
The key is the connection; the standard output connection is the key
nil.  What a client announced at `initialize' says what it
understands of the wire.")

(defun yeah-acp--jsonable-args (args)
  "Return ARGS as a JSON value: an array when every element serializes,
the printed form otherwise."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((array (apply #'vector args)))
        (ignore (json-serialize array))
        array)
    (error (format "%S" args))))

(defun yeah-acp--session-rules (session-id)
  "Return the permission rules that decide for SESSION-ID.
The standing permissions of the service come first and the decisions the
client remembered for this session come last: the last match wins."
  (let ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id)))
    (append (yeah-perm-rules-list) (plist-get state :rules))))

(defun yeah-acp--ask-client (session-id output request)
  "Ask the client about REQUEST and return the deferral of the question.
The question carries three answers: allow once, allow always (the decision
is remembered for the session) and reject.  The question itself is kept,
so that the answer reaches the turn that asked and may be remembered."
  (let* ((request-id (yeah-acp--fresh-id "perm"))
         (params (list :sessionId session-id
                       :toolCall (list :toolCallId request-id
                                       :title (format "%s on %s"
                                                      (plist-get request :action)
                                                      (plist-get request :resource))
                                       :rawInput
                                       (yeah-acp--jsonable-args
                                        (plist-get request :args)))
                       :options (vector
                                 (list :optionId "allow-once"
                                       :name "Allow once" :kind "allow_once")
                                 (list :optionId "allow-always"
                                       :name "Allow always" :kind "allow_always")
                                 (list :optionId "reject-once"
                                       :name "Reject" :kind "reject_once")))))
    (puthash request-id
             (list :session-id session-id
                   :action (plist-get request :action)
                   :resource (plist-get request :resource))
             yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
    (funcall output (json-serialize
                     (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id request-id
                           :method "session/request_permission"
                           :params params)))
    (list :defer request-id)))

(defun yeah-acp--client-answerer (session-id output)
  "Return the answerer of SESSION-ID that asks the client over the wire.
The rules decide first; what they do not name is asked of the client as a
`session/request_permission', and the call waits for the answer.  A safe
read needs no question: it is allowed, and it says why."
  (lambda (request)
    (let* ((action (plist-get request :action))
           (resource (plist-get request :resource))
           (effect (yeah-perm-effect action resource
                                     (yeah-acp--session-rules session-id))))
      (pcase effect
        ('allow (list :effect :allow :reply :once))
        ('deny (list :effect :deny :reply :reject
                     :reason (format "the rules deny %s on %s"
                                     action resource)))
        (_ (or (yeah-approval-safe-read-decision request)
               (yeah-acp--ask-client session-id output request)))))))

(defvar yeah-acp--counter 0
  "Monotonic counter for generated identifiers.")

(defvar yeah-acp--transport nil
  "Optional model transport used by the ACP server.")

(defvar yeah-acp-default-transport nil
  "Model transport of the service when none is passed at start.
A service init file (`yeah-service-init-file') sets this; nil falls back
to the gptel transport of the service's own configuration.")

(defvar yeah-acp--answerer nil
  "Optional permission answerer used by the ACP server.")

(defvar yeah-acp--output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line
  "Function receiving one serialized JSON message per call.")

(defvar yeah-acp--output nil
  "Output function of the connection being served, or nil for standard output.
This variable is bound dynamically while a connection is served, so the
messages of one connection do not reach another one.")

(defun yeah-acp--session-answerer (state)
  "Return the answerer of STATE: the client of the session over the wire.
The rules of the session decide first; what they do not name is asked of
the client as a `session/request_permission', and the call waits for the
answer.  The question is asked of the connection the session belongs to."

             request)))

(defun yeah-acp--make-control (state)
  "Return the controller of STATE.
The controller owns the turn of the session and its persistent pending
queue: the wire and the attached path share one queue, one set of journal
events and one set of semantics.  The transport and the answerer are the
service's, and the working directory travels with every input."
  (yeah-control-new (plist-get state :session)
                    (or yeah-acp--transport yeah-acp-default-transport)
                    (yeah-acp--session-answerer state)
                    nil nil
                    (list :cwd (plist-get state :cwd))))

(defun yeah-acp-version ()
  "Return the ACP protocol version spoken by Yeah."
  yeah-acp-protocol-version)

(defun yeah-acp--print-line (text)
  "Write TEXT and a newline to standard output.
The bytes of a serialized message are UTF-8, and they are written as
they are: `yeah-wire-print-line' knows how."
  (yeah-wire-print-line text))

(defun yeah-acp--emit (object)
  "Serialize OBJECT and pass it to the output function of this connection."
  (funcall (or yeah-acp--output yeah-acp--output-function
               #'yeah-acp--print-line)
           (json-serialize object)))

(defun yeah-acp--response (id result)
  "Return a JSON-RPC response string for ID and RESULT."
  (json-serialize (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id :result result)))

(defun yeah-acp--error (id code message)
  "Return a JSON-RPC error response string for ID, CODE and MESSAGE."
  (json-serialize
   (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id
         :error (list :code code :message message))))

(defun yeah-acp--fresh-id (prefix)
  "Return a fresh id beginning with PREFIX."
  (setq yeah-acp--counter (1+ yeah-acp--counter))
  (format "%s-%d-%x" prefix yeah-acp--counter (random #x1000000)))

(defun yeah-acp--session-state (session-id &optional required)

  "Return ARGS as a JSON value for the wire.

client that shows the call wants the values themselves, so the printed form
is read back into them.

not as code: a form that the reader would evaluate is not read at all, and
the printed form travels to the client as it is."

          (if (string-match-p "#\\." args)

                           :toolCallId tool-call-id

carry is left out of the update."

    (when-let ((input-id (plist-get fields :input_id)))
      (plist-put update :inputId input-id))
    (when-let ((input-kind (or (plist-get fields :input_kind)
                                (plist-get fields :kind))))
      (plist-put update :inputKind input-kind))
    (when-let ((prompt (plist-get fields :prompt)))
      (plist-put update :content (vector (list :type "text" :text prompt))))

      (plist-put update :reason reason))

;;

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; This file defines the current 20 transitions of the agent-loop FSM and
;; exposes `yeah-loop-tick', which returns the next state for a state/event
;; pair or signals `user-error' for an invalid transition.  The target
;; invariants are valid, bounded and recoverable transitions, not a permanent
;; transition count; see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md' and `docs/PLAN.md'.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-state)

(defconst yeah-loop--raw-transitions
  '(;; happy path
    (idle           user-prompt     . deciding)
    (idle           tick-resume     . deciding)
    (deciding       stream-end      . post-decide)
    (post-decide    no-tool-calls   . completed)
    (post-decide    tool-call       . awaiting-tool)
    (post-decide    permission-ask  . awaiting-user-permission)
    (post-decide    ask-user        . awaiting-user-input)
    ;; the model is asked again, with the results of what was dispatched
    (post-decide    continue        . deciding)
    ;; the model answered with nothing usable: the run failed
    (deciding       error           . failed)
    (awaiting-tool  tool-end        . accumulating)
    (accumulating   budget-ok       . post-decide)
    (accumulating   budget-overflow . compacting)
    (compacting     compact-done    . post-decide)
    (blocked-on-rate rate-relief    . deciding)
    ;; interrupt fan-in (two sources)
    (deciding       interrupt       . interrupted)
    (awaiting-tool  interrupt       . interrupted)
    ;; wait-state timeouts
    (awaiting-user-permission timeout . failed)
    (awaiting-user-permission answer  . post-decide)
    (awaiting-user-input     timeout . failed)
    (awaiting-user-input     answer  . post-decide))
  "The 20 raw transition cells.
Each cell has the shape (FROM LABEL . TO). The runtime
transition table is built from this list at load time so that
the count can be checked.")

(unless (= 20 (length yeah-loop--raw-transitions))
  (error "yeah-loop: transition count drift; expected 20, got %d"
         (length yeah-loop--raw-transitions)))

(defvar yeah-loop-transitions yeah-loop--raw-transitions
  "The current FSM transition cells, each with shape (FROM LABEL . TO).
Changes must keep the run bounded and recoverable and be reflected in
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md', `docs/PLAN.md' and the relevant checks.")

(defun yeah-loop--find-transition (from label)
  "Return the destination state for the transition FROM
triggered by LABEL, or nil if no such transition exists."
  (catch 'found
    (dolist (cell yeah-loop-transitions nil)
      (when (and (eq (nth 0 cell) from)
                 (eq (nth 1 cell) label))
        (throw 'found (nthcdr 2 cell))))))

(defun yeah-loop-transition-p (from label)
  "Return non-nil when FROM has a transition on LABEL."
  (and (yeah-state-p from)
       (symbolp label)
       (yeah-loop--find-transition from label)))

(defun yeah-loop-tick (from label)
  "One step of the agent loop.

Return the next state when LABEL is a valid transition from
FROM. Signal `user-error' otherwise. The function is pure:
no global state, no IO, no side effects.

FROM must satisfy `yeah-state-p'; LABEL must be a symbol."
  (unless (yeah-state-p from)
    (signal 'user-error (list (format "yeah-loop-tick: not a FSM state: %S" from))))
  (unless (symbolp label)
    (signal 'user-error (list (format "yeah-loop-tick: label must be a symbol, got %S" label))))
  (let ((to (yeah-loop--find-transition from label)))
    (unless to
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-loop-tick: no transition from %S on %S" from label))))
    to))

(defun yeah-loop-transition-count ()
  "Return the number of transitions in `yeah-loop-transitions'."
  (declare (pure t) (side-effect-free t))
  (length yeah-loop-transitions))

(provide 'yeah-loop)

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; In batch mode Emacs reads standard input a line at a time with
;; `read-string'; `read-char' does not see it.  A server therefore reads one
;; request, then pumps the event loop until the work it started has settled,
;; so asynchronous answers leave immediately instead of waiting for the next
;; request.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire nil
  "Shared stdio plumbing for Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defun yeah-wire-read-line ()
  "Read one line from standard input.
Return the line without its newline, or nil at end of file."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((line (read-string "")))
        (if (or (null line) (string= line "")) nil line))
    (error nil)))

(defun yeah-wire-print-line (text)
  "Write TEXT and a newline to standard output.
TEXT is one message of a wire protocol, serialized as JSON.  The
serializer returns a unibyte string whose bytes are UTF-8, and printing
such a string as it is makes Emacs read every byte as a character of
Latin-1 and write it back as UTF-8: the client reads the text twice
over, and a Russian answer arrives as mojibake.  The bytes are decoded
as UTF-8 before they are printed, so the client reads what the model
wrote.

(defun yeah-acp--connection-closed (connection)
  "Cancel the work CONNECTION started and forget its pending questions.

turn is cancelled with the reason in the journal, and the request ids
of the dead connection are dropped."
  (let ((sessions nil))

     (lambda (id state)
       (when (eq connection (plist-get state :connection))

     yeah-acp--sessions)
    (let ((stale nil))
      (maphash (lambda (id question)

               yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
      (dolist (id stale)

    (dolist (session-id sessions)

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-tools)

(declare-function gptel-request "gptel"

(defvar gptel-tools nil)
(defvar gptel-include-reasoning nil)
(defvar gptel-use-context nil)

(defgroup yeah-gptel nil
  "Yeah / private gptel transport adapter."
  :group 'yeah)

(defconst yeah-gptel--supported-versions '("0.9.9.5" "0.9.9.6")
  "gptel versions whose request contract has been checked by Yeah.")

(defcustom yeah-gptel-prelude
  (concat
   "# Yeah — system prompt\n\n"
   "You are Yeah, an agent running inside Emacs through the Yeah harness. "
   "Act with the advertised tools; do not narrate what you are about to do. "
   "Read files with `read', find files with `glob' and `grep', change them "
   "with `edit', and run commands with `bash'. Your edits are saved to disk. "
   "When the work is done and verified, call the `finish' tool with a summary. "
   "A text answer that only describes what you will do is not a completion: "
   "it is answered with a nudge naming the tools you have not called yet.\n")
  "Default system prompt for Yeah model requests.
A model that is only told to be helpful narrates its plan instead of acting.
The harness asks for actions, not for a plan."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-gptel)

(defcustom yeah-gptel-include-reasoning t
  "How the model's reasoning is kept in the conversation.
A model that reasons narrates its plan, and dropping that plan from the
history makes the model start the task over on every turn.  Keep the
reasoning in the conversation by default; set this to nil to hide it.
The value is bound per request, never mutated globally."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Keep the reasoning" t)
                 (const :tag "Hide it" nil))
  :group 'yeah-gptel)

(defun yeah-gptel--require-gptel (what)
  "Signal `user-error' unless gptel is available, naming WHAT wanted it."
  (unless (fboundp 'gptel-request)
    (signal 'user-error

continuing with an incompatible transport."
  (yeah-gptel--require-gptel "yeah-gptel-check-contract")
  (unless (and (boundp 'gptel-version)
               (stringp gptel-version))
    (signal 'user-error
            (list "yeah-gptel: loaded gptel does not expose `gptel-version'")))
  (unless (member gptel-version yeah-gptel--supported-versions)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-gptel: unsupported gptel version %S; supported: %s"
                          gptel-version

                      gptel-use-tools gptel-use-context))

  (pcase type

    ('boolean "boolean")
    ('symbol  "string")

logging path."
  (yeah-gptel--require-gptel "yeah-gptel-tool-for")

    (signal 'user-error (list "yeah-gptel-tool-for: gptel-make-tool is unavailable")))

      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-gptel-tool-for: no such tool: %S" name))))

     :name name
     :function (lambda (&rest args)
                 (yeah-tools-call name (yeah-tools-normalize-args name args)))
     :description (plist-get spec :description)
     :args (mapcar (lambda (param)

                                                 (plist-get param :name))

(defun yeah-gptel--request-tools (tools)
  "Resolve the request TOOLS option.
`registry' builds tools from Yeah's registry, nil disables tools, and a list
is used as an explicit list of gptel tool objects."
  (pcase tools
    ('registry (mapcar #'yeah-gptel-tool-for (yeah-tools-names)))
    ('nil nil)
    ((pred listp) tools)
    (_ (signal 'user-error
               (list (format "yeah-gptel-request: invalid tools option: %S" tools))))))

(defun yeah-gptel--usage (info)
  "Return normalized token usage from request INFO, or nil when unavailable."
  (when-let ((tokens (plist-get info :tokens)))
    (list :input (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :input))
                      (plist-get tokens :input))
          :output (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :output))
                       (plist-get tokens :output))
          :cache (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :cache))
                      (plist-get tokens :cache))
          :cached (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :cached))
                       (plist-get tokens :cached)))))

(defun yeah-gptel--failure-reason (info)
  "Return a printable provider failure reason from request INFO."
  (let ((reason (or (plist-get info :error)
                    (plist-get info :status)
                    "no response")))
    (if (stringp reason) reason (format "%S" reason))))

(defun yeah-gptel--normalize-response (response info)
  "Normalize gptel RESPONSE and INFO for Yeah's run loop.
Text, reasoning, tool calls/results and the streaming sentinel t retain
gptel's public shapes.  Failures and unknown shapes become `(error . REASON)'."
  (cond
   ((or (stringp response) (eq response t)) response)
   ((and (consp response)
         (memq (car response) '(reasoning tool-call tool-result)))
    response)
   ((eq response 'abort) (cons 'error "the model request was aborted"))
   ((null response) (cons 'error (yeah-gptel--failure-reason info)))
   (t (cons 'error (format "unsupported gptel response shape: %S" response)))))

(defun yeah-gptel--callback (callback response info)
  "Deliver normalized RESPONSE and INFO to CALLBACK."
  (let ((normalized-info (and (listp info) (copy-sequence info))))
    (when-let ((usage (yeah-gptel--usage info)))
      (setq normalized-info (plist-put normalized-info :yeah-usage usage)))
    (funcall callback
             (yeah-gptel--normalize-response response info)
             normalized-info)))

;;;###autoload
(cl-defun yeah-gptel-request
    (prompt callback &key backend model (tools 'registry)
                    (system yeah-gptel-prelude) stream context dry-run)
  "Ask the model PROMPT and call CALLBACK with its response and request info.

This is the only place in Yeah that calls `gptel-request'.  BACKEND and MODEL
default to the user's current gptel choices.  TOOLS is `registry' for Yeah's
registered tools, nil for no tools, or an explicit list of gptel tools.
SYSTEM defaults to `yeah-gptel-prelude' and may be nil.  STREAM, CONTEXT and
DRY-RUN have the meanings documented by `gptel-request'.

Responses retain gptel's text/reasoning/tool shapes; failures become
`(error . REASON)'.  When usage is available, CALLBACK's info contains
`:yeah-usage' with normalized input/output/cache/cached counts.

The configuration is captured for this request only.  Global gptel settings
are not modified and ambient gptel editor context is disabled.  The return
value is gptel's request state machine, which can be inspected or aborted."
  (unless (functionp callback)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-gptel-request: callback is not a function: %S"
                          callback))))
  (yeah-gptel-check-contract)
  (let* ((request-tools (yeah-gptel--request-tools tools))
         (gptel-backend (or backend gptel-backend))
         (gptel-model (or model gptel-model))
         (gptel-tools request-tools)
         (gptel-use-tools (and request-tools t))
         (gptel-use-context nil)
         (gptel-include-reasoning yeah-gptel-include-reasoning))
    (gptel-request prompt
                   :callback (lambda (response info)
                               (yeah-gptel--callback callback response info))
                   :system system
                   :stream stream
                   :context context
                   :dry-run dry-run)))

(defun yeah-gptel-bind-tools (&optional buffer)
  "Advertise Yeah's registry as buffer-local gptel tools in BUFFER.
This helper is for interactive gptel buffers only.  `yeah-gptel-request'
passes its own tools directly and does not depend on this buffer state."
  (yeah-gptel--require-gptel "yeah-gptel-bind-tools")
  (with-current-buffer (or buffer (current-buffer))
    (setq-local gptel-tools
                (mapcar #'yeah-gptel-tool-for (yeah-tools-names)))))

(provide 'yeah-gptel)

;;; yeah-client.el --- an ACP client for the editor -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The editor is a client of a service Emacs.  This module is the client:
;; it speaks ACP over a Unix-domain socket or a loopback TCP port, matches
;; answers to requests by their id, and hands the session/update
;; notifications to the caller.  The session's journal is the service's
;; truth; the client renders the stream the service sends.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)

(defgroup yeah-client nil
  "The Yeah ACP client."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-client-network-family nil
  "Network family used to reach a Yeah service.
Nil chooses automatically: `local' uses a Unix-domain socket on
Unix-like systems, while `ipv4' uses a loopback TCP port on
Windows-like systems.  Set this to `local' or `ipv4' to override the
automatic choice; an IPv4 service publishes its port in a `.port'
file next to the socket path."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Automatic" nil)
                 (symbol :tag "Socket family"))
  :group 'yeah-client)

(defun yeah-client-automatic-network-family ()
  "Return the network family selected for the current platform."
  (if (memq system-type '(windows-nt ms-dos cygwin))
      'ipv4
    'local))

(defun yeah-client-effective-network-family ()
  "Return the configured network family for a Yeah service.
Signal `user-error' when the override is not a supported family."
  (let ((family (or yeah-client-network-family
                   (yeah-client-automatic-network-family))))
    (unless (memq family '(local ipv4))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-client-network-family: unsupported family %S"
                            family))))
    family))

(defun yeah-client-port-file (socket)
  "Return the file that publishes the TCP port for SOCKET."
  (concat socket ".port"))

(defun yeah-client--read-port (socket)
  "Return the TCP port published for SOCKET, or nil when it is unavailable."
  (let ((file (yeah-client-port-file socket)))
    (when (file-readable-p file)
      (with-temp-buffer
        (insert-file-contents file)
        (let ((text (string-trim (buffer-string))))
          (when (string-match-p "\\`[0-9]+\\'" text)
            (let ((port (string-to-number text)))
              (when (and (> port 0) (<= port 65535))
                port))))))))

(defun yeah-client-connection-params (socket)
  "Return the network connection parameters for SOCKET.
The result is a plist for `make-network-process'.  It is nil when an
IPv4 service has not published its port yet."
  (if (eq (yeah-client-effective-network-family) 'local)
      (list :family 'local :service socket)
    (let ((port (yeah-client--read-port socket)))
      (when port
        (list :family 'ipv4 :host "127.0.0.1" :service port)))))

(defun yeah-client--open-connection (socket)
  "Open one connection to SOCKET, or return nil when it is not ready."
  (let ((params (yeah-client-connection-params socket)))
    (when params
      (if (eq (plist-get params :family) 'local)
          (condition-case nil
              (apply #'make-network-process
                     :name (format "yeah-client-%s"
                                    (file-name-nondirectory socket))
                     :noquery t
                     params)
            (file-missing nil))
        (condition-case nil
            (apply #'make-network-process
                   :name (format "yeah-client-%s"
                                  (file-name-nondirectory socket))
                   :noquery t
                   params)
          (file-error nil))))))

(cl-defstruct (yeah-client (:constructor yeah-client--make))
  "One connection to a service Emacs.

CONNECTION is the network process.  PENDING maps request ids to their
answer callbacks.  ON-NOTIFICATION is called with each session/update.
ON-REQUEST is called with (METHOD PARAMS RESPOND) for each request the
service sends (such as session/request_permission); RESPOND takes the
result plist and answers the request.  ON-CLOSE is called once when the
connection drops without the client closing it.  COUNTER is the next
request id."
  (connection nil)
  (pending nil)
  (on-notification nil)
  (on-request nil)
  (on-close nil)
  (counter 0)
  (partial ""))

(defun yeah-client--filter (client _process chunk)
  "Accumulate CHUNK and dispatch the complete lines of CLIENT."
  (let* ((combined (concat (yeah-client-partial client) chunk))
         (parts (split-string combined "\n"))
         (complete (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined) parts (butlast parts)))
         (tail (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined) "" (car (last parts)))))
    (setf (yeah-client-partial client) tail)
    (dolist (line complete)
      (unless (string-blank-p line)
        (yeah-client--handle client line)))))

(defun yeah-client--handle (client line)
  "Handle one JSON LINE received by CLIENT."
  (condition-case nil
      (let* ((message (json-parse-string line :object-type 'plist
                                          :array-type 'list))
             (id (plist-get message :id))
             (method (plist-get message :method)))
        (cond
         ((and id (plist-member message :result))
          (when-let ((answer (gethash id (yeah-client-pending client))))
            (remhash id (yeah-client-pending client))
            (funcall answer (plist-get message :result) nil)))
         ((and id (plist-member message :error))
          (when-let ((answer (gethash id (yeah-client-pending client))))
            (remhash id (yeah-client-pending client))
            (funcall answer nil (plist-get message :error))))
         ((and method id)
          ;; a request of the service (session/request_permission): it
          ;; must be answered, not dropped
          (if-let ((on-request (yeah-client-on-request client)))
              (funcall on-request method (plist-get message :params)
                       (lambda (result)
                         (yeah-client--send client
                           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id :result result))))
            (yeah-client--send client
              (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id
                    :error (list :code -32601
                                 :message (format "the client does not answer %s"
                                                  method))))))
         (method
          (when-let ((on-notification (yeah-client-on-notification client)))
            (funcall on-notification message)))))
    (error nil)))

;;;###autoload
(cl-defun yeah-client-connect (socket &key on-notification on-request on-close
                                         timeout)
  "Connect to the service on SOCKET and return the client.
ON-NOTIFICATION is called with each notification the service sends.
ON-REQUEST is called with (METHOD PARAMS RESPOND) for each request the
service sends; RESPOND takes the result plist and answers the request.
ON-CLOSE is called once when the connection drops without the client
closing it.
Waits up to TIMEOUT seconds (default 10) for the socket to appear."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 10)))
        (connection nil))
    (while (and (null connection) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (setq connection (yeah-client--open-connection socket))
      (unless connection
        (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
    (unless connection
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-client-connect: no service on %s" socket))))
    (let ((client (yeah-client--make
                   :pending (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
                   :on-notification on-notification
                   :on-request on-request
                   :on-close on-close
                   :connection connection)))
      (set-process-filter connection
                          (lambda (process chunk)
                            (yeah-client--filter client process chunk)))
      (set-process-sentinel
       connection
       (lambda (process _event)
         (when (and (eq (process-status process) 'closed)
                    (yeah-client-connection client)
                    (functionp (yeah-client-on-close client)))
           (setf (yeah-client-connection client) nil)
           (funcall (yeah-client-on-close client) client))))
      client)))

(defun yeah-client--send (client object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line from CLIENT."
  (process-send-string (yeah-client-connection client)
                       (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-client-request (client method params on-answer)
  "Send a request with METHOD and PARAMS; ON-ANSWER gets (RESULT ERROR)."
  (let ((id (cl-incf (yeah-client-counter client))))
    (puthash id on-answer (yeah-client-pending client))
    (yeah-client--send client (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id
                                    :method method :params params))
    id))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-client-notify (client method params)
  "Send a notification with METHOD and PARAMS."
  (yeah-client--send client (list :jsonrpc "2.0"
                                  :method method :params params)))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-client-close (client)
  "Close the connection of CLIENT.
A close the client asked for is not a death: the sentinel is removed
before the process is deleted, so ON-CLOSE does not fire for it."
  (when-let ((connection (yeah-client-connection client)))
    (setf (yeah-client-connection client) nil)
    (set-process-sentinel connection nil)
    (when (process-live-p connection)
      (delete-process connection))))

(provide 'yeah-client)
;;; yeah-client.el ends here
