;;; yeah-emacs.el --- introspection and live editor tools -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Tools that expose Emacs itself: live buffers, documentation/source,
;; non-evaluating Elisp reader checks and Flymake diagnostics.  Variable
;; values are deliberately not printed by introspection because they may
;; contain credentials or other private state.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-result)

(declare-function find-function-noselect "find-func"
                  (symbol &optional switch-to-buffer))
(declare-function flymake-diagnostics "flymake" (&optional beg end))
(declare-function flymake-diagnostic-type "flymake" (diag))
(declare-function flymake-diagnostic-text "flymake" (diag))
(declare-function flymake-diagnostic-beg "flymake" (diag))
(declare-function flymake-diagnostic-end "flymake" (diag))
(defvar flymake-mode)
(defvar read-eval)

(defun yeah-emacs--documentation (symbol)
  "Return bounded documentation and source metadata for SYMBOL."
  (let* ((kind (cond ((fboundp symbol) "function")
                     ((boundp symbol) "variable")
                     (t nil)))
         (file (and kind (symbol-file symbol))))
    (unless kind
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-introspect: unknown function or variable: %S"
                            symbol))))
    (list :kind kind
          :file file
          :text (format "%s\nType: %s\nSource: %s\n\n%s"
                        symbol kind (or file "unknown")
                        (or (and (equal kind "function") (documentation symbol))
                            (and (equal kind "variable")
                                 (documentation-property symbol
                                                         'variable-documentation))
                            "No documentation available.")))))

(defun yeah-emacs--function-source (symbol)
  "Return the source form of function SYMBOL without evaluating it."
  (unless (fboundp symbol)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-introspect: not a function: %S" symbol))))
  (let ((location (find-function-noselect symbol)))
    (with-current-buffer (car location)
      (save-excursion
        (goto-char (cdr location))
        (let ((start (point)))
          (forward-sexp)
          (buffer-substring-no-properties start (point)))))))

(defun yeah-emacs-introspect (name &optional kind)
  "Return documentation, source or matching symbols for NAME.
KIND is `function', `variable', `source' or `apropos' (the default is
`function').  No variable values are returned."
  (let ((kind (or kind "function")))
    (condition-case err
        (pcase kind
          ("apropos"
           (let* ((symbols (sort (mapcar #'symbol-name
                                        (apropos-internal name))
                                 #'string<))
                  (limited (seq-take symbols 100)))
             (yeah-result-from-output
              (mapconcat #'identity limited "\n")
              nil
              (list :query name :count (length symbols)
                    :returned (length limited)))))
          ((or "function" "variable")
           (let ((info (yeah-emacs--documentation (intern name))))
             (yeah-result-from-output
              (plist-get info :text) nil
              (list :name name :kind (plist-get info :kind)
                    :file (plist-get info :file)))))
          ("source"
           (yeah-result-from-output
            (yeah-emacs--function-source (intern name)) nil
            (list :name name :kind "source")))
          (_ (yeah-result-error
              (format "unknown introspection kind: %s" kind))))
      (error (yeah-result-error (error-message-string err))))))

(defun yeah-emacs-elisp-check (path)
  "Read PATH without evaluation and report reader/parenthesis validity."
  (condition-case err
      (let ((absolute (expand-file-name path))
            (forms 0))
        (unless (file-regular-p absolute)
          (signal 'user-error (list (format "not a regular file: %s" path))))
        (when (> (file-attribute-size (file-attributes absolute))
                 (* 2 1024 1024))
          (signal 'user-error (list "yeah-elisp-check: file exceeds 2 MiB")))
        (with-temp-buffer
          (insert-file-contents absolute)
          (goto-char (point-min))
          (check-parens)
          (goto-char (point-min))
          (let ((read-eval nil)
                (done nil))
            (while (not done)
              (condition-case nil
                  (progn (read (current-buffer)) (setq forms (1+ forms)))
                (end-of-file (setq done t))))))
        (yeah-result-ok
         (format "OK: %d forms read; parentheses are balanced." forms)
         (list :path absolute :forms forms)))
    (error
     (yeah-result-error (error-message-string err)))))

(defun yeah-emacs-buffer-read (name &optional offset limit widen)
  "Read live buffer NAME by lines and return its modification tick.
OFFSET is 1-based and LIMIT defaults to 2000 lines.  WIDEN non-nil explicitly
permits reading beyond the current narrowing."
  (let ((offset (or offset 1))
        (limit (or limit 2000))
        (buffer (get-buffer name)))
    (cond
     ((not (buffer-live-p buffer))
      (yeah-result-error (format "no live buffer named %s" name)))
     ((or (< offset 1) (< limit 1))
      (yeah-result-error "offset and limit must be positive"))
     (t
      (with-current-buffer buffer
        (save-restriction
          (when widen (widen))
          (let* ((tick (buffer-chars-modified-tick))
                 (total (count-lines (point-min) (point-max)))
                 (start (save-excursion
                          (goto-char (point-min))
                          (forward-line (1- offset))
                          (point)))
                 (end (save-excursion
                        (goto-char start)
                        (forward-line limit)
                        (point))))
            (yeah-result-ok
             (buffer-substring-no-properties start end)
             (list :buffer name :offset offset :limit limit
                   :total-lines total :tick tick
                   :truncated (< end (point-max)))))))))))

(defun yeah-emacs-diagnostics (&optional path)
  "Return Flymake diagnostics for PATH or the current buffer.
PATH must already have a visiting buffer; this tool does not open files or
start a language server."
  (let ((buffer (if path (find-buffer-visiting (expand-file-name path))
                  (current-buffer))))
    (cond
     ((not (buffer-live-p buffer))
      (yeah-result-error "diagnostics require an existing visiting buffer"))
     ((not (and (boundp 'flymake-mode) flymake-mode
                (fboundp 'flymake-diagnostics)))
      (yeah-result-error
       (format "Flymake is not active in %s" (buffer-name buffer))))
     (t
      (with-current-buffer buffer
        (let* ((diagnostics (flymake-diagnostics))
               (lines
                (mapcar
                 (lambda (diag)
                   (let ((beg (flymake-diagnostic-beg diag))
                         (end (flymake-diagnostic-end diag)))
                     (format "%s:%d:%d: %s: %s"
                             (buffer-name)
                             (line-number-at-pos beg)
                             (max 0 (- end beg))
                             (flymake-diagnostic-type diag)
                             (flymake-diagnostic-text diag))))
                 diagnostics)))
          (yeah-result-from-output
           (if lines (mapconcat #'identity lines "\n")
             "No diagnostics.")
           nil
           (list :buffer (buffer-name) :count (length diagnostics)))))))))

(defun yeah-emacs-tools ()
  "Return the built-in Emacs capability tool specifications."
  (list
   (list :name "introspect"
         :description "Look up the Emacs documentation, source or matching symbols for a symbol; no variable values are returned."
         :input (list (list :name "symbol" :type 'string)
                      (list :name "kind" :type 'string :optional t))
         :handler #'yeah-emacs-introspect)
   (list :name "buffer-read"
         :description "Read the content of a live Emacs buffer by its buffer name, from a 1-based line offset, up to a line limit. Use it for a buffer that is open in this Emacs."
         :input (list (list :name "name" :type 'string)
                      (list :name "offset" :type 'integer :optional t)
                      (list :name "limit" :type 'integer :optional t)
                      (list :name "widen" :type 'boolean :optional t))
         :handler #'yeah-emacs-buffer-read)
   (list :name "elisp-check"
         :description "Check that an Elisp source parses: reader syntax and balanced parentheses, without evaluating any form."
         :input (list (list :name "path" :type 'string))
         :handler #'yeah-emacs-elisp-check)
   (list :name "diagnostics"
         :description "Return the Flymake/Eglot diagnostics of a buffer that visits a path, or of the current buffer; it returns the diagnostics, not the content of the buffer."
         :input (list (list :name "path" :type 'string :optional t))
         :handler #'yeah-emacs-diagnostics)))

(provide 'yeah-emacs)

;;; yeah-service.el --- a service Emacs running the Yeah harness -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The primary placement: a dedicated Emacs process runs the harness, so
;; the editing Emacs never shares a thread with a long turn.  This module
;; starts such a service, connects to it and stops it.  The service
;; serves ACP on a Unix-domain socket, or on a loopback TCP port when the
;; platform has no Unix socket; a cancel is handled while a prompt is still
;; running.
;;
;; The service runs the same Emacs as the person: the program is resolved
;; when the service starts, and the running binary is the fallback, so a
;; service starts on a machine where `emacs' is not on PATH.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-client)
(require 'yeah-wire-socket)

(defgroup yeah-service nil
  "A service Emacs running the Yeah harness."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-service-emacs
  (or (executable-find "emacs")
      (and (file-executable-p (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
           (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
      invocation-name)
  "The Emacs program that runs the service."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-service)

(defvar yeah-service--processes (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map a service name to its process.")

(defun yeah-service--emacs-program ()
  "Return the program that runs the service Emacs.

The service runs the SAME Emacs as the person: the binary that is
running now, when the platform can name it.  A program name that the
PATH does not carry would make the service impossible to start on a
machine where Emacs lives in a profile, so the running binary is the
fallback, and `EMACS' comes before it."
  (let ((configured (or yeah-service-emacs "emacs")))
    (cond
     ((or (file-name-absolute-p configured)
          (file-directory-p configured))
      configured)
     ((executable-find configured) (executable-find configured))
     ((and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS")))
      (getenv "EMACS"))
     ((file-executable-p "/proc/self/exe") "/proc/self/exe")
     ((file-executable-p (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
     (t configured))))

(defun yeah-service--socket-directory ()
  "Return the user-private directory the service sockets live in.
Anyone who can connect to the socket drives the agent with the person's
permissions, so the socket never sits in a world-writable /tmp: it goes
under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR when there is one, else under a directory of this
user with mode 0700."
  (let ((dir (if-let ((runtime (getenv "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")))
                 (expand-file-name "yeah" runtime)
               (expand-file-name (format "yeah-%d" (user-uid))
                                 (or (getenv "TMPDIR") "/tmp")))))
    (unless (file-directory-p dir)
      (make-directory dir t)
      (set-file-modes dir #o700))
    dir))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-socket-path (name)
  "Return the socket path of the service NAME."
  (expand-file-name (format "yeah-service-%s.sock" name)
                    (yeah-service--socket-directory)))

(defun yeah-service--socket-path (name)
  "Return the socket path of the service NAME."
  (yeah-service-socket-path name))

(defun yeah-service--reserve-loopback-port ()
  "Return an unused loopback TCP port.
The probe binds the port briefly so the service child can bind the same
port without choosing a fixed, commonly occupied number."
  (let ((probe
         (make-network-process
          :name (format "yeah-service-port-%d" (random 1000000000))
          :server t
          :family 'ipv4
          :service 0
          :noquery t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((port (process-contact probe :service)))
          (unless (and (integerp port) (> port 0) (<= port 65535))
            (signal 'user-error
                    (list "yeah-service-start: could not reserve a TCP port")))
          port)
      (when (process-live-p probe)
        (delete-process probe)))))

(defun yeah-service--write-port-file (socket port)
  "Publish PORT for SOCKET in the port file next to its socket path.
The file contains the port number only; it is not a credential."
  (let ((file (yeah-client-port-file socket)))
    (with-temp-file file
      (insert (number-to-string port)))
    (set-file-modes file #o600)
    file))

(defun yeah-service--lib-directory ()
  "Return the directory holding Yeah's Elisp modules."
  (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-acp") "yeah-acp.el")))

(defun yeah-service--rules-eval (rules)
  "Return the Elisp that installs RULES in the service.
RULES is a list of permission rule plists, as `yeah-perm-rule-make'
builds them; the service adds each of them to its own ruleset."
  (if (null rules)
      ""
    (format "(dolist (rule '%S) (yeah-perm-rules-add rule))" rules)))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-start (name &optional extra-eval data-home transport clean rules)
  "Start a service Emacs named NAME and return its process.
The service serves ACP on a Unix-domain socket, or on a loopback TCP port
when `yeah-client-network-family' selects `ipv4'.  In the TCP case the port
number is published in a `.port' file next to the socket path.  EXTRA-EVAL
is evaluated in the service before the server starts (to configure the
model backend); DATA-HOME is the service's data directory; TRANSPORT is a
form evaluating to the model transport of the service (nil uses the
default).  A service with the same name is not started twice.
CLEAN (the default) starts the service without the user's init; nil lets
the service inherit the user's configuration, including the gptel backend.
RULES is a list of permission rule plists: the standing permissions the
person grants the service, which is how a headless service may edit at
all."
  (let ((existing (gethash name yeah-service--processes)))
    (when (and existing (process-live-p existing))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-service-start: %S is already running" name)))))
  (let* ((socket (yeah-service--socket-path name))
         (family (yeah-client-effective-network-family))
         (port (when (eq family 'ipv4)
                 (yeah-service--reserve-loopback-port)))
         (server-form
          (if (eq family 'local)
              (format "(yeah-acp-serve-socket %S %s)"
                      socket
                      (or transport "yeah-acp-default-transport"))
            (format "(yeah-acp-serve-socket %d %s nil 'ipv4)"
                    port
                    (or transport "yeah-acp-default-transport"))))
         (buffer (generate-new-buffer (format " *yeah service %s*" name)))
         (process
          (make-process
           :name (format "yeah-service-%s" name)
           :buffer buffer
           :command
           (append (list (yeah-service--emacs-program))
                   (if clean (list "-Q" "--batch") (list "--batch"))
                   (list "-L" (yeah-service--lib-directory)
                         "-l" "yeah-acp"
                         "--eval"
                         (format "(progn %s %s %s %s)"
                                 (or extra-eval "")
                                 (if data-home
                                     (format "(setq yeah-data-home %S)" data-home)
                                   "")
                                 (yeah-service--rules-eval rules)
                                 server-form)))
           :connection-type 'pipe
           :noquery t)))
    (when (eq family 'ipv4)
      (condition-case error
          (yeah-service--write-port-file socket port)
        (error
         (delete-process process)
         (signal (car error) (cdr error)))))
    (puthash name process yeah-service--processes)
    process))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-connect (name &optional timeout)
  "Connect to the service NAME and return the connection process.
Waits up to TIMEOUT seconds (default 10) for the socket to appear."
  (let ((socket (yeah-service-socket-path-internal name))
        (deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 10)))
        (connection nil))
    (while (and (null connection) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (setq connection (yeah-client--open-connection socket))
      (unless connection
        (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
    connection))

(defun yeah-service-socket-path-internal (name)
  "Return the socket path of the service NAME."
  (yeah-service--socket-path name))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-stop (name)
  "Stop the service NAME and remove its socket."
  (when-let ((process (gethash name yeah-service--processes)))
    (when (process-live-p process)
      (delete-process process))
    (remhash name yeah-service--processes))
  (let ((socket (yeah-service--socket-path name)))
    (when (file-exists-p socket)
      (ignore-errors (delete-file socket)))
    (let ((port-file (yeah-client-port-file socket)))
      (when (file-exists-p port-file)
        (ignore-errors (delete-file port-file)))))
  t)

(provide 'yeah-service)
;;; yeah-service.el ends here

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.
4. The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
   with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`, since wave 40), but
   no `kind`: a client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read,
   an edit, a shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The
   arguments of a call are positional, so a client that looks for named
   fields (`path`, `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.

**What changes.**  The gaps are closed in the order of what the live
integration needs today: the `cwd` first, because the agent must work in the
repository of the task; then the `kind` of the call and its named arguments,
because the client must be able to show what the agent did; then
`session/set_mode`; then the model of the session; then the `mcpServers` of
the session, whose tools do not reach the model today.

**The claims.**  Each gap is a claim of its own, and the name of the claim is
the name of the gap: `a-session-runs-in-its-own-directory`,
`a-tool-call-carries-its-kind`, `a-tool-call-carries-named-arguments`,
`a-session-changes-its-permission-profile-over-the-wire`,
`a-session-changes-its-model-over-the-wire`,
`the-mcp-servers-of-a-session-reach-the-model`.

**The exit criteria.**
1. The check of the `cwd` sends a session into a temporary directory, and the
   tool of that session sees the temporary directory and not the directory of
   the process.
2. The plugin of Paseo runs a turn in the repository of the task, and the
   timeline of the client shows the kind of the call of the tool.
3. The wire answers `session/set_mode` and no longer answers `-32601`.

**The estimate.**  Two to three days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The
wire of Yeah is ACP plus the one extension that was announced
(`yeah.queueEvents`); this wave adds no method that ACP does not have.

### 18.4 Wave 44 — parallel children in a live turn

**The defect.**  Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the
audit of wave 35 proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What
is not proven is a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live
provider.  No child of a live provider has run on a model other than the
model of its parent, and the live checks do not exercise the delegation at
all: the benchmark gives its runs a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is
not among them.

**What changes.**  The live check grows a second child in the same turn of
the parent, and the offline check with a fake model becomes the claim that
the map binds — the live check lives outside the map, because it needs a
provider.

**The claims.**
- `two-children-run-in-one-turn-of-the-parent` — the claim of the map, with a
  fake model: two delegations in one turn of the parent give two children,
  both alive, and the turn of the parent goes on (the control refuses the
  second delegation: the check must fail).
- `a-child-runs-on-the-model-of-its-preset` — the model of a child is the
  model of the preset, and not the model of its parent (the control names
  another model in the preset: the child must run on it).

**The exit criteria.**
1. The offline check passes and its control bites.
2. The live check with a real provider shows two children in one turn of the
   parent, and the tree of the children in the journal holds both.

**The estimate.**  One to two days, and a key of the provider for the live
part.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The budget of the completion
supervision of a child is zero today, and that is a decision of the owner
(§17.2), not a defect of this wave.

### 18.5 What this plan does not decide

Three decisions of the owner stay open, and no wave above takes them:
- the threshold of the parity, and the final set of the tasks of the benchmark
  (`docs/PLAN.md` §13): until it is decided, the parity is not claimed
  anywhere, and the pilot stays a measurement;
- whether a run that the provider silenced is a failure of the agent or a run
  that was never measured: it changes the number of every pilot;
- the budget of the completion supervision of a child of a delegation: the
  default of the kernel is positive since wave 39, the default of the child is
  still zero.

Two more items of the open work (§17.1) are not in the order above and stay
where they are: the pilot again, with a larger set of tasks, when the
provider answers; and the pixel check, which waits for the owner to name the
place of the frame server.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The primary placement is a dedicated Emacs process.  This check starts
;; such a service, connects to it as a client, and drives one prompt over
;; the socket: the answer comes back with the end_turn stop reason, and
;; the journal of the service records the turn.  The model is a FAKE, so
;; no network and no key are needed.  The service is stopped afterwards.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-service)
(load (expand-file-name "tests/support/yeah-journal-files.el") nil t)

(defvar yeah-check--buffer nil
  "The buffer collecting the messages the client received.")

(defvar yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the client buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--send (connection object)

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The Bash tool starts a managed shell process and returns its job ID.  Its
;; continuation receives one bounded result when the process exits, times out,
;; or is cancelled.  Job tools expose the same output without waiting for the
;; process.  Cancellation deletes only the managed process; it does not claim
;; to terminate descendants or roll back their effects.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-result)

(defconst yeah-process--default-timeout 120
  "Default maximum process runtime in seconds.")

(defvar yeah-process--jobs (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map job IDs to their managed process records.")

(defvar yeah-process--next-id 0
  "Last numeric suffix allocated to a process job.")

(defvar yeah-process--current-run-id nil
  "Run identifier captured when a job is started, or nil for an independent job.")

(cl-defstruct (yeah-process--job
               (:constructor yeah-process--make-job)
               (:conc-name yeah-process--job-))
  "Mutable state for one managed process.
OUTPUT is the final output after settlement.  Before then, output is read
from BUFFER.  SETTLED is the once-only guard shared by the sentinel, timer,
and cancellation path."
  id
  run-id
  process
  stderr-process
  buffer
  timer
  done
  command
  directory
  timeout
  idle
  idle-timer
  (status "running")
  exit
  (timed-out nil)
  (output "")
  result
  (settled nil))

(defun yeah-process--new-id ()
  "Allocate an ID that is not present in the job registry."
  (let (id)
    (while (or (null id) (gethash id yeah-process--jobs))
      (setq yeah-process--next-id (1+ yeah-process--next-id)
            id (format "job-%d" yeah-process--next-id)))
    id))

(defun yeah-process--list-length (args name minimum maximum)
  "Validate ARGS as a list for NAME with MINIMUM..MAXIMUM items."
  (unless (listp args)
    (signal 'user-error (list (format "yeah-process-%s: args must be a list"
                                      name))))
  (let ((count (condition-case nil (length args) (error -1))))
    (unless (and (>= count minimum) (<= count maximum))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-process-%s: expected %d..%d args, got %S"
                            name minimum maximum args))))
    count))

(defun yeah-process--directory (directory)
  "Return DIRECTORY as an absolute, existing directory name."
  (let ((expanded (file-name-as-directory
                   (expand-file-name (or directory default-directory)))))
    (unless (file-directory-p expanded)
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-process-bash: not a directory: %s"
                            expanded))))
    expanded))

(defun yeah-process--output (job)
  "Return JOB's currently available combined standard output and error."
  (let ((buffer (yeah-process--job-buffer job)))
    (if (buffer-live-p buffer)
        (with-current-buffer buffer
          (buffer-substring-no-properties (point-min) (point-max)))
      (yeah-process--job-output job))))

(defun yeah-process--metadata (job)
  "Return serializable status metadata for JOB."
  (list :id (yeah-process--job-id job)
        :run-id (yeah-process--job-run-id job)
        :status (yeah-process--job-status job)
        :exit (yeah-process--job-exit job)
        :timeout (yeah-process--job-timed-out job)
        :command (yeah-process--job-command job)
        :directory (yeah-process--job-directory job)
        :timeout-seconds (yeah-process--job-timeout job)
        :idle-seconds (yeah-process--job-idle job)))

(defun yeah-process--settle (job status exit timed-out &optional kill)
  "Settle JOB with STATUS, EXIT, and TIMED-OUT unless it already settled.
When KILL is non-nil, delete the managed process after winning settlement.
The stored continuation is called only by the winning path.  Return the
job's result."
  (if (yeah-process--job-settled job)
      (yeah-process--job-result job)
    (let ((output (yeah-process--output job))
          (process (yeah-process--job-process job))
          (stderr-process (yeah-process--job-stderr-process job))
          (timer (yeah-process--job-timer job))
          (idle-timer (yeah-process--job-idle-timer job))
          (buffer (yeah-process--job-buffer job)))

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'

;;; yeah-acp.el --- ACP v1 agent over newline JSON-RPC -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Agent-side ACP v1 over newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0.  Sessions are real
;; Yeah sessions; prompt responses are sent when the run reaches a terminal
;; state; session/cancel is a notification; journal events become
;; session/update notifications through `yeah-events-write-functions'.
;;
;; A session is driven by a controller: the same one the attached path uses.
;; The controller owns the session's turn and its persistent pending queue,
;; so the wire can ask, steer, cancel, withdraw a pending input and recover
;; one.  There is no second queue in this module: the pending inputs of a
;; session are the ones the control keeps, and the queue the editor sees is
;; a projection of the journal -- the events that move an input in or out of
;; the queue reach the client as session/update notifications.
;;
;; `session/load' opens a session again and replays its journal: the records
;; of the session become session/update notifications, so that an editor can
;; rebuild the transcript of a session it opens a second time.
;;
;; An answer to a permission that arrives after the run that asked has ended
;; is not applied: the journal shows the question as deferred and the run as
;; ended, and the late answer changes nothing.
;;
;; The protocol is spoken over two transports.  On stdio the server reads
;; standard input with a blocking read, so a notification that arrives
;; while a prompt is running is read only after the prompt settled.  On a
;; socket the connection is a process, the data arrives in a filter and the
;; event loop keeps running, so a cancellation is handled while the prompt
;; is still running.  `yeah-acp-serve-socket' is the transport of the
;; primary deployment.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-acp-vocabulary)
(require 'yeah-control)
(require 'yeah-events)
(require 'yeah-product)
(require 'yeah-result)
(require 'yeah-turn)
(require 'yeah-wire)
(require 'yeah-wire-socket)

(defgroup yeah-acp nil
  "Yeah ACP v1 agent."
  :group 'yeah)

(defconst yeah-acp--agent-name "yeah")
(defconst yeah-acp--agent-version "0.1.0")

(defvar yeah-acp--sessions (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map ACP session ids to their Yeah session state.")

(defvar yeah-acp--pending-permissions (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map permission request ids to the question they ask.
The value names the session, the action and the resource, so that the
answer reaches the turn that asked and may be remembered for the
session.")

(defvar yeah-acp--connection nil
  "The connection being served, bound dynamically by the socket handler.
A session remembers which connection owns it, so the death of that
connection can cancel the work it started.")

(defvar yeah-acp--client-capabilities (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "Map every connection to the capabilities its client announced.
The key is the connection; the standard output connection is the key
nil.  What a client announced at `initialize' says what it
understands of the wire.")

(defun yeah-acp--jsonable-args (args)
  "Return ARGS as a JSON value: an array when every element serializes,
the printed form otherwise."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((array (apply #'vector args)))
        (ignore (json-serialize array))
        array)
    (error (format "%S" args))))

(defun yeah-acp--session-rules (session-id)
  "Return the permission rules that decide for SESSION-ID.
The standing permissions of the service come first and the decisions the
client remembered for this session come last: the last match wins."
  (let ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id)))
    (append (yeah-perm-rules-list) (plist-get state :rules))))

(defun yeah-acp--ask-client (session-id output request)
  "Ask the client about REQUEST and return the deferral of the question.
The question carries three answers: allow once, allow always (the decision
is remembered for the session) and reject.  The question itself is kept,
so that the answer reaches the turn that asked and may be remembered."
  (let* ((request-id (yeah-acp--fresh-id "perm"))

                                                      (plist-get request :resource))

          exit 2

          ;;

;;; yeah-control.el --- queued human control of agent runs -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; A controller owns one session's active turn and persistent pending FIFO.
;; Inputs carry frozen configuration captured at submission.  Steering is
;; consumed only at tool-batch boundaries.  Loading pending work never starts
;; a model request; recovery is always explicit.
;;
;; The pending queue is written into the journal as it changes: an input that
;; enters the queue, starts a run, is recovered or is withdrawn is named in
;; the log by its id.  The editor's view of the queue is therefore a
;; projection of the records and not a second, invisible state.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-turn)
(require 'yeah-events)
(require 'yeah-input)

(cl-defstruct (yeah-control (:constructor yeah-control--make))
  "Runtime control state for one session."
  session
  transport
  answerer
  budget
  max-nudges
  frozen-defaults
  active-turn
  completion-listeners)

(defun yeah-control-new (session &optional transport answerer budget max-nudges frozen)
  "Return a controller for SESSION without starting any work.
TRANSPORT, ANSWERER, BUDGET and MAX-NUDGES are frozen for subsequent inputs.
FROZEN is additional serializable configuration recorded with each input."
  (yeah-control--make
   :session session
   :transport (or transport
                  (and (fboundp 'yeah-gptel-request) #'yeah-gptel-request))
   :answerer (or answerer #'yeah-approval-policy-decision)
   :budget (or budget yeah-context-default-budget)
   :max-nudges (or max-nudges yeah-turn-default-max-nudges)
   :frozen-defaults frozen
   :completion-listeners (make-hash-table :test 'equal)))

(defun yeah-control--frozen (control kind prompt frozen)
  "Build a new KIND input for PROMPT with FROZEN configuration."
  (list :kind kind
        :prompt prompt
        :frozen (append (list :budget (yeah-control-budget control)
                              :max-nudges (yeah-control-max-nudges control)
                              :submitted-at (time-to-seconds))
                        (yeah-control-frozen-defaults control)
                        frozen)))

(defun yeah-control--steering-batch (control)
  "Pop all currently queued steering inputs from CONTROL.
Ordinary asks retain their FIFO positions.

The batch itself writes nothing into the journal: the caller says what
happened to the inputs — delivered to a run, or withdrawn with it."
  (let ((inputs nil))
    (dolist (input (yeah-input-pending (yeah-control-session control)))
      (when (eq 'steering (plist-get input :kind))
        (let ((taken (yeah-input-withdraw (yeah-control-session control)
                                          (plist-get input :id))))
          (when taken
            (push taken inputs)))))
    (nreverse inputs)))

(defun yeah-control--deliver-steering (control)
  "Return the steering of CONTROL that a running turn may take now.
The inputs leave the queue because a run takes them: the journal says
`input-taken' for each of them."
  (mapc (lambda (input) (yeah-control--write-taken control input))
        (yeah-control--steering-batch control)))

(defun yeah-control--journal-kind (input)
  "Return the kind of INPUT as the string the journal holds."
  (format "%s" (or (plist-get input :kind) 'ask)))

(defun yeah-control--write-queued (control input)
  "Write the `input-queued' event of INPUT into the journal of CONTROL.
The frozen configuration of the input belongs to the event.  A frozen
configuration the journal cannot represent is left out of it: the queue
event still tells the truth about the queue, and the run it belongs to
must not stop because of it."
  (let* ((session (yeah-control-session control))
         (fields (list :input_id (plist-get input :id)
                       :input_kind (yeah-control--journal-kind input)
                       :prompt (plist-get input :prompt)))
         (frozen (plist-get input :frozen)))
    (if frozen
        (condition-case nil
            (apply #'yeah-events-write session "input-queued"
                   (append fields (list :frozen frozen)))
          (error
           (apply #'yeah-events-write session "input-queued" fields)))
      (apply #'yeah-events-write session "input-queued" fields))))

(defun yeah-control--write-taken (control input &optional recovered)
  "Write the `input-taken' event of INPUT into the journal of CONTROL.
A RECOVERED input was started explicitly by the person, after a restart
or a cancellation: the journal then says `input-recovered'."
  (yeah-events-write (yeah-control-session control)
                     (if recovered "input-recovered" "input-taken")
                     :input_id (plist-get input :id)
                     :input_kind (yeah-control--journal-kind input)))

(defun yeah-control--write-withdrawn (control input reason)
  "Write the `input-withdrawn' event of INPUT into the journal of CONTROL.
REASON says why the input left the queue.  The id of the input is part of
the event: a withdrawn input must leave the pending list of the editor."
  (yeah-events-write (yeah-control-session control) "input-withdrawn"
                     :input_id (plist-get input :id)
                     :kind (yeah-control--journal-kind input)
                     :reason reason))

(defun yeah-control--release-steering (control)
  "Withdraw the steering that the run which just ended never delivered.
A steering is addressed to one run.  When that run is over, the
steering is not handed to the next one: it is withdrawn, and the
withdrawal is written into the journal, so that the person can see
that their words were not used."

The callback is memory-only and is never included in frozen input data.
Multiple listeners run in registration order and are removed before running."

(defun yeah-control--start-next (control &optional recovered)
  "Start the oldest pending ask in CONTROL when no turn is active.
A steering is not a task: it belongs to a run, and it is delivered at
a tool-batch boundary, never started on its own.
When RECOVERED is non-nil, the input was started explicitly by the

Return the active turn or nil when the queue holds no ask."

                (plist-get input :prompt)
                (yeah-control-transport control)
                (yeah-control-answerer control)

                    (yeah-control-budget control))
                (or (plist-get (plist-get input :frozen) :max-nudges)
                    (yeah-control-max-nudges control))

                  (setf (yeah-control-active-turn control) nil)
                  (yeah-control--release-steering control)
                  (yeah-control--notify-completion control input finished)
                  (yeah-control--start-next control))

(defun yeah-control-submit (control prompt &optional frozen on-complete)
  "Queue PROMPT with FROZEN data and return its persistent input id.
ON-COMPLETE receives one plist of shape
`:input-id ID :input INPUT :turn TURN-OR-NIL :state STATE'.  It is runtime
state only, never serialized with INPUT.  A queued input has its own completion
notification, and withdrawing it reports state `cancelled' with a nil turn."
  (let ((input (yeah-input-enqueue
                (yeah-control-session control)
                (yeah-control--frozen control 'ask prompt frozen))))
    (yeah-control--write-queued control input)
    (when on-complete
      (yeah-control-add-completion-listener control (plist-get input :id)
                                            on-complete))
    (unless (yeah-control-active-turn control)
      (yeah-control--start-next control))
    (plist-get input :id)))

(defun yeah-control-ask (control prompt &optional frozen)
  "Queue PROMPT as an ordinary ask with FROZEN configuration.
Retain the original return value: CONTROL's active turn, or nil when all work
finished synchronously.  Use `yeah-control-submit' to obtain the input id."
  (yeah-control-submit control prompt frozen)
  (yeah-control-active-turn control))

(defun yeah-control-steer (control prompt &optional frozen)
  "Queue clarification for the active run, or an ordinary ask when idle.
Steering is delivered after the current tool batch, never between tools."
  (let ((active (yeah-control-active-turn control)))
    (if (and active (not (yeah-turn-done active)))
        (let ((input (yeah-input-enqueue
                      (yeah-control-session control)
                      (yeah-control--frozen control 'steering prompt frozen))))
          (yeah-control--write-queued control input)
          input)
      (yeah-control-ask control prompt frozen)))
  (yeah-control-active-turn control))

(defun yeah-control-cancel (control &optional reason)
  "Cancel CONTROL's active turn, leaving pending inputs for subsequent runs."
  (when-let ((active (yeah-control-active-turn control)))
    (yeah-turn-cancel active reason)))

(defun yeah-control-recover-next (control)
  "Explicitly start the oldest pending input after a restart or cancellation.
The journal says `input-recovered': the input was started by the person,
not by the automatic continuation of a run."
  (yeah-control--start-next control t))

(defun yeah-control-pending (control)
  "Return CONTROL's pending inputs without executing them."
  (yeah-input-pending (yeah-control-session control)))

(defun yeah-control-withdraw (control id)
  "Withdraw pending input ID and complete its runtime listeners as cancelled.
The journal records the withdrawal with the id of the input: the pending
list of the editor is a projection of the journal, and a withdrawn input
must leave it."
  (when-let ((input (yeah-input-withdraw (yeah-control-session control) id)))
    (yeah-control--write-withdrawn control input "withdrawn by the person")
    (yeah-control--notify-completion control input nil 'cancelled)
    input))

(defun yeah-control-done-p (control)
  "Return non-nil when CONTROL has no active turn."
  (null (yeah-control-active-turn control)))

;;; yeah-acp.el --- ACP v1 agent over newline JSON-RPC -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Agent-side ACP v1 over newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0.  Sessions are real
;; Yeah sessions; prompt responses are sent when the run reaches a terminal
;; state; session/cancel is a notification; journal events become
;; session/update notifications through `yeah-events-write-functions'.
;;
;; A session is driven by a controller: the same one the attached path uses.
;; The controller owns the session's turn and its persistent pending queue,
;; so the wire can ask, steer, cancel, withdraw a pending input and recover
;; one.  There is no second queue in this module: the pending inputs of a
;; session are the ones the control keeps, and the queue the editor sees is
;; a projection of the journal -- the events that move an input in or out of
;; the queue reach the client as session/update notifications.
;;
;; `session/load' opens a session again and replays its journal: the records
;; of the session become session/update notifications, so that an editor can
;; rebuild the transcript of a session it opens a second time.
;;
;; An answer to a permission that arrives after the run that asked has ended
;; is not applied: the journal shows the question as deferred and the run as
;; ended, and the late answer changes nothing.
;;
;; The protocol is spoken over two transports.  On stdio the server reads
;; standard input with a blocking read, so a notification that arrives
;; while a prompt is running is read only after the prompt settled.  On a
;; socket the connection is a process, the data arrives in a filter and the
;; event loop keeps running, so a cancellation is handled while the prompt
;; is still running.  `yeah-acp-serve-socket' is the transport of the
;; primary deployment.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-acp-vocabulary)
(require 'yeah-control)
(require 'yeah-events)
(require 'yeah-product)
(require 'yeah-result)
(require 'yeah-turn)
(require 'yeah-wire)
(require 'yeah-wire-socket)

(defgroup yeah-acp nil
  "Yeah ACP v1 agent."
  :group 'yeah)

(defconst yeah-acp--agent-name "yeah")
(defconst yeah-acp--agent-version "0.1.0")

(defvar yeah-acp--sessions (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map ACP session ids to their Yeah session state.")

(defvar yeah-acp--pending-permissions (make-hash-table :test 'equal)
  "Map permission request ids to the question they ask.
The value names the session, the action and the resource, so that the
answer reaches the turn that asked and may be remembered for the
session.")

(defvar yeah-acp--connection nil
  "The connection being served, bound dynamically by the socket handler.
A session remembers which connection owns it, so the death of that
connection can cancel the work it started.")

(defvar yeah-acp--client-capabilities (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "Map every connection to the capabilities its client announced.
The key is the connection; the standard output connection is the key
nil.  What a client announced at `initialize' says what it
understands of the wire.")

(defun yeah-acp--jsonable-args (args)
  "Return ARGS as a JSON value: an array when every element serializes,
the printed form otherwise."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((array (apply #'vector args)))
        (ignore (json-serialize array))
        array)
    (error (format "%S" args))))

(defun yeah-acp--session-rules (session-id)
  "Return the permission rules that decide for SESSION-ID.
The standing permissions of the service come first and the decisions the
client remembered for this session come last: the last match wins."
  (let ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id)))
    (append (yeah-perm-rules-list) (plist-get state :rules))))

(defun yeah-acp--ask-client (session-id output request)
  "Ask the client about REQUEST and return the deferral of the question.
The question carries three answers: allow once, allow always (the decision
is remembered for the session) and reject.  The question itself is kept,
so that the answer reaches the turn that asked and may be remembered."
  (let* ((request-id (yeah-acp--fresh-id "perm"))
         (params (list :sessionId session-id
                       :toolCall (list :toolCallId request-id
                                       :title (format "%s on %s"
                                                      (plist-get request :action)
                                                      (plist-get request :resource))
                                       :rawInput
                                       (yeah-acp--jsonable-args
                                        (plist-get request :args)))
                       :options (vector
                                 (list :optionId "allow-once"
                                       :name "Allow once" :kind "allow_once")
                                 (list :optionId "allow-always"
                                       :name "Allow always" :kind "allow_always")
                                 (list :optionId "reject-once"
                                       :name "Reject" :kind "reject_once")))))
    (puthash request-id
             (list :session-id session-id
                   :action (plist-get request :action)
                   :resource (plist-get request :resource))
             yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
    (funcall output (json-serialize
                     (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id request-id
                           :method "session/request_permission"
                           :params params)))
    (list :defer request-id)))

(defun yeah-acp--client-answerer (session-id output)
  "Return the answerer of SESSION-ID that asks the client over the wire.
The rules decide first; what they do not name is asked of the client as a
`session/request_permission', and the call waits for the answer.  A safe
read needs no question: it is allowed, and it says why."
  (lambda (request)
    (let* ((action (plist-get request :action))
           (resource (plist-get request :resource))
           (effect (yeah-perm-effect action resource
                                     (yeah-acp--session-rules session-id))))
      (pcase effect
        ('allow (list :effect :allow :reply :once))
        ('deny (list :effect :deny :reply :reject
                     :reason (format "the rules deny %s on %s"
                                     action resource)))
        (_ (or (yeah-approval-safe-read-decision request)
               (yeah-acp--ask-client session-id output request)))))))

(defvar yeah-acp--counter 0
  "Monotonic counter for generated identifiers.")

(defvar yeah-acp--transport nil
  "Optional model transport used by the ACP server.")

(defvar yeah-acp-default-transport nil
  "Model transport of the service when none is passed at start.
A service init file (`yeah-service-init-file') sets this; nil falls back
to the gptel transport of the service's own configuration.")

(defvar yeah-acp--answerer nil
  "Optional permission answerer used by the ACP server.")

(defvar yeah-acp--output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line
  "Function receiving one serialized JSON message per call.")

(defvar yeah-acp--output nil
  "Output function of the connection being served, or nil for standard output.
This variable is bound dynamically while a connection is served, so the
messages of one connection do not reach another one.")

(defun yeah-acp--session-answerer (state)
  "Return the answerer of STATE: the client of the session over the wire.
The rules of the session decide first; what they do not name is asked of
the client as a `session/request_permission', and the call waits for the
answer.  The question is asked of the connection the session belongs to."
  (lambda (request)
    (funcall (or yeah-acp--answerer
                 (yeah-acp--client-answerer (plist-get state :id)
                                             (yeah-acp--output-for state)))
             request)))

(defun yeah-acp--make-control (state)
  "Return the controller of STATE.
The controller owns the turn of the session and its persistent pending
queue: the wire and the attached path share one queue, one set of journal
events and one set of semantics.  The transport and the answerer are the
service's, and the working directory travels with every input."
  (yeah-control-new (plist-get state :session)
                    (or yeah-acp--transport yeah-acp-default-transport)
                    (yeah-acp--session-answerer state)
                    nil nil
                    (list :cwd (plist-get state :cwd))))

(defun yeah-acp-version ()
  "Return the ACP protocol version spoken by Yeah."
  yeah-acp-protocol-version)

(defun yeah-acp--print-line (text)
  "Write TEXT and a newline to standard output.
The bytes of a serialized message are UTF-8, and they are written as
they are: `yeah-wire-print-line' knows how."
  (yeah-wire-print-line text))

(defun yeah-acp--emit (object)
  "Serialize OBJECT and pass it to the output function of this connection."

(defun yeah-acp--client-answerer (session-id output)
  "Return the answerer of SESSION-ID that asks the client over the wire.
The rules decide first; what they do not name is asked of the client as a
`session/request_permission', and the call waits for the answer.  A safe
read needs no question: it is allowed, and it says why."

                    (or yeah-acp--transport yeah-acp-default-transport)

(defun yeah-acp--input-update (kind fields)
  "Return an ACP update of KIND for a queue event with FIELDS.
The update names the input, its kind, the words the person wrote and, for a
withdrawal, the reason the input left the queue.  A field the event does not
carry is left out of the update."
  (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate kind)))
    (when-let ((input-id (plist-get fields :input_id)))
      (plist-put update :inputId input-id))
    (when-let ((input-kind (or (plist-get fields :input_kind)
                                (plist-get fields :kind))))
      (plist-put update :inputKind input-kind))
    (when-let ((prompt (plist-get fields :prompt)))
      (plist-put update :content (vector (list :type "text" :text prompt))))
    (when-let ((reason (plist-get fields :reason)))

  "Return the ACP update for the journal event TYPE with FIELDS, or nil.

whole update, so they travel only where they were asked for.  The

an input in or out of the queue have their own kinds, so that the
editor learns the queue from the journal and keeps no state of its own."

     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "user_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ("assistant-message"

                              (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ("finish"

     ;; writes it for the human, and the editor shows it as the answer of the

(defun yeah-acp--stop-reason (turn)
  "Return the ACP stopReason for terminal TURN."
  (pcase (yeah-turn-state turn)
    ('completed "end_turn")
    ('interrupted "cancelled")
    (_ "refusal")))

(defun yeah-acp--completion-stop-reason (completion)
  "Return the ACP stopReason of the control COMPLETION.
A withdrawn input has no turn: it was cancelled before it ever ran."
  (let ((turn (plist-get completion :turn)))
    (if turn
        (yeah-acp--stop-reason turn)
      (pcase (plist-get completion :state)
        ('completed "end_turn")
        ('interrupted "cancelled")
        ('cancelled "cancelled")
        (_ "refusal")))))

(defun yeah-acp-session-prompt (request id)
  "Queue a prompt for REQUEST and send its response later under request ID.
The prompt is an ordinary ask of the session's controller: it runs when the
session is idle and waits in the queue of the session when a run is active.
The response leaves when the run reaches a terminal state, and it carries the
same stop reasons as before."
  (unless (listp request)
    (signal 'user-error (list "session/prompt params must be an object")))
  (let* ((session-id (plist-get request :sessionId))
         (state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id t))
         (output (yeah-acp--output-for state))
         (control (plist-get state :control))
         (prompt (yeah-acp--prompt-text (plist-get request :prompt))))
    (yeah-control-submit
     control prompt nil
     (lambda (completion)
       (funcall
        output
        (json-serialize
         (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id
               :result (list :stopReason
                             (yeah-acp--completion-stop-reason completion))))))))
  nil)

(defun yeah-acp-session-cancel (request)
  "Handle the session/cancel notification REQUEST.
The cancel reaches the run of the session's controller: it stops the turn
that runs now and leaves the pending inputs of the session for a later run."
  (unless (and (listp request) (stringp (plist-get request :sessionId)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "session/cancel needs sessionId")))
  (let ((state (yeah-acp--session-state (plist-get request :sessionId))))
    (when state
      (yeah-control-cancel (plist-get state :control) "cancelled by ACP client")))
  nil)

(defun yeah-acp--require-session-id (request method)
  "Signal `user-error' unless REQUEST names a session for METHOD."
  (unless (and (listp request) (stringp (plist-get request :sessionId)))
    (signal 'user-error (list (format "%s needs sessionId" method)))))

(defun yeah-acp--input-ids (control)
  "Return the ids of the pending inputs of CONTROL."
  (mapcar (lambda (input) (plist-get input :id))
          (yeah-control-pending control)))

(defun yeah-acp--queued-id (session)
  "Return the id of the last input that entered the queue of SESSION.
The journal names every input that enters the queue, so the id of a queued
input is known even when the run it started has already ended."
  (let ((record (seq-find
                 (lambda (candidate)
                   (equal "input-queued" (plist-get candidate :type)))
                 (reverse (yeah-session-records session)))))
    (and record (plist-get record :input_id))))

(defun yeah-acp--steer-input-id (control session prompt)
  "Queue PROMPT as steering in CONTROL and return the id of the new input.
A steering that waits in the queue is named by the queue itself; a steering
that the control turned into an ask (the session was idle) is named by the
run it started."
  (let* ((before (yeah-acp--input-ids control))
         (turn (yeah-control-steer control prompt))
         (fresh (seq-difference (yeah-acp--input-ids control) before #'equal)))
    (or (car fresh)
        (and turn (yeah-turn-id turn))
        (yeah-acp--queued-id session))))

(defun yeah-acp-session-steer (request)
  "Queue a clarification for the running turn of REQUEST.
The answer names the input the clarification waits as.  A clarification that
the session cannot deliver to a running turn becomes an ordinary ask."
  (yeah-acp--require-session-id request "session/steer")
  (unless (stringp (plist-get request :prompt))
    (signal 'user-error (list "session/steer needs a prompt")))
  (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state (plist-get request :sessionId) t))
         (control (plist-get state :control))
         (session (plist-get state :session))
         (input-id (yeah-acp--steer-input-id
                    control session (plist-get request :prompt))))
    (unless input-id
      (signal 'user-error (list "session/steer: the clarification was not queued")))
    (list :inputId input-id)))

(defun yeah-acp-session-withdraw (request)
  "Withdraw the pending input named by REQUEST and answer with the outcome.
The answer names the input and says whether it was pending: an input that
is not in the queue is not withdrawn twice."
  (yeah-acp--require-session-id request "session/withdraw")
  (unless (stringp (plist-get request :inputId))
    (signal 'user-error (list "session/withdraw needs an inputId")))
  (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state (plist-get request :sessionId) t))
         (control (plist-get state :control))
         (input-id (plist-get request :inputId))
         (input (yeah-control-withdraw control input-id)))
    (list :inputId input-id
          :withdrawn (if input t :false))))

(defun yeah-acp-session-recover (request)
  "Start the oldest pending input of REQUEST and answer with the outcome.
Recovery is explicit: a pending input waits until the person asks for it,
and the journal says that it was recovered.

A run that is already active is not an error of the protocol: nothing is
recovered then, and the answer says so.  The answer names the INPUT that
was recovered, not the turn that carries it."
  (yeah-acp--require-session-id request "session/recover")
  (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state (plist-get request :sessionId) t))
         (control (plist-get state :control))
         (active (yeah-control-active-turn control))
         (input (seq-find (lambda (candidate)
                            (eq 'ask (plist-get candidate :kind)))
                          (yeah-control-pending control))))
    (if (and active (not (yeah-turn-done active)))
        (list :started :false)
      (let ((turn (yeah-control-recover-next control)))
        (if turn
            (list :started t :inputId (and input (plist-get input :id)))
          (list :started :false))))))

(defun yeah-acp--permission-decision (message)
  "Return the permission decision carried by client RESPONSE MESSAGE.
Only an explicit `allow-once' permits the effect.  A rejection, a
cancelled request, a protocol error, or an unknown option refuses it."
  (let* ((error (plist-get message :error))
         (result (plist-get message :result))
         (outcome (plist-get result :outcome))
         (state (plist-get outcome :outcome))
         (option (plist-get outcome :optionId)))
    (cond
     (error
      (list :effect :deny
            :reason "the client could not answer the permission request"))
     ((equal state "cancelled")
      (list :effect :deny :reason "cancelled"))
     ((equal option "allow-once")
      (list :effect :allow :reply :once))
     ((equal option "allow-always")
      ;; the person says that this action on this resource is allowed from
      ;; now on; the kernel remembers the decision
      (list :effect :allow :reply :always))
     ((equal option "reject-once")
      (list :effect :deny :reason "the person refused"))
     (t
      (list :effect :deny
            :reason "the client returned an unknown permission response")))))

(defun yeah-acp--turn-waiting-for (session-id request-id)
  "Return the turn of SESSION-ID that waits for the answer of REQUEST-ID.
The turn of a session is the one its controller runs: the answer of a
permission question reaches the turn that asked it."
  (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id))
         (control (and state (plist-get state :control)))
         (turn (and control (yeah-control-active-turn control))))
    (when (and turn
               (not (yeah-turn-done turn))
               (gethash request-id (yeah-turn-pending-permissions turn)))
      turn)))

(defun yeah-acp--remember-decision (question decision)
  "Remember an `always' DECISION for QUESTION in the rules of its session.
The decision is remembered for this session only: the standing permissions
of the service are not touched."
  (let ((session-id (plist-get question :session-id)))
    (when-let ((rule (yeah-approval-remember-rule
                      (list :action (plist-get question :action)
                            :resource (plist-get question :resource))
                      decision)))
      (let ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id)))
        (plist-put state :rules
                   (yeah-perm-rules-append (plist-get state :rules) rule))))))

(defun yeah-acp--route-response (message)
  "Route a client RESPONSE (a message with an id and no method) to the
permission it answers.  Return non-nil when it was a response."
  (let ((id (plist-get message :id)))
    (when (and id (null (plist-get message :method)))
      (when-let ((question (gethash id yeah-acp--pending-permissions)))
        (remhash id yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
        (let ((decision (yeah-acp--permission-decision message)))
          (when (yeah-approval-always-p decision)
            (yeah-acp--remember-decision question decision))
          (when-let ((turn (yeah-acp--turn-waiting-for
                            (plist-get question :session-id) id)))
            (yeah-turn-resume-permission turn id decision)))
        t))))

(defun yeah-acp--connection-closed (connection)
  "Cancel the work CONNECTION started and forget its pending questions.
A permission request whose asker is gone must never hang the run: the
turn is cancelled with the reason in the journal, and the request ids
of the dead connection are dropped."
  (let ((sessions nil))
    (maphash
     (lambda (id state)
       (when (eq connection (plist-get state :connection))
         (push id sessions)))
     yeah-acp--sessions)
    (let ((stale nil))
      (maphash (lambda (id question)
                 (when (memq (plist-get question :session-id) sessions)
                   (push id stale)))
               yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
      (dolist (id stale)
        (remhash id yeah-acp--pending-permissions)))
    (dolist (session-id sessions)
      (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id))
             (control (and state (plist-get state :control))))
        (when control
          (yeah-control-cancel control "the client disconnected"))))))

(defun yeah-acp--dispatch (method params id)
  "Dispatch ACP METHOD with PARAMS and request ID.
Return a response string for immediate requests, or nil for notifications
and asynchronously answered prompts."
  (pcase method
    ("initialize"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-initialize params)))
    ("session/new"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-new params)))
    ("session/load"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-load params)))
    ("session/prompt"
     (yeah-acp-session-prompt params id))
    ("session/cancel"
     (yeah-acp-session-cancel params))
    ("session/steer"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-steer params)))
    ("session/withdraw"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-withdraw params)))
    ("session/recover"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-recover params)))
    (_
     (yeah-acp--error id -32601 (format "Method not found: %s" method)))))

(defun yeah-acp-handle-message (json-string)
  "Handle one JSON-RPC message string and return a response string or nil."
  (condition-case nil
      (let* ((parsed (json-parse-string json-string :object-type 'plist
                                        :array-type 'list))
             (method (plist-get parsed :method))
             (id (plist-get parsed :id))
             (params (or (plist-get parsed :params) '())))
        (if (null method)
            (when (yeah-acp--route-response parsed)
              nil)
          (condition-case err

handled while that prompt is still running, and two connections are
served at the same time."

        yeah-acp--answerer answerer)

   service
   (lambda (line respond &optional connection)
     (let ((yeah-acp--output respond)
           (yeah-acp--connection connection))
       (let ((response (yeah-acp-handle-message line)))

  (clrhash yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--client-capabilities)

## 4. Processes, waiting and cancellation

- Start subprocesses with `make-process`, never blocking shell commands in a
  tool body. Use argv arrays where possible; make any shell interpretation an
  explicit part of the tool contract.
- Set process coding systems deliberately, normally UTF-8. Bound collected

  running waits for them instead of breaking the run. The calls that are not
  running yet are kept and run when the running batch has settled; the state

  callbacks. It does not claim transactional rollback, recursive process-tree

;;; yeah-wire-socket.el --- the socket transport for Yeah's wire protocols -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The stdio transport of a wire protocol reads standard input with a
;; blocking read.  While that read blocks, the event loop of Emacs does
;; not run, so a notification that arrives while a request is being
;; answered is read only after the answer settled.  A reader thread does
;; not help: a thread blocked in `read-string' holds the interpreter lock,
;; and the whole Emacs stops until the read returns.
;;
;; A socket does help.  Emacs represents a connection as a process, so the
;; data of a connection arrives in a filter and the event loop keeps
;; running while the server waits.  A `session/cancel' that arrives during
;; a running prompt is therefore handled while the prompt is still
;; running, and two connections can be served at the same time.
;;
;; The transport is a local Unix socket by default; `ipv4' serves a
;; loopback TCP port instead.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire-socket nil
  "The socket transport of Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defvar yeah-wire-socket--pending (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "The part of the last line received on each connection.")

(defun yeah-wire-socket--lines (connection chunk)
  "Return the complete lines in CHUNK for CONNECTION and keep the rest.
The incomplete tail of CONNECTION is kept for the next chunk."
  (let* ((pending (gethash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending ""))
         (combined (concat pending chunk))
         (parts (split-string combined "\n"))
         (complete (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                        parts
                      (butlast parts)))
         (tail (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                    ""
                  (car (last parts)))))
    (puthash connection tail yeah-wire-socket--pending)
    complete))

(defun yeah-wire-socket--respond (connection text)
  "Send TEXT to CONNECTION as one line."
  (when (process-live-p connection)
    (process-send-string connection (concat text "\n"))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-server (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Listen on the local socket SERVICE and serve connections with HANDLER.
FAMILY is `local' for a Unix socket and `ipv4' for a loopback TCP port.
HANDLER is called with (LINE RESPOND CONNECTION) for every complete line
of input; RESPOND takes one message and sends it back to that connection.
ON-CLOSE, when given, is called with CONNECTION after it closed: a
question asked of a dead connection must not hang the server.
Return the server process."
  (make-network-process
   :name "yeah-wire-socket"
   :server t
   :family (or family 'local)
   :service service
   :noquery t
   :sentinel
   (when on-close
     (lambda (connection _event)
       (when (memq (process-status connection) '(closed failed exit))
         (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending)
         (funcall on-close connection))))
   :filter
   (lambda (connection chunk)
     (cond
      ((string= chunk "")
       (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending))
      (t
       (dolist (line (yeah-wire-socket--lines connection chunk))
         (unless (string-blank-p line)
           (funcall handler line
                    (lambda (text) (yeah-wire-socket--respond connection text))
                    connection))))))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-serve (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Serve connections on SERVICE with HANDLER until the server stops.
FAMILY, HANDLER and ON-CLOSE mean what they mean in
`yeah-wire-socket-server'."
  (let ((server (yeah-wire-socket-server service handler family on-close)))
    (while (process-live-p server)
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05))
    server))

(provide 'yeah-wire-socket)
;;; yeah-wire-socket.el ends here
