;;; yeah-wire.el --- shared stdio plumbing for the wire protocols -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; In batch mode Emacs reads standard input a line at a time with
;; `read-string'; `read-char' does not see it.  A server therefore reads one
;; request, then pumps the event loop until the work it started has settled,
;; so asynchronous answers leave immediately instead of waiting for the next
;; request.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire nil
  "Shared stdio plumbing for Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defun yeah-wire-read-line ()
  "Read one line from standard input.
Return the line without its newline, or nil at end of file."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((line (read-string "")))
        (if (or (null line) (string= line "")) nil line))
    (error nil)))

(defun yeah-wire-print-line (text)
  "Write TEXT and a newline to standard output.
TEXT is one message of a wire protocol, serialized as JSON.  The
serializer returns a unibyte string whose bytes are UTF-8, and printing
such a string as it is makes Emacs read every byte as a character of
Latin-1 and write it back as UTF-8: the client reads the text twice
over, and a Russian answer arrives as mojibake.  The bytes are decoded
as UTF-8 before they are printed, so the client reads what the model
wrote.

A text that is not UTF-8 is printed as it is: a wire that carries
broken bytes is better than a wire that carries nothing."
  (princ (if (and (stringp text) (not (multibyte-string-p text)))
              (condition-case nil
                  (decode-coding-string text 'utf-8)
                (error text))
            text))
  (terpri))

(defun yeah-wire-pump-until (predicate &optional timeout)
  "Pump the event loop until PREDICATE returns non-nil or TIMEOUT seconds pass.
TIMEOUT defaults to 600 seconds.  Return non-nil when the predicate held."
  (let* ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 600)))
         (ok nil))
    (while (and (not ok) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (setq ok (and (functionp predicate) (funcall predicate))))
    ok))

(provide 'yeah-wire)
;;; yeah-wire.el ends here

;;; Commentary:

;;; Code:

(require 'json)

  "Position in the server output buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--emacs ()

      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs")))

(defun yeah-check--lib-directory ()
  "Return the directory holding Yeah's Elisp modules."
  (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-mcp") "yeah-mcp.el")))

(defun yeah-check--start-server (feature expression)
  "Start a server process serving FEATURE with EXPRESSION.
Return the process and the buffer holding its output."
  (let ((buffer (generate-new-buffer "*yeah-wire-test*")))
    (with-current-buffer buffer
      (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
    (list (make-process
           :name "yeah-wire-test"
           :buffer buffer
           :command (list (yeah-check--emacs) "-Q" "--batch"
                          "-L" (yeah-check--lib-directory)
                          "-l" feature "--eval" expression)
           :connection-type 'pipe
           :noquery t
           :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                     (with-current-buffer buffer
                       (insert chunk))))
          buffer)))

(defun yeah-check--send (process object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line to PROCESS."
  (process-send-string process (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

(defun yeah-check--await-line (buffer &optional timeout)
  "Return the next complete JSON line in BUFFER, waiting at most TIMEOUT."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))

      (progn

                         "yeah-mcp"
                         (format "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) (yeah-mcp-serve))"
                                 data-home)))

        (let* ((started (yeah-check--start-server
                         "yeah-acp"
                         (format "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) (yeah-acp-serve))"
                                 data-home)))
               (process (nth 0 started))
               (buffer (nth 1 started)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion 1)))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (equal 1 (plist-get (plist-get response :result)
                                        :protocolVersion))
              (push (format "ACP initialize did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))

           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "session/new"
                 :params (list :cwd data-home :mcpServers nil)))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (stringp (plist-get (plist-get response :result) :sessionId))
              (push (format "ACP session/new did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (when (process-live-p process)
            (delete-process process))))

    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "wire: %s" failure))
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; yeah-wire-socket.el --- the socket transport for Yeah's wire protocols -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The stdio transport of a wire protocol reads standard input with a
;; blocking read.  While that read blocks, the event loop of Emacs does
;; not run, so a notification that arrives while a request is being
;; answered is read only after the answer settled.  A reader thread does
;; not help: a thread blocked in `read-string' holds the interpreter lock,
;; and the whole Emacs stops until the read returns.
;;
;; A socket does help.  Emacs represents a connection as a process, so the
;; data of a connection arrives in a filter and the event loop keeps
;; running while the server waits.  A `session/cancel' that arrives during
;; a running prompt is therefore handled while the prompt is still
;; running, and two connections can be served at the same time.
;;
;; The transport is a local Unix socket by default; `ipv4' serves a
;; loopback TCP port instead.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire-socket nil
  "The socket transport of Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defvar yeah-wire-socket--pending (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "The part of the last line received on each connection.")

(defun yeah-wire-socket--lines (connection chunk)
  "Return the complete lines in CHUNK for CONNECTION and keep the rest.
The incomplete tail of CONNECTION is kept for the next chunk."
  (let* ((pending (gethash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending ""))
         (combined (concat pending chunk))
         (parts (split-string combined "\n"))
         (complete (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                        parts
                      (butlast parts)))
         (tail (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                    ""
                  (car (last parts)))))
    (puthash connection tail yeah-wire-socket--pending)
    complete))

(defun yeah-wire-socket--respond (connection text)
  "Send TEXT to CONNECTION as one line."
  (when (process-live-p connection)
    (process-send-string connection (concat text "\n"))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-server (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Listen on the local socket SERVICE and serve connections with HANDLER.
FAMILY is `local' for a Unix socket and `ipv4' for a loopback TCP port.
HANDLER is called with (LINE RESPOND CONNECTION) for every complete line
of input; RESPOND takes one message and sends it back to that connection.
ON-CLOSE, when given, is called with CONNECTION after it closed: a
question asked of a dead connection must not hang the server.
Return the server process."
  (make-network-process
   :name "yeah-wire-socket"
   :server t
   :family (or family 'local)
   :service service
   :noquery t
   :sentinel
   (when on-close
     (lambda (connection _event)
       (when (memq (process-status connection) '(closed failed exit))
         (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending)
         (funcall on-close connection))))
   :filter
   (lambda (connection chunk)
     (cond
      ((string= chunk "")
       (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending))
      (t
       (dolist (line (yeah-wire-socket--lines connection chunk))
         (unless (string-blank-p line)
           (funcall handler line
                    (lambda (text) (yeah-wire-socket--respond connection text))
                    connection))))))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-serve (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Serve connections on SERVICE with HANDLER until the server stops.
FAMILY, HANDLER and ON-CLOSE mean what they mean in
`yeah-wire-socket-server'."
  (let ((server (yeah-wire-socket-server service handler family on-close)))
    (while (process-live-p server)
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05))
    server))

(provide 'yeah-wire-socket)
;;; yeah-wire-socket.el ends here

  (format "%s-%d-%x" prefix yeah-acp--counter (random #x1000000)))

(defun yeah-acp--session-state (session-id &optional required)
  "Return the ACP state for SESSION-ID, optionally requiring it to exist."
  (let ((state (gethash session-id yeah-acp--sessions)))
    (when (and required (null state))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "unknown ACP session: %s" session-id))))
    state))

(defun yeah-acp-initialize (handshake)
  "Negotiate an ACP HANDSHAKE and return agent capabilities."
  (unless (and (listp handshake)
               (integerp (plist-get handshake :protocolVersion)))
    (signal 'user-error
            (list "initialize: protocolVersion must be an integer")))
  (yeah-acp--remember-capabilities handshake)
  (list :protocolVersion yeah-acp-protocol-version
        :agentInfo (list :name yeah-acp--agent-name
                         :version yeah-acp--agent-version)
        :agentCapabilities
        (list :loadSession t
              :promptCapabilities (list :image :false
                                        :audio :false
                                        :embeddedContext :false)
              :mcpCapabilities (list :http :false :sse :false))))

(defun yeah-acp--remember-capabilities (handshake)
  "Remember the client capabilities of HANDSHAKE for the current connection.
What the client announced is what it understands of the wire: Yeah's own
events travel to the clients that asked for them and to nobody else."
  (puthash yeah-acp--connection
           (plist-get handshake :clientCapabilities)
           yeah-acp--client-capabilities))

(defun yeah-acp--queue-events-p (state)
  "Return non-nil when the client of STATE asked for Yeah's queue events.
The queue events are Yeah's own vocabulary, not the vocabulary of ACP: a
client that does not know them refuses the whole update.  A client asks
for them in the `_meta' of the capabilities it announced."
  (let* ((capabilities (gethash (plist-get state :connection)
                                yeah-acp--client-capabilities))
         (meta (and (listp capabilities) (plist-get capabilities :_meta))))
    (and (listp meta)
         (eq t (plist-get meta yeah-acp-queue-events-capability)))))

(defun yeah-acp--validate-session-request (request &optional load)
  "Validate a session/new or session/load REQUEST.  LOAD selects its shape."
  (unless (listp request)
    (signal 'user-error (list "session request must be an object")))
  (when load
    (unless (stringp (plist-get request :sessionId))
      (signal 'user-error (list "session/load needs sessionId"))))
  (unless (and (stringp (plist-get request :cwd))
               (file-name-absolute-p (plist-get request :cwd)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "session request needs an absolute cwd")))
  (unless (or (null (plist-get request :mcpServers))
              (eq (plist-get request :mcpServers) :null)
              (listp (plist-get request :mcpServers)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "mcpServers must be an array or null"))))

(defun yeah-acp--send-update (session-id update &optional output)
  "Send a session/update notification for SESSION-ID and UPDATE.
OUTPUT receives the serialized message and defaults to standard output."
  (funcall (or output yeah-acp--output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line)
           (json-serialize
            (list :jsonrpc "2.0"
                  :method "session/update"
                  :params (list :sessionId session-id :update update)))))

(defun yeah-acp--content-chunk (kind text)
  "Return an ACP content chunk of KIND containing TEXT.
The content of an ACP chunk is one content block, not an array of them:
the protocol says so, and a client that checks the wire refuses a chunk
that carries an array."
  (list :sessionUpdate kind
        :content (list :type "text" :text (or text ""))))

(defun yeah-acp--tool-input (args)
  "Return ARGS as a JSON value for the wire.
The journal holds the arguments of a call in their printed form, because the
journal is a log of what happened and not a place for structured data.  A
client that shows the call wants the values themselves, so the printed form
is read back into them.

The arguments come from the model, so the printed form is read as data and
not as code: a form that the reader would evaluate is not read at all, and
the printed form travels to the client as it is."
  (if (stringp args)
      (condition-case nil
          (if (string-match-p "#\\." args)
              args
            (let ((value (car (read-from-string args))))
              (cond
               ((and (listp value) (proper-list-p value))
                (apply #'vector (mapcar #'yeah-result-json-safe value)))
               ((vectorp value) value)
               (t (format "%S" value)))))
        (error args))
    args))

(defun yeah-acp--tool-call (tool-call-id name status &optional input result)
  "Return a tool_call or tool_call_update ACP update for TOOL-CALL-ID.
INPUT is what the tool was called with and RESULT is what it returned.
The protocol has a field for each of them, and a client that shows the call
of a tool shows them: a call without its input is a name."
  (if (eq status 'started)
      (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate "tool_call"
                           :toolCallId tool-call-id
                           :title name
                           :status "pending")))
        (when input
          (plist-put update :rawInput input))
        update)
    (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate "tool_call_update"
                         :toolCallId tool-call-id
                         :status (if (eq status 'failed) "failed" "completed")
                         :content (vector (list :type "text"
                                                :text (or result ""))))))
      (when result
        (plist-put update :rawOutput result))
      update)))

(defun yeah-acp--input-update (kind fields)
  "Return an ACP update of KIND for a queue event with FIELDS.
The update names the input, its kind, the words the person wrote and, for a
withdrawal, the reason the input left the queue.  A field the event does not
carry is left out of the update."
  (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate kind)))
    (when-let ((input-id (plist-get fields :input_id)))
      (plist-put update :inputId input-id))
    (when-let ((input-kind (or (plist-get fields :input_kind)
                                (plist-get fields :kind))))
      (plist-put update :inputKind input-kind))
    (when-let ((prompt (plist-get fields :prompt)))
      (plist-put update :content (vector (list :type "text" :text prompt))))
    (when-let ((reason (plist-get fields :reason)))
      (plist-put update :reason reason))
    update))

(defun yeah-acp--update-for (type fields id &optional queue-events)
  "Return the ACP update for the journal event TYPE with FIELDS, or nil.
ID names the record.  QUEUE-EVENTS says that the client understands
Yeah's own queue events; a client that does not know them refuses the
whole update, so they travel only where they were asked for.  The
pending queue of a session is visible in the log: the events that move
an input in or out of the queue have their own kinds, so that the
editor learns the queue from the journal and keeps no state of its own."
  (pcase type
    ("user-message"
     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "user_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ("assistant-message"
     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "agent_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ("finish"
     ;; The summary of a finished run is the answer of the agent: the model
     ;; writes it for the human, and the editor shows it as the answer of the
     ;; run.  A client that speaks ACP expects the words of the agent as the
     ;; message of the agent, and a model that answers only through the
     ;; `finish' tool says nothing else.
     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "agent_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :summary)))
    ("tool-request"
     (yeah-acp--tool-call
      (or (plist-get fields :tool_call_id) id)
      (plist-get fields :tool) 'started
      (yeah-acp--tool-input (plist-get fields :args))))
    ("tool-end"
     (yeah-acp--tool-call
      (or (plist-get fields :tool_call_id) id)
      (plist-get fields :tool)
      (if (yeah-events-boolean-p (plist-get fields :ok))
          'completed
        'failed)
      nil
      (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ((and (guard queue-events) "input-queued")
     (yeah-acp--input-update "input_queued" fields))
    ((and (guard queue-events) "input-taken")
     (yeah-acp--input-update "input_taken" fields))
    ((and (guard queue-events) "input-recovered")
     (yeah-acp--input-update "input_recovered" fields))
    ((and (guard queue-events) "input-withdrawn")
     (yeah-acp--input-update "input_withdrawn" fields))
    (_ nil)))

(defun yeah-acp--observe-event (state session type fields id)
  "Send ACP updates for journal events belonging to STATE's SESSION."
  (when (eq session (plist-get state :session))
    (let ((update (yeah-acp--update-for type fields id
                                         (yeah-acp--queue-events-p state))))
      (when update
        (yeah-acp--send-update (plist-get state :id) update
                               (yeah-acp--output-for state))))))

(defun yeah-acp--replay (state session)
  "Send the journal of SESSION to the client as session/update notifications.
Return the number of records that were replayed.  The editor rebuilds its
transcript from them: the messages, the tool calls and the queue events of
the session, in the order the journal holds them."
  (let ((output (yeah-acp--output-for state))
        (queue-events (yeah-acp--queue-events-p state))
        (count 0))
    (dolist (record (yeah-session-records session))
      (let ((update (yeah-acp--update-for
                     (plist-get record :type)
                     (yeah-session-record-fields record)
                     (plist-get record :id)
                     queue-events)))
        (when update
          (yeah-acp--send-update (plist-get state :id) update output)
          (setq count (1+ count)))))
    count))

(defun yeah-acp--output-for (state)
  "Return the output function of STATE: its connection's, or the global one."
  (or (plist-get state :output) yeah-acp--output-function
      #'yeah-acp--print-line))

(defun yeah-acp--register-session (session cwd)
  "Register SESSION for ACP and return its state plist.
The state carries the output function of the connection the session was
created on, so its notifications reach that connection; when the session
was created without a connection the current output function is used.
The state also carries the rules the client remembered for this session:
a decision of the client is remembered here and in no other session.
The state carries the controller of the session: its turn and its queue."
  (let* ((id (plist-get session :id))
         (previous (gethash id yeah-acp--sessions))
         (state (list :id id :session session :cwd cwd :listener nil
                      :output yeah-acp--output
                      :connection yeah-acp--connection
                      :rules nil))
         (listener (lambda (observed-session type fields event-id)
                     (yeah-acp--observe-event state observed-session type fields event-id))))
    (when previous
      (when-let ((old (plist-get previous :listener)))
        (setq yeah-events-write-functions
              (delete old yeah-events-write-functions))))
    (plist-put state :listener listener)
    (plist-put state :control (yeah-acp--make-control state))
    (add-to-list 'yeah-events-write-functions listener)
    (puthash id state yeah-acp--sessions)
    state))

(defun yeah-acp-session-new (request)
  "Create a real Yeah session for ACP REQUEST and return `(:sessionId ID)'."
  (yeah-acp--validate-session-request request)
  (let* ((cwd (file-truename (plist-get request :cwd)))
         (root (yeah-product-session-root cwd))
         (session (yeah-session-open (yeah-acp--fresh-id "session") root)))
    (yeah-acp--register-session session cwd)
    (list :sessionId (plist-get session :id))))

(defun yeah-acp-session-load (request)
  "Load an existing session and replay its journal into the editor's view.
The records of the session become session/update notifications, so that the
editor can rebuild the transcript of a session it opens again.  The answer
names the session and the number of records that were replayed."
  (yeah-acp--validate-session-request request t)
  (let* ((cwd (file-truename (plist-get request :cwd)))
         (root (yeah-product-session-root cwd))
         (session-id (plist-get request :sessionId)))
    (unless (file-exists-p (yeah-session--path-for session-id root))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "unknown ACP session: %s" session-id))))
    (let* ((session (yeah-session-open session-id root))
           (state (yeah-acp--register-session session cwd)))
      (list :sessionId (plist-get session :id)
            :replayed (yeah-acp--replay state session)))))

(defun yeah-acp--prompt-text (blocks)
  "Return prompt text from ACP content BLOCKS.
Text and resource_link blocks are supported; every other block is refused."
  (unless (listp blocks)
    (signal 'user-error (list "session/prompt needs a prompt array")))
  (mapconcat
   (lambda (block)
     (pcase (plist-get block :type)
       ("text" (or (plist-get block :text) ""))
       ("resource_link"
        (format "[%s](%s)"
                (or (plist-get block :name) "resource")
                (or (plist-get block :uri) "")))
       (_ (signal 'user-error
                  (list (format "unsupported prompt block: %S"
                                (plist-get block :type)))))))
   blocks "\n"))

(defun yeah-acp--stop-reason (turn)
  "Return the ACP stopReason for terminal TURN."
  (pcase (yeah-turn-state turn)
    ('completed "end_turn")
    ('interrupted "cancelled")
    (_ "refusal")))

(defun yeah-acp--completion-stop-reason (completion)
  "Return the ACP stopReason of the control COMPLETION.
A withdrawn input has no turn: it was cancelled before it ever ran."
  (let ((turn (plist-get completion :turn)))
    (if turn
        (yeah-acp--stop-reason turn)
      (pcase (plist-get completion :state)
        ('completed "end_turn")
        ('interrupted "cancelled")
        ('cancelled "cancelled")
        (_ "refusal")))))

(defun yeah-acp-session-prompt (request id)
  "Queue a prompt for REQUEST and send its response later under request ID.
The prompt is an ordinary ask of the session's controller: it runs when the
session is idle and waits in the queue of the session when a run is active.
The response leaves when the run reaches a terminal state, and it carries the
same stop reasons as before."
  (unless (listp request)
    (signal 'user-error (list "session/prompt params must be an object")))
  (let* ((session-id (plist-get request :sessionId))
         (state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id t))
         (output (yeah-acp--output-for state))
         (control (plist-get state :control))
         (prompt (yeah-acp--prompt-text (plist-get request :prompt))))

;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; This module is the only integration point between Yeah and gptel.  A
;; request carries its own backend, model, tools and system prompt; Yeah does
;; not install global hooks or change the user's global gptel configuration.
;;
;; gptel intentionally reads several request settings dynamically.  The
;; `let' bindings in `yeah-gptel-request' follow its public contract: they
;; give one request a frozen configuration without changing global values.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-tools)
(require 'gptel nil t)

(declare-function gptel-request "gptel"
  (&optional prompt &key callback buffer position context dry-run
                    stream in-place system schema transforms fsm))
(declare-function gptel-make-tool "gptel" (&rest slots))
(defvar gptel-backend nil)
(defvar gptel-model nil)
(defvar gptel-tools nil)
(defvar gptel-include-reasoning nil)
(defvar gptel-use-context nil)
(defvar gptel-use-tools nil)
(defvar gptel-version nil)

(defgroup yeah-gptel nil
  "Yeah / private gptel transport adapter."
  :group 'yeah)

(defconst yeah-gptel--supported-versions '("0.9.9.5" "0.9.9.6")
  "gptel versions whose request contract has been checked by Yeah.")

(defcustom yeah-gptel-prelude
  (concat
   "# Yeah — system prompt\n\n"
   "You are Yeah, an agent running inside Emacs through the Yeah harness. "
   "Act with the advertised tools; do not narrate what you are about to do. "
   "Read files with `read', find files with `glob' and `grep', change them "
   "with `edit', and run commands with `bash'. Your edits are saved to disk. "
   "When the work is done and verified, call the `finish' tool with a summary. "
   "A text answer that only describes what you will do is not a completion: "
   "it is answered with a nudge naming the tools you have not called yet.\n")
  "Default system prompt for Yeah model requests.
A model that is only told to be helpful narrates its plan instead of acting.
The harness asks for actions, not for a plan."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-gptel)

(defcustom yeah-gptel-include-reasoning t
  "How the model's reasoning is kept in the conversation.
A model that reasons narrates its plan, and dropping that plan from the
history makes the model start the task over on every turn.  Keep the
reasoning in the conversation by default; set this to nil to hide it.
The value is bound per request, never mutated globally."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Keep the reasoning" t)
                 (const :tag "Hide it" nil))
  :group 'yeah-gptel)

(defun yeah-gptel--require-gptel (what)
  "Signal `user-error' unless gptel is available, naming WHAT wanted it."
  (unless (fboundp 'gptel-request)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-gptel: %s needs gptel, which is not loaded" what))))
  t)

(defun yeah-gptel-check-contract ()
  "Validate the gptel contract used by Yeah.
Return t when the loaded gptel is supported.  Signal `user-error' for an
unknown version or missing request/tool bindings instead of silently
continuing with an incompatible transport."
  (yeah-gptel--require-gptel "yeah-gptel-check-contract")
  (unless (and (boundp 'gptel-version)
               (stringp gptel-version))
    (signal 'user-error
            (list "yeah-gptel: loaded gptel does not expose `gptel-version'")))
  (unless (member gptel-version yeah-gptel--supported-versions)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-gptel: unsupported gptel version %S; supported: %s"
                          gptel-version
                          (string-join yeah-gptel--supported-versions ", ")))))
  (dolist (variable '(gptel-backend gptel-model gptel-tools
                      gptel-use-tools gptel-use-context))
    (unless (boundp variable)
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-gptel: gptel %s does not bind %S"
                            gptel-version variable)))))
  (unless (fboundp 'gptel-make-tool)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-gptel: gptel %s does not define `gptel-make-tool'"
                          gptel-version))))
  t)

(defun yeah-gptel--argument-type (type)
  "Return the JSON Schema type name for registry TYPE."
  (pcase type
    ('string  "string")
    ('integer "integer")
    ('boolean "boolean")
    ('symbol  "string")
    (_        "string")))

(defun yeah-gptel-tool-for (name)
  "Return a gptel tool description for registry tool NAME.
The confirmation function always returns true, so gptel returns tool calls
to Yeah's callback instead of executing them outside Yeah's permission and
logging path."
  (yeah-gptel--require-gptel "yeah-gptel-tool-for")
  (unless (fboundp 'gptel-make-tool)
    (signal 'user-error (list "yeah-gptel-tool-for: gptel-make-tool is unavailable")))
  (let ((spec (yeah-tools-get name)))
    (unless spec
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-gptel-tool-for: no such tool: %S" name))))
    (gptel-make-tool
     :name name
     :function (lambda (&rest args)
                 (yeah-tools-call name (yeah-tools-normalize-args name args)))
     :description (plist-get spec :description)
     :args (mapcar (lambda (param)
                     (list :name (plist-get param :name)
                           :description (format "the %s argument"
                                                 (plist-get param :name))
                           :type (yeah-gptel--argument-type
                                  (plist-get param :type))))
                   (plist-get spec :input))
     :confirm (lambda (&rest _args) t))))

(defun yeah-gptel--request-tools (tools)
  "Resolve the request TOOLS option.
`registry' builds tools from Yeah's registry, nil disables tools, and a list
is used as an explicit list of gptel tool objects."
  (pcase tools
    ('registry (mapcar #'yeah-gptel-tool-for (yeah-tools-names)))
    ('nil nil)
    ((pred listp) tools)
    (_ (signal 'user-error
               (list (format "yeah-gptel-request: invalid tools option: %S" tools))))))

(defun yeah-gptel--usage (info)
  "Return normalized token usage from request INFO, or nil when unavailable."
  (when-let ((tokens (plist-get info :tokens)))
    (list :input (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :input))
                      (plist-get tokens :input))
          :output (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :output))
                       (plist-get tokens :output))
          :cache (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :cache))
                      (plist-get tokens :cache))
          :cached (and (numberp (plist-get tokens :cached))
                       (plist-get tokens :cached)))))

(defun yeah-gptel--failure-reason (info)
  "Return a printable provider failure reason from request INFO."
  (let ((reason (or (plist-get info :error)
                    (plist-get info :status)
                    "no response")))
    (if (stringp reason) reason (format "%S" reason))))

(defun yeah-gptel--normalize-response (response info)
  "Normalize gptel RESPONSE and INFO for Yeah's run loop.
Text, reasoning, tool calls/results and the streaming sentinel t retain
gptel's public shapes.  Failures and unknown shapes become `(error . REASON)'."
  (cond
   ((or (stringp response) (eq response t)) response)
   ((and (consp response)
         (memq (car response) '(reasoning tool-call tool-result)))
    response)
   ((eq response 'abort) (cons 'error "the model request was aborted"))
   ((null response) (cons 'error (yeah-gptel--failure-reason info)))
   (t (cons 'error (format "unsupported gptel response shape: %S" response)))))

(defun yeah-gptel--callback (callback response info)
  "Deliver normalized RESPONSE and INFO to CALLBACK."
  (let ((normalized-info (and (listp info) (copy-sequence info))))
    (when-let ((usage (yeah-gptel--usage info)))
      (setq normalized-info (plist-put normalized-info :yeah-usage usage)))
    (funcall callback
             (yeah-gptel--normalize-response response info)
             normalized-info)))

;;;###autoload
(cl-defun yeah-gptel-request
    (prompt callback &key backend model (tools 'registry)
                    (system yeah-gptel-prelude) stream context dry-run)
  "Ask the model PROMPT and call CALLBACK with its response and request info.

This is the only place in Yeah that calls `gptel-request'.  BACKEND and MODEL
default to the user's current gptel choices.  TOOLS is `registry' for Yeah's
registered tools, nil for no tools, or an explicit list of gptel tools.
SYSTEM defaults to `yeah-gptel-prelude' and may be nil.  STREAM, CONTEXT and
DRY-RUN have the meanings documented by `gptel-request'.

Responses retain gptel's text/reasoning/tool shapes; failures become
`(error . REASON)'.  When usage is available, CALLBACK's info contains
`:yeah-usage' with normalized input/output/cache/cached counts.

The configuration is captured for this request only.  Global gptel settings
are not modified and ambient gptel editor context is disabled.  The return
value is gptel's request state machine, which can be inspected or aborted."
  (unless (functionp callback)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-gptel-request: callback is not a function: %S"
                          callback))))
  (yeah-gptel-check-contract)
  (let* ((request-tools (yeah-gptel--request-tools tools))
         (gptel-backend (or backend gptel-backend))
         (gptel-model (or model gptel-model))
         (gptel-tools request-tools)
         (gptel-use-tools (and request-tools t))
         (gptel-use-context nil)
         (gptel-include-reasoning yeah-gptel-include-reasoning))
    (gptel-request prompt
                   :callback (lambda (response info)
                               (yeah-gptel--callback callback response info))
                   :system system
                   :stream stream
                   :context context
                   :dry-run dry-run)))

(defun yeah-gptel-bind-tools (&optional buffer)
  "Advertise Yeah's registry as buffer-local gptel tools in BUFFER.
This helper is for interactive gptel buffers only.  `yeah-gptel-request'
passes its own tools directly and does not depend on this buffer state."
  (yeah-gptel--require-gptel "yeah-gptel-bind-tools")
  (with-current-buffer (or buffer (current-buffer))
    (setq-local gptel-tools
                (mapcar #'yeah-gptel-tool-for (yeah-tools-names)))))

(provide 'yeah-gptel)

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The transport of Yeah answers with the shapes of gptel, and the shapes do
;; not all mean the same thing:
;;
;;   - a model that reasons sends its thinking before its answer, and the
;;     thinking is not the answer: it is the road to the answer;
;;   - a model that acts instead of talking answers with a tool call, and that
;;     is an answer: the model reached for a tool and the transport carried
;;     the call;
;;   - the result of a tool that ran is on its way to the model, and it is
;;     not the answer either;
;;   - gptel sends the sentinel `t' when the stream is over;
;;   - a request that ends in an error is the end of the road.
;;
;; The decision lives here, in the kernel, and not in the stands that ask a
;; real model: the run loop has to make it, the compaction of the context has
;; to make it, and a stand that decides it alone cannot be checked offline.
;; The stands that used to decide it for themselves (`tests/support/
;; yeah-live-answer.el') are wrappers around this module now.

;;; Code:

(defun yeah-answer-shape (response)
  "Return the shape of RESPONSE.
The shape is one of the symbols `none', `empty', `text', `stream',
`reasoning', `tool-call', `tool-result', `error' and `unknown'."
  (cond
   ((null response) 'none)
   ((stringp response) (if (string-empty-p response) 'empty 'text))
   ((eq response t) 'stream)
   ((and (consp response)
         (memq (car response) '(reasoning tool-call tool-result)))
    (car response))
   ((and (consp response) (eq (car response) 'error)) 'error)
   (t 'unknown)))

(defun yeah-answer-answered-p (response)
  "Return non-nil when RESPONSE is an answer of the model.
Text with content and a tool call are answers: the model spoke, or it acted.
The empty string, the streaming sentinel, the reasoning and the result of an
earlier tool call are not: they are the road to the answer."
  (memq (yeah-answer-shape response) '(text tool-call)))

(defun yeah-answer-end-p (response)
  "Return non-nil when RESPONSE ends the request of the provider.
Everything but the road to the answer ends the request: the text that the
model wrote, the tool it called, the error of the provider and the sentinel
of a stream that is over.  The reasoning and the result of a tool that ran do
not end it: the answer comes after them."
  (not (memq (yeah-answer-shape response) '(reasoning tool-result))))

(defun yeah-answer-error (response)
  "Return the reason of an error RESPONSE, or nil."
  (when (eq (yeah-answer-shape response) 'error)
    (cdr response)))

(defun yeah-answer-text (response)
  "Return the text of RESPONSE, or nil when it carries none.
A text with content is the text of the answer; an empty answer carries none."
  (when (eq (yeah-answer-shape response) 'text)
    response))

(provide 'yeah-answer)

          :withdrawn (if input t :false))))

(defun yeah-acp-session-recover (request)
  "Start the oldest pending input of REQUEST and answer with the outcome.
Recovery is explicit: a pending input waits until the person asks for it,
and the journal says that it was recovered.

A run that is already active is not an error of the protocol: nothing is
recovered then, and the answer says so.  The answer names the INPUT that
was recovered, not the turn that carries it."
  (yeah-acp--require-session-id request "session/recover")
  (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state (plist-get request :sessionId) t))
         (control (plist-get state :control))
         (active (yeah-control-active-turn control))
         (input (seq-find (lambda (candidate)
                            (eq 'ask (plist-get candidate :kind)))
                          (yeah-control-pending control))))
    (if (and active (not (yeah-turn-done active)))
        (list :started :false)
      (let ((turn (yeah-control-recover-next control)))
        (if turn
            (list :started t :inputId (and input (plist-get input :id)))
          (list :started :false))))))

(defun yeah-acp--permission-decision (message)
  "Return the permission decision carried by client RESPONSE MESSAGE.
Only an explicit `allow-once' permits the effect.  A rejection, a
cancelled request, a protocol error, or an unknown option refuses it."
  (let* ((error (plist-get message :error))
         (result (plist-get message :result))
         (outcome (plist-get result :outcome))
         (state (plist-get outcome :outcome))
         (option (plist-get outcome :optionId)))
    (cond
     (error
      (list :effect :deny
            :reason "the client could not answer the permission request"))
     ((equal state "cancelled")
      (list :effect :deny :reason "cancelled"))
     ((equal option "allow-once")
      (list :effect :allow :reply :once))
     ((equal option "allow-always")
      ;; the person says that this action on this resource is allowed from
      ;; now on; the kernel remembers the decision
      (list :effect :allow :reply :always))
     ((equal option "reject-once")
      (list :effect :deny :reason "the person refused"))
     (t
      (list :effect :deny
            :reason "the client returned an unknown permission response")))))

(defun yeah-acp--turn-waiting-for (session-id request-id)
  "Return the turn of SESSION-ID that waits for the answer of REQUEST-ID.
The turn of a session is the one its controller runs: the answer of a
permission question reaches the turn that asked it."
  (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id))
         (control (and state (plist-get state :control)))
         (turn (and control (yeah-control-active-turn control))))
    (when (and turn
               (not (yeah-turn-done turn))
               (gethash request-id (yeah-turn-pending-permissions turn)))
      turn)))

(defun yeah-acp--remember-decision (question decision)
  "Remember an `always' DECISION for QUESTION in the rules of its session.
The decision is remembered for this session only: the standing permissions
of the service are not touched."
  (let ((session-id (plist-get question :session-id)))
    (when-let ((rule (yeah-approval-remember-rule
                      (list :action (plist-get question :action)
                            :resource (plist-get question :resource))
                      decision)))
      (let ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id)))
        (plist-put state :rules
                   (yeah-perm-rules-append (plist-get state :rules) rule))))))

(defun yeah-acp--route-response (message)
  "Route a client RESPONSE (a message with an id and no method) to the
permission it answers.  Return non-nil when it was a response."
  (let ((id (plist-get message :id)))
    (when (and id (null (plist-get message :method)))
      (when-let ((question (gethash id yeah-acp--pending-permissions)))
        (remhash id yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
        (let ((decision (yeah-acp--permission-decision message)))
          (when (yeah-approval-always-p decision)
            (yeah-acp--remember-decision question decision))
          (when-let ((turn (yeah-acp--turn-waiting-for
                            (plist-get question :session-id) id)))
            (yeah-turn-resume-permission turn id decision)))
        t))))

(defun yeah-acp--connection-closed (connection)
  "Cancel the work CONNECTION started and forget its pending questions.
A permission request whose asker is gone must never hang the run: the
turn is cancelled with the reason in the journal, and the request ids
of the dead connection are dropped."
  (let ((sessions nil))
    (maphash
     (lambda (id state)
       (when (eq connection (plist-get state :connection))
         (push id sessions)))
     yeah-acp--sessions)
    (let ((stale nil))
      (maphash (lambda (id question)
                 (when (memq (plist-get question :session-id) sessions)
                   (push id stale)))
               yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
      (dolist (id stale)
        (remhash id yeah-acp--pending-permissions)))
    (dolist (session-id sessions)
      (let* ((state (yeah-acp--session-state session-id))
             (control (and state (plist-get state :control))))
        (when control
          (yeah-control-cancel control "the client disconnected"))))))

(defun yeah-acp--dispatch (method params id)
  "Dispatch ACP METHOD with PARAMS and request ID.
Return a response string for immediate requests, or nil for notifications
and asynchronously answered prompts."
  (pcase method
    ("initialize"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-initialize params)))
    ("session/new"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-new params)))
    ("session/load"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-load params)))
    ("session/prompt"
     (yeah-acp-session-prompt params id))
    ("session/cancel"
     (yeah-acp-session-cancel params))
    ("session/steer"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-steer params)))
    ("session/withdraw"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-withdraw params)))
    ("session/recover"
     (yeah-acp--response id (yeah-acp-session-recover params)))
    (_
     (yeah-acp--error id -32601 (format "Method not found: %s" method)))))

(defun yeah-acp-handle-message (json-string)
  "Handle one JSON-RPC message string and return a response string or nil."
  (condition-case nil
      (let* ((parsed (json-parse-string json-string :object-type 'plist
                                        :array-type 'list))
             (method (plist-get parsed :method))
             (id (plist-get parsed :id))
             (params (or (plist-get parsed :params) '())))
        (if (null method)
            (when (yeah-acp--route-response parsed)
              nil)
          (condition-case err
              (yeah-acp--dispatch method params id)
            (user-error
             (yeah-acp--error id -32602 (error-message-string err))))))
    (error
     (yeah-acp--error nil -32700 "Parse error"))))

(defun yeah-acp--read-line ()
  "Read one line from standard input, or nil at end of file."
  (yeah-wire-read-line))

(defun yeah-acp--live-turns ()
  "Return the turns that run now, one per session at most.
The turn of a session is the one its controller runs: the wire drives the
sessions through their controllers, so the controllers know what runs."
  (let (turns)
    (maphash
     (lambda (_id state)
       (let ((control (plist-get state :control)))
         (when-let ((turn (and control (yeah-control-active-turn control))))
           (unless (yeah-turn-done turn)
             (push turn turns)))))
     yeah-acp--sessions)
    turns))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-acp-serve (&optional transport answerer output-function)
  "Serve ACP over standard input/output until EOF.
TRANSPORT and ANSWERER configure the agent for this service process.
OUTPUT-FUNCTION receives serialized JSON messages and defaults to stdout.
After each request the server lets the work it started settle, so an
asynchronous prompt answer leaves before the next request is read.
A cancellation that arrives while a prompt runs is therefore read only
after that prompt settled; `yeah-acp-serve-socket' does not have this
limit."
  (setq yeah-acp--transport transport
        yeah-acp--answerer answerer
        yeah-acp--output-function (or output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line))
  (let ((yeah-acp--output yeah-acp--output-function))
    (catch 'eof
      (while t
        (let ((line (yeah-acp--read-line)))
          (unless line
            (throw 'eof nil))
          (unless (string-blank-p line)
            (let ((response (yeah-acp-handle-message line)))
              (when response
                (funcall yeah-acp--output-function response)))
            (yeah-wire-pump-until
             (lambda () (null (yeah-acp--live-turns)))))))))
  nil)

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-acp-serve-socket (service &optional transport answerer family)
  "Serve ACP on the local socket SERVICE until the server stops.
TRANSPORT and ANSWERER configure the agent for this service process.
FAMILY is `local' for a Unix socket and `ipv4' for a loopback TCP port.
The connection is a process, so the event loop keeps running while the
server waits: a `session/cancel' that arrives during a running prompt is
handled while that prompt is still running, and two connections are
served at the same time."
  (setq yeah-acp--transport transport
        yeah-acp--answerer answerer)
  (yeah-wire-socket-serve
   service
   (lambda (line respond &optional connection)
     (let ((yeah-acp--output respond)
           (yeah-acp--connection connection))
       (let ((response (yeah-acp-handle-message line)))
         (when response
           (funcall respond response)))))
   family
   #'yeah-acp--connection-closed))

(defun yeah-acp--reset-for-test ()
  "Clear ACP sessions, listeners and pending questions for tests."
  (maphash
   (lambda (_id state)
     (when-let ((listener (plist-get state :listener)))
       (setq yeah-events-write-functions
             (delete listener yeah-events-write-functions))))
   yeah-acp--sessions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--sessions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--client-capabilities)
  (setq yeah-acp--counter 0))

(provide 'yeah-acp)
;;; yeah-acp.el ends here

;;; yeah-wire-socket.el --- the socket transport for Yeah's wire protocols -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The stdio transport of a wire protocol reads standard input with a
;; blocking read.  While that read blocks, the event loop of Emacs does
;; not run, so a notification that arrives while a request is being
;; answered is read only after the answer settled.  A reader thread does
;; not help: a thread blocked in `read-string' holds the interpreter lock,
;; and the whole Emacs stops until the read returns.
;;
;; A socket does help.  Emacs represents a connection as a process, so the
;; data of a connection arrives in a filter and the event loop keeps
;; running while the server waits.  A `session/cancel' that arrives during
;; a running prompt is therefore handled while the prompt is still
;; running, and two connections can be served at the same time.
;;
;; The transport is a local Unix socket by default; `ipv4' serves a
;; loopback TCP port instead.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire-socket nil
  "The socket transport of Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defvar yeah-wire-socket--pending (make-hash-table :test 'eq)
  "The part of the last line received on each connection.")

(defun yeah-wire-socket--lines (connection chunk)
  "Return the complete lines in CHUNK for CONNECTION and keep the rest.
The incomplete tail of CONNECTION is kept for the next chunk."
  (let* ((pending (gethash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending ""))
         (combined (concat pending chunk))
         (parts (split-string combined "\n"))
         (complete (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                        parts
                      (butlast parts)))
         (tail (if (string-suffix-p "\n" combined)
                    ""
                  (car (last parts)))))
    (puthash connection tail yeah-wire-socket--pending)
    complete))

(defun yeah-wire-socket--respond (connection text)
  "Send TEXT to CONNECTION as one line."
  (when (process-live-p connection)
    (process-send-string connection (concat text "\n"))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-server (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Listen on the local socket SERVICE and serve connections with HANDLER.
FAMILY is `local' for a Unix socket and `ipv4' for a loopback TCP port.
HANDLER is called with (LINE RESPOND CONNECTION) for every complete line
of input; RESPOND takes one message and sends it back to that connection.
ON-CLOSE, when given, is called with CONNECTION after it closed: a
question asked of a dead connection must not hang the server.
Return the server process."
  (make-network-process
   :name "yeah-wire-socket"
   :server t
   :family (or family 'local)
   :service service
   :noquery t
   :sentinel
   (when on-close
     (lambda (connection _event)
       (when (memq (process-status connection) '(closed failed exit))
         (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending)
         (funcall on-close connection))))
   :filter
   (lambda (connection chunk)
     (cond
      ((string= chunk "")
       (remhash connection yeah-wire-socket--pending))
      (t
       (dolist (line (yeah-wire-socket--lines connection chunk))
         (unless (string-blank-p line)
           (funcall handler line
                    (lambda (text) (yeah-wire-socket--respond connection text))
                    connection))))))))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-wire-socket-serve (service handler &optional family on-close)
  "Serve connections on SERVICE with HANDLER until the server stops.
FAMILY, HANDLER and ON-CLOSE mean what they mean in
`yeah-wire-socket-server'."
  (let ((server (yeah-wire-socket-server service handler family on-close)))
    (while (process-live-p server)
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05))
    server))

(provide 'yeah-wire-socket)
;;; yeah-wire-socket.el ends here

"Serialize OBJECT and pass it to the output function of this connection."
  (funcall (or yeah-acp--output yeah-acp--output-function
               #'yeah-acp--print-line)
           (json-serialize object)))

(defun yeah-acp--response (id result)
  "Return a JSON-RPC response string for ID and RESULT."
  (json-serialize (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id :result result)))

(defun yeah-acp--error (id code message)
  "Return a JSON-RPC error response string for ID, CODE and MESSAGE."
  (json-serialize
   (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id id
         :error (list :code code :message message))))

(defun yeah-acp--fresh-id (prefix)
  "Return a fresh id beginning with PREFIX."
  (setq yeah-acp--counter (1+ yeah-acp--counter))
  (format "%s-%d-%x" prefix yeah-acp--counter (random #x1000000)))

(defun yeah-acp--session-state (session-id &optional required)
  "Return the ACP state for SESSION-ID, optionally requiring it to exist."
  (let ((state (gethash session-id yeah-acp--sessions)))
    (when (and required (null state))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "unknown ACP session: %s" session-id))))
    state))

(defun yeah-acp-initialize (handshake)
  "Negotiate an ACP HANDSHAKE and return agent capabilities."
  (unless (and (listp handshake)
               (integerp (plist-get handshake :protocolVersion)))
    (signal 'user-error
            (list "initialize: protocolVersion must be an integer")))
  (yeah-acp--remember-capabilities handshake)
  (list :protocolVersion yeah-acp-protocol-version
        :agentInfo (list :name yeah-acp--agent-name
                         :version yeah-acp--agent-version)
        :agentCapabilities
        (list :loadSession t
              :promptCapabilities (list :image :false
                                        :audio :false
                                        :embeddedContext :false)
              :mcpCapabilities (list :http :false :sse :false))))

(defun yeah-acp--remember-capabilities (handshake)
  "Remember the client capabilities of HANDSHAKE for the current connection.
What the client announced is what it understands of the wire: Yeah's own
events travel to the clients that asked for them and to nobody else."
  (puthash yeah-acp--connection
           (plist-get handshake :clientCapabilities)
           yeah-acp--client-capabilities))

(defun yeah-acp--queue-events-p (state)
  "Return non-nil when the client of STATE asked for Yeah's queue events.
The queue events are Yeah's own vocabulary, not the vocabulary of ACP: a
client that does not know them refuses the whole update.  A client asks
for them in the `_meta' of the capabilities it announced."
  (let* ((capabilities (gethash (plist-get state :connection)
                                yeah-acp--client-capabilities))
         (meta (and (listp capabilities) (plist-get capabilities :_meta))))
    (and (listp meta)
         (eq t (plist-get meta yeah-acp-queue-events-capability)))))

(defun yeah-acp--validate-session-request (request &optional load)
  "Validate a session/new or session/load REQUEST.  LOAD selects its shape."
  (unless (listp request)
    (signal 'user-error (list "session request must be an object")))
  (when load
    (unless (stringp (plist-get request :sessionId))
      (signal 'user-error (list "session/load needs sessionId"))))
  (unless (and (stringp (plist-get request :cwd))
               (file-name-absolute-p (plist-get request :cwd)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "session request needs an absolute cwd")))
  (unless (or (null (plist-get request :mcpServers))
              (eq (plist-get request :mcpServers) :null)
              (listp (plist-get request :mcpServers)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "mcpServers must be an array or null"))))

(defun yeah-acp--send-update (session-id update &optional output)
  "Send a session/update notification for SESSION-ID and UPDATE.
OUTPUT receives the serialized message and defaults to standard output."
  (funcall (or output yeah-acp--output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line)
           (json-serialize
            (list :jsonrpc "2.0"
                  :method "session/update"
                  :params (list :sessionId session-id :update update)))))

(defun yeah-acp--content-chunk (kind text)
  "Return an ACP content chunk of KIND containing TEXT.
The content of an ACP chunk is one content block, not an array of them:
the protocol says so, and a client that checks the wire refuses a chunk
that carries an array."
  (list :sessionUpdate kind
        :content (list :type "text" :text (or text ""))))

(defun yeah-acp--tool-input (args)
  "Return ARGS as a JSON value for the wire.
The journal holds the arguments of a call in their printed form, because the
journal is a log of what happened and not a place for structured data.  A
client that shows the call wants the values themselves, so the printed form
is read back into them.

The arguments come from the model, so the printed form is read as data and
not as code: a form that the reader would evaluate is not read at all, and
the printed form travels to the client as it is."
  (if (stringp args)
      (condition-case nil
          (if (string-match-p "#\\." args)
              args
            (let ((value (car (read-from-string args))))
              (cond
               ((and (listp value) (proper-list-p value))
                (apply #'vector (mapcar #'yeah-result-json-safe value)))
               ((vectorp value) value)
               (t (format "%S" value)))))
        (error args))
    args))

(defun yeah-acp--tool-call (tool-call-id name status &optional input result)
  "Return a tool_call or tool_call_update ACP update for TOOL-CALL-ID.
INPUT is what the tool was called with and RESULT is what it returned.
The protocol has a field for each of them, and a client that shows the call
of a tool shows them: a call without its input is a name."
  (if (eq status 'started)
      (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate "tool_call"
                           :toolCallId tool-call-id
                           :title name
                           :status "pending")))
        (when input
          (plist-put update :rawInput input))
        update)
    (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate "tool_call_update"
                         :toolCallId tool-call-id
                         :status (if (eq status 'failed) "failed" "completed")
                         :content (vector (list :type "text"
                                                :text (or result ""))))))
      (when result
        (plist-put update :rawOutput result))
      update)))

(defun yeah-acp--input-update (kind fields)
  "Return an ACP update of KIND for a queue event with FIELDS.
The update names the input, its kind, the words the person wrote and, for a
withdrawal, the reason the input left the queue.  A field the event does not
carry is left out of the update."
  (let ((update (list :sessionUpdate kind)))
    (when-let ((input-id (plist-get fields :input_id)))
      (plist-put update :inputId input-id))
    (when-let ((input-kind (or (plist-get fields :input_kind)
                                (plist-get fields :kind))))
      (plist-put update :inputKind input-kind))
    (when-let ((prompt (plist-get fields :prompt)))
      (plist-put update :content (vector (list :type "text" :text prompt))))
    (when-let ((reason (plist-get fields :reason)))
      (plist-put update :reason reason))
    update))

(defun yeah-acp--update-for (type fields id &optional queue-events)
  "Return the ACP update for the journal event TYPE with FIELDS, or nil.
ID names the record.  QUEUE-EVENTS says that the client understands
Yeah's own queue events; a client that does not know them refuses the
whole update, so they travel only where they were asked for.  The
pending queue of a session is visible in the log: the events that move
an input in or out of the queue have their own kinds, so that the
editor learns the queue from the journal and keeps no state of its own."
  (pcase type
    ("user-message"
     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "user_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ("assistant-message"
     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "agent_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ("finish"
     ;; The summary of a finished run is the answer of the agent: the model
     ;; writes it for the human, and the editor shows it as the answer of the
     ;; run.  A client that speaks ACP expects the words of the agent as the
     ;; message of the agent, and a model that answers only through the
     ;; `finish' tool says nothing else.
     (yeah-acp--content-chunk "agent_message_chunk"
                              (plist-get fields :summary)))
    ("tool-request"
     (yeah-acp--tool-call
      (or (plist-get fields :tool_call_id) id)
      (plist-get fields :tool) 'started
      (yeah-acp--tool-input (plist-get fields :args))))
    ("tool-end"
     (yeah-acp--tool-call
      (or (plist-get fields :tool_call_id) id)
      (plist-get fields :tool)
      (if (yeah-events-boolean-p (plist-get fields :ok))
          'completed
        'failed)
      nil
      (plist-get fields :payload)))
    ((and (guard queue-events) "input-queued")
     (yeah-acp--input-update "input_queued" fields))
    ((and (guard queue-events) "input-taken")

        (last nil)
        (found nil))
    (dolist (call calls)

        (timeout (plist-get state :timeout))
        (attempt (plist-get state :attempt))
        (retries (plist-get state :retries))
        (backoff (plist-get state :backoff))
        (timed-out (plist-get state :timed-out))
        (status (plist-get state :status))
        (output (plist-get state :output)))

     ((and (not timed-out) (zerop status))

     (timed-out

                              :output output)))

                                :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)

     process

;;; check-client-sees-service-death.el --- the client notices the service is gone -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; A dead service that looks alive is the worst failure of the primary
;; path: the person types into a buffer nobody answers.  This check starts
;; a service, connects a client with an on-close callback, kills the
;; service, and proves the callback fires — the editor's line "the service
;; is gone" is built on it.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-service)
(require 'yeah-client)

(let ((failures nil)
      (data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-death" t))
      (name (format "death-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (closed nil))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (yeah-service-start name nil data-home nil t nil)
        (let ((client
               (yeah-client-connect (yeah-service-socket-path name)
                                    :on-close (lambda (_client)
                                                (setq closed t)))))
          ;; a deliberate close by the client is not a death
          (yeah-client-close client)
          (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 5)))
            (while (and (not closed) (< (float-time) deadline))
              (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
          (when closed
            (push "the client's own close was reported as a death" failures))
          ;; now the death: kill the service behind a fresh connection
          (let ((client2
                 (yeah-client-connect (yeah-service-socket-path name)
                                      :on-close (lambda (_client)
                                                  (setq closed t)))))
            (when-let ((process (gethash name yeah-service--processes)))
              (delete-process process))
            (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 10)))
              (while (and (not closed) (< (float-time) deadline))
                (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
            (unless closed
              (push "the client did not notice the service died" failures))
            (yeah-client-close client2))))
    (yeah-service-stop name)
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "client-death: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-client-sees-service-death.el ends here

;;; check-service-lifecycle.el --- a service Emacs answers a prompt -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The primary placement is a dedicated Emacs process.  This check starts
;; such a service, connects to it as a client, and drives one prompt over
;; the socket: the answer comes back with the end_turn stop reason, and
;; the journal of the service records the turn.  The model is a FAKE, so
;; no network and no key are needed.  The service is stopped afterwards.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-service)
(load (expand-file-name "tests/support/yeah-journal-files.el") nil t)

(defvar yeah-check--buffer nil
  "The buffer collecting the messages the client received.")

(defvar yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the client buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--send (connection object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line to CONNECTION."
  (process-send-string connection (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

(defun yeah-check--next-message (&optional timeout)
  "Return the next message the client received, or nil."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (message nil))
    (while (and (null message) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
        (goto-char yeah-check--position)
        (when (re-search-forward "^\\(.+\\)\n" nil t)
          (setq message (json-parse-string (match-string 1)
                                          :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))
          (setq yeah-check--position (match-end 0)))))
    message))

(defun yeah-check--response (id)
  "Return a predicate matching the JSON-RPC response with ID."
  (lambda (message)
    (and (equal (plist-get message :id) id)
         (not (plist-get message :method)))))

(defun yeah-check--await (predicate &optional timeout)
  "Return the next message that satisfies PREDICATE."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (message nil))
    (while (and (null message) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (let ((candidate (yeah-check--next-message 1)))
        (when (and candidate (funcall predicate candidate))
          (setq message candidate))))
    message))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "check-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-service-data" t))
      (connection nil))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (setq yeah-check--buffer (generate-new-buffer "*yeah-service-client*"))
        (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
          (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
        ;; start a service with a fake model
        (yeah-service-start
         name
         (concat "(defvar yeah-check--asked 0) "
                 "(defun yeah-check--transport (prompt callback) "
                 "(setq yeah-check--asked (1+ yeah-check--asked)) "
                 "(if (= yeah-check--asked 1) "
                 "(funcall callback \"the answer\") "
                 "(funcall callback (list 'tool-call "
                 "(list (list :name \"finish\") (list \"done\") "
                 "(lambda (_value) nil)))))) ")
         data-home
         "#'yeah-check--transport")
        (setq connection (yeah-service-connect name 6))
        (unless connection
          (push "the client could not connect to the service" failures))
        (when connection
          (set-process-filter
           connection
           (lambda (_process chunk)
             (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
               (insert chunk))))
          ;; the handshake
          (yeah-check--send
           connection
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion 1)))
          (unless (equal 1 (plist-get
                            (plist-get (yeah-check--await
                                        (yeah-check--response 1))
                                       :result)
                            :protocolVersion))
            (push "the service did not answer the handshake" failures))
          ;; a session
          (yeah-check--send
           connection
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "session/new"
                 :params (list :cwd data-home :mcpServers nil)))
          (let ((session-id (plist-get
                             (plist-get (yeah-check--await
                                         (yeah-check--response 2))
                                        :result)
                             :sessionId)))
            (unless (stringp session-id)
              (push "the service did not create a session" failures))
            (when session-id
              ;; a prompt
              (yeah-check--send
               connection
               (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 3 :method "session/prompt"
                     :params (list :sessionId session-id
                                   :prompt (vector (list :type "text"
                                                         :text "hi")))))
              (let ((answer (yeah-check--await (yeah-check--response 3) 5)))
                (unless (equal "end_turn"
                               (plist-get (plist-get answer :result)
                                          :stopReason))
                  (push (format "the prompt answered with %S"
                                (plist-get (plist-get answer :result)
                                           :stopReason))
                        failures)))
              ;; the journal of the service records the turn
              (let ((journal (car (yeah-journal-files--files data-home))))
                (unless (and journal
                             (string-match-p "assistant-message"
                                             (yeah-journal-files--read journal)))
                  (push "the service journal has no assistant message"
                        failures)))))))
    (when connection
      (ignore-errors (delete-process connection)))
    (yeah-service-stop name)
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "service: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-service-lifecycle.el ends here

(declare-function gptel-abort "gptel-request" (buffer))

(defcustom yeah-turn-nudge-message
  "Continue the work you were doing: call the tools you still need. Do not start the task over. When the work is done, say what you did and stop."
  "Prompt sent as a visible completion nudge when enabled for a run."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-turn-default-max-nudges 3
  "Default completion nudge budget.
The budget is positive: a run of the kernel is supervised unless a caller
asks for no supervision at all (a budget of zero).  A supervised run is
nudged when the model describes its next step instead of taking it, or when
it reports a result that no tool backs; the nudge names the tools the run
has not called yet.  A run that spends its budget without an effect says so
in the journal instead of looking done, and a run that is not supervised ends
as soon as the model answers with text."
  :type 'integer
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-turn-default-max-retries 2
  "How many times a request that the provider dropped is asked again.
A provider that drops the connection (a timeout of the transport, a closed
connection, a server that is too busy) did not refuse the request: the
request is asked again, and this budget bounds the tries.  A request that the
provider refused for a reason of its own (an HTTP status of the client, a
refusal of the model) is not asked again: the run fails and says why."
  :type 'integer

(defun yeah-turn--answer-text (turn answer transport answerer)

spent its nudge budget without an effect ends as a failed run: it did not do
the work, and it must not look as if it had.

The budget pays for the nudges that no effect answered.  A provider that
answers with an empty message after the tools of the model have come back
does not spend it: the model has acted, and a run that works must not be
ended by the noise of the provider."

                    (yeah-turn--context

           (= (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn) 0))

      ;; says nothing is no answer at all: the run fails instead of ending
      ;; as if the work were done.

                       "the model answered with an empty message and the run is not done")

           (acted (and silent (yeah-turn--acted-since-nudge-p turn)))
           (premature (or (yeah-turn--plan-p answer)

                          ;; model has not advanced, and the run nudges it into
                          ;; the action instead of taking the silence for the

                          ;; has not touched anything yet.  And a run that is
                          ;; supervised ends through `finish', not through talk.

        ;; nudge: the run asks again, and the noise does not spend the
        ;; budget.
