### 17.1 The open work of the code

**The delegation (Stage 7, after wave 36).**

- Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the audit of wave 35
  proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What is not proven is
  a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live provider.
- The model of the child is the model of the preset, and the preset names it;
  no child of a live provider has run yet on a model other than the model of
  its parent.
- The depth of the tree of the children and the children of a run are in the
  journal since wave 37: the journal of the run holds the short id, the
  session and the depth of every child, and the journal of the child holds
  where the child stands in the tree.  A restart of the harness finds the
  child of a run again and tells what became of it, and a child that the
  journal holds no end of is not reported as a child that still works.
- A child that was running when the Emacs died is not brought back to life: the
  journal says that the child was delegated and what became of it, and the
  work of that child is lost, because nobody restarts it.
- The live checks do not exercise the delegation: the benchmark gives its runs
  a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is not among them.  The live
  evidence of a child that works is the fixed point, and that is one child and
  one task.
- The tools of the delegation are not in `yeah-builtins-specs` (the built-ins
  are the tools of the kernel, and the delegation is a tool of the product),
  so a reader of that list does not see them.

**The turn, and what the provider and the model do.**

- A model can end its turn with a message that announces an action and call no
  tool ("I'll look at the current state of calc.el.").  The harness cannot tell
  a promise of an action from an answer: the completion nudge fires when the
  model is silent and not when the model talks without acting.  Since wave 39 a
  run of the kernel is supervised by default, so such a model is nudged into
  the action; a model that spends the budget without an effect ends the run as
  a failed run, and the ACP route answers `refusal` and not `end_turn`.
- The harness cannot tell the research from the work: a model that reads the
  whole repository, measures a race with experiments of its own and never
  changes a file makes calls of tools like any other model, and the nudge
  names the tools the run has not called yet — among them `edit` and `write`.
  Two live runs of the wave 41 (2026-11-17, 15:45 and 16:16) found that
  shape: 108 calls of tools, no change of the repository.  A guard that asks
  the model for the change after a number of calls of tools without one is
  open work; nothing in the harness does it yet.
- Since wave 47 the model is told what the run has done: every request of a run
  carries the transcript of the run before the prompt, and the transcript is a
  projection of the journal — the tail of the records of the run, cut at twelve
  records and six hundred characters of the result of a tool.  What it is not
  is a context: a long run pays for the tail of its own work in every
  request, and the projection of the context (`lib/yeah-context.el`), the
  compaction and the pruning are still not on the road to the model.  The
  transcript fixes the memory of the model and not the shape of the provider,
  which still answers with a plan instead of an action: the two live runs that
  found the defect of the transcript were made with a model of that shape, and
  the run on the code of wave 47 is the measurement that says whether the two
  together are enough.
- Since wave 48 a request that the provider dropped is asked again: the
  death of the transport is not the death of the run.  The retry is bounded
  (two by default), the journal holds it as a record of its own, and the
  model is asked the same question with the transcript of the run in front of
  it.  A request the provider refused is not asked again.  What the wave does
  not repair is the run that meets a provider that is down: such a run ends
  after the budget of the retries, where it ended before the wave.
- Since wave 49 the compaction of the context waits for the answer of the
  provider: the thinking of a model is the road to the answer and not the end
  of the request, and the outcome of a compaction is delivered once.  What the
  wave does not repair: the wait has no bound of its own, so a provider that
  thinks and then says nothing leaves the run in the state `compacting` until
  the deadline of the run cancels it, and the decision of an answer is the
  decision of the shapes of gptel, so a transport that answers with shapes of
  its own ends the request of a summary without a summary.
- A caller that wants the old behaviour of the kernel (a run that ends as soon
  as the model answers with text) must now say so with an explicit budget of

;;; check-service-lifecycle.el --- a service Emacs answers a prompt -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The primary placement is a dedicated Emacs process.  This check starts
;; such a service, connects to it as a client, and drives one prompt over
;; the socket: the answer comes back with the end_turn stop reason, and
;; the journal of the service records the turn.  The model is a FAKE, so
;; no network and no key are needed.  The service is stopped afterwards.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-service)
(load (expand-file-name "tests/support/yeah-journal-files.el") nil t)

(defvar yeah-check--buffer nil
  "The buffer collecting the messages the client received.")

(defvar yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the client buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--send (connection object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line to CONNECTION."
  (process-send-string connection (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

(defun yeah-check--next-message (&optional timeout)
  "Return the next message the client received, or nil."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (message nil))
    (while (and (null message) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
        (goto-char yeah-check--position)
        (when (re-search-forward "^\\(.+\\)\n" nil t)
          (setq message (json-parse-string (match-string 1)
                                          :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))
          (setq yeah-check--position (match-end 0)))))
    message))

(defun yeah-check--response (id)
  "Return a predicate matching the JSON-RPC response with ID."
  (lambda (message)
    (and (equal (plist-get message :id) id)
         (not (plist-get message :method)))))

(defun yeah-check--await (predicate &optional timeout)
  "Return the next message that satisfies PREDICATE."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (message nil))
    (while (and (null message) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (let ((candidate (yeah-check--next-message 1)))
        (when (and candidate (funcall predicate candidate))
          (setq message candidate))))
    message))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "check-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-service-data" t))
      (connection nil))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (setq yeah-check--buffer (generate-new-buffer "*yeah-service-client*"))
        (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
          (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
        ;; start a service with a fake model
        (yeah-service-start
         name
         (concat "(defvar yeah-check--asked 0) "
                 "(defun yeah-check--transport (prompt callback) "
                 "(setq yeah-check--asked (1+ yeah-check--asked)) "
                 "(if (= yeah-check--asked 1) "
                 "(funcall callback \"the answer\") "
                 "(funcall callback (list 'tool-call "
                 "(list (list :name \"finish\") (list \"done\") "
                 "(lambda (_value) nil)))))) ")
         data-home
         "#'yeah-check--transport")
        (setq connection (yeah-service-connect name 6))
        (unless connection
          (push "the client could not connect to the service" failures))
        (when connection
          (set-process-filter
           connection
           (lambda (_process chunk)
             (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
               (insert chunk))))
          ;; the handshake
          (yeah-check--send
           connection
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion 1)))
          (unless (equal 1 (plist-get
                            (plist-get (yeah-check--await
                                        (yeah-check--response 1))
                                       :result)
                            :protocolVersion))
            (push "the service did not answer the handshake" failures))
          ;; a session
          (yeah-check--send
           connection
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "session/new"
                 :params (list :cwd data-home :mcpServers nil)))
          (let ((session-id (plist-get
                             (plist-get (yeah-check--await
                                         (yeah-check--response 2))
                                        :result)
                             :sessionId)))
            (unless (stringp session-id)
              (push "the service did not create a session" failures))
            (when session-id
              ;; a prompt
              (yeah-check--send
               connection
               (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 3 :method "session/prompt"
                     :params (list :sessionId session-id
                                   :prompt (vector (list :type "text"
                                                         :text "hi")))))
              (let ((answer (yeah-check--await (yeah-check--response 3) 5)))
                (unless (equal "end_turn"
                               (plist-get (plist-get answer :result)
                                          :stopReason))
                  (push (format "the prompt answered with %S"
                                (plist-get (plist-get answer :result)
                                           :stopReason))
                        failures)))
              ;; the journal of the service records the turn
              (let ((journal (car (yeah-journal-files--files data-home))))
                (unless (and journal
                             (string-match-p "assistant-message"
                                             (yeah-journal-files--read journal)))
                  (push "the service journal has no assistant message"
                        failures)))))))
    (when connection
      (ignore-errors (delete-process connection)))
    (yeah-service-stop name)
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "service: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.
4. The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
   with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`, since wave 40), but

(defvar-local yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the server output buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--emacs ()

(defun yeah-check--start-server (feature expression)
  "Start a server process serving FEATURE with EXPRESSION.

    (with-current-buffer buffer
      (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
    (list (make-process
           :name "yeah-wire-test"
           :buffer buffer

                          "-L" (yeah-check--lib-directory)

  "Return the next complete JSON line in BUFFER, waiting at most TIMEOUT."

      (with-current-buffer buffer
        (goto-char yeah-check--position)
        (when (re-search-forward "^\\(.+\\)\n" nil t)

          (setq yeah-check--position (match-end 0)))))
    (and line (json-parse-string line :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi

;;; yeah-client.el --- an ACP client for the editor -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The editor is a client of a service Emacs.  This module is the client:
;; it speaks ACP over a Unix-domain socket or a loopback TCP port, matches
;; answers to requests by their id, and hands the session/update
;; notifications to the caller.  The session's journal is the service's
;; truth; the client renders the stream the service sends.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)

(defgroup yeah-client nil
  "The Yeah ACP client."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-client-network-family nil
  "Network family used to reach a Yeah service.
Nil chooses automatically: `local' uses a Unix-domain socket on
Unix-like systems, while `ipv4' uses a loopback TCP port on
Windows-like systems.  Set this to `local' or `ipv4' to override the
automatic choice; an IPv4 service publishes its port in a `.port'
file next to the socket path."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Automatic" nil)
                 (symbol :tag "Socket family"))
  :group 'yeah-client)

(defun yeah-client-automatic-network-family ()
  "Return the network family selected for the current platform."
  (if (memq system-type '(windows-nt ms-dos cygwin))
      'ipv4
    'local))

(defun yeah-client-effective-network-family ()
  "Return the configured network family for a Yeah service.
Signal `user-error' when the override is not a supported family."
  (let ((family (or yeah-client-network-family
                   (yeah-client-automatic-network-family))))
    (unless (memq family '(local ipv4))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-client-network-family: unsupported family %S"
                            family))))
    family))

(defun yeah-client-port-file (socket)
  "Return the file that publishes the TCP port for SOCKET."
  (concat socket ".port"))

(defun yeah-client--read-port (socket)
  "Return the TCP port published for SOCKET, or nil when it is unavailable."

;;; check-wire-speaks-over-stdio.el --- real ACP and MCP servers over stdio -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Start real Emacs processes serving ACP and MCP on stdio, exchange JSON-RPC
;; lines with them and read the answers back.  No network is involved.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)

(defvar-local yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the server output buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--emacs ()
  "Return the Emacs program to run the servers."
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS")) (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs")))

(defun yeah-check--lib-directory ()
  "Return the directory holding Yeah's Elisp modules."
  (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-mcp") "yeah-mcp.el")))

(defun yeah-check--start-server (feature expression)
  "Start a server process serving FEATURE with EXPRESSION.
Return the process and the buffer holding its output."
  (let ((buffer (generate-new-buffer "*yeah-wire-test*")))
    (with-current-buffer buffer
      (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
    (list (make-process
           :name "yeah-wire-test"
           :buffer buffer
           :command (list (yeah-check--emacs) "-Q" "--batch"
                          "-L" (yeah-check--lib-directory)
                          "-l" feature "--eval" expression)
           :connection-type 'pipe
           :noquery t
           :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                     (with-current-buffer buffer
                       (insert chunk))))
          buffer)))

(defun yeah-check--send (process object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line to PROCESS."
  (process-send-string process (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

(defun yeah-check--await-line (buffer &optional timeout)
  "Return the next complete JSON line in BUFFER, waiting at most TIMEOUT."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (line nil))
    (while (and (null line) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (with-current-buffer buffer
        (goto-char yeah-check--position)
        (when (re-search-forward "^\\(.+\\)\n" nil t)
          (setq line (match-string 1))
          (setq yeah-check--position (match-end 0)))))
    (and line (json-parse-string line :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))))

(let ((failures nil)
      (data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-wire-data" t)))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        ;; --- MCP over stdio ---
        (let* ((started (yeah-check--start-server
                         "yeah-mcp"
                         (format "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) (yeah-mcp-serve))"
                                 data-home)))
               (process (nth 0 started))
               (buffer (nth 1 started)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion "2025-06-18")))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (equal "2025-06-18"
                           (plist-get (plist-get response :result)
                                      :protocolVersion))
              (push (format "MCP initialize did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (yeah-check--send process (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "tools/list"))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (let ((tools (plist-get (plist-get response :result) :tools)))
              (unless (and (listp tools)
                           (cl-some (lambda (tool)
                                       (equal "emacs__buffer_list"
                                              (plist-get tool :name)))
                                     tools))
                (push (format "MCP tools/list did not publish the tools: %S"
                              response)
                      failures))))
          (when (process-live-p process)
            (delete-process process)))

        ;; --- ACP over stdio ---
        (let* ((started (yeah-check--start-server
                         "yeah-acp"
                         (format "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) (yeah-acp-serve))"
                                 data-home)))
               (process (nth 0 started))
               (buffer (nth 1 started)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion 1)))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (equal 1 (plist-get (plist-get response :result)
                                        :protocolVersion))
              (push (format "ACP initialize did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "session/new"
                 :params (list :cwd data-home :mcpServers nil)))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (stringp (plist-get (plist-get response :result) :sessionId))
              (push (format "ACP session/new did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (when (process-live-p process)
            (delete-process process))))

    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "wire: %s" failure))
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-wire-speaks-over-stdio.el ends here

(defun yeah-service--lib-directory ()

(defun yeah-service--rules-eval (rules)
  "Return the Elisp that installs RULES in the service.
RULES is a list of permission rule plists, as `yeah-perm-rule-make'

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-start (name &optional extra-eval data-home transport clean rules)
  "Start a service Emacs named NAME and return its process.
The service serves ACP on a Unix-domain socket, or on a loopback TCP port
when `yeah-client-network-family' selects `ipv4'.  In the TCP case the port
number is published in a `.port' file next to the socket path.  EXTRA-EVAL
is evaluated in the service before the server starts (to configure the
model backend); DATA-HOME is the service's data directory; TRANSPORT is a
form evaluating to the model transport of the service (nil uses the
default).  A service with the same name is not started twice.
CLEAN (the default) starts the service without the user's init; nil lets
the service inherit the user's configuration, including the gptel backend.
RULES is a list of permission rule plists: the standing permissions the
person grants the service, which is how a headless service may edit at
all."
  (let ((existing (gethash name yeah-service--processes)))
    (when (and existing (process-live-p existing))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-service-start: %S is already running" name)))))
  (let* ((socket (yeah-service--socket-path name))
         (family (yeah-client-effective-network-family))
         (port (when (eq family 'ipv4)
                 (yeah-service--reserve-loopback-port)))
         (server-form
          (if (eq family 'local)
              (format "(yeah-acp-serve-socket %S %s)"
                      socket
                      (or transport "yeah-acp-default-transport"))
            (format "(yeah-acp-serve-socket %d %s nil 'ipv4)"
                    port
                    (or transport "yeah-acp-default-transport"))))
         (buffer (generate-new-buffer (format " *yeah service %s*" name)))
         (process
          (make-process
           :name (format "yeah-service-%s" name)
           :buffer buffer
           :command
           (append (list (yeah-service--emacs-program))
                   (if clean (list "-Q" "--batch") (list "--batch"))
                   (list "-L" (yeah-service--lib-directory)
                         "-l" "yeah-acp"
                         "--eval"
                         (format "(progn %s %s %s %s)"
                                 (or extra-eval "")
                                 (if data-home
                                     (format "(setq yeah-data-home %S)" data-home)
                                   "")
                                 (yeah-service--rules-eval rules)
                                 server-form)))
           :connection-type 'pipe
           :noquery t)))
    (when (eq family 'ipv4)
      (condition-case error
          (yeah-service--write-port-file socket port)
        (error
         (delete-process process)
         (signal (car error) (cdr error)))))
    (puthash name process yeah-service--processes)
    process))

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-service-connect (name &optional timeout)
  "Connect to the service NAME and return the connection process.
Waits up to TIMEOUT seconds (default 10) for the socket to appear."

    (while (and (null connection) (< (float-time) deadline))

    connection))

(defun yeah-service-socket-path-internal (name)
  "Return the socket path of the service NAME."
  (yeah-service--socket-path name))

(defun yeah-service-stop (name)

    (remhash name yeah-service--processes))

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:
  smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings
  ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
  bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
  pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
  map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
  run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
  gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
  help                  — this text

Exit codes:
  0 — pass       (Green)
  1 — fail       (Red)
  2 — blocked    (input error)
  3 — unknown    (the method could not tell)

Environment:
  MATHC  — path to the math-coding binary (default: `mathc` on PATH)
  EMACS  — path to the Emacs binary (default: `emacs` on PATH)
EOF
    ;;

  smoke)
    echo "yeah-dev ok ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
    exit 0
    ;;

  byte-compile-all)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -d lib ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: lib/ does not exist" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    out="$("$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -f batch-byte-compile lib/*.el 2>&1)"
    rc=$?
    clean_bytecode
    printf '%s\n' "$out"
    if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation failed" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "Warning:"; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation produced warnings" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;

  ert)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev ert: needs at least one test file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev ert: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    load_args=()
    for f in "$@"; do
      load_args+=(-l "$f")
    done
    "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . "${load_args[@]}" -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
    ;;

  check)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev check: needs at least one check file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev check: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    rc=0
    started="$(now_ms)"
    for f in "$@"; do
      before="$(now_ms)"
      case "$f" in
        *.el)
          "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . -l "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *.sh)
          bash "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev check: unknown kind of check: $f" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
      printf 'check: %6d ms  %s\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - before ))" "$f"
    done
    printf 'check: %6d ms  total for %s file(s)\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - started ))" "$#"
    exit $rc
    ;;

  bench)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev bench: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -f bench/run-bench.el ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev bench: bench/run-bench.el does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    mode="--self-check"
    for arg in "$@"; do
      case "$arg" in
        --run) mode="--run" ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev bench: unknown option: $arg" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
    done
    # The task checks call emacs themselves: EMACS tells them which one.
    # gptel is not part of this repository: YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH names the
    # directory it is installed in, so the Yeah harness can reach a provider.
    clean_bytecode
    gptel_args=()
    if [ -n "${YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH:-}" ]; then

    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    exit $rc
    ;;

  *)
    echo "scripts/dev: unknown subcommand: $cmd" >&2
    echo "Run \`scripts/dev help\` for the list of subcommands." >&2
    exit 2
    ;;

;;; check-wire-speaks-over-stdio.el --- real ACP and MCP servers over stdio -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Start real Emacs processes serving ACP and MCP on stdio, exchange JSON-RPC
;; lines with them and read the answers back.  No network is involved.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)

(defvar-local yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the server output buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--emacs ()
  "Return the Emacs program to run the servers."
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS")) (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs")))

(defun yeah-check--lib-directory ()
  "Return the directory holding Yeah's Elisp modules."
  (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-mcp") "yeah-mcp.el")))

(defun yeah-check--start-server (feature expression)
  "Start a server process serving FEATURE with EXPRESSION.
Return the process and the buffer holding its output."
  (let ((buffer (generate-new-buffer "*yeah-wire-test*")))
    (with-current-buffer buffer
      (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
    (list (make-process
           :name "yeah-wire-test"
           :buffer buffer
           :command (list (yeah-check--emacs) "-Q" "--batch"
                          "-L" (yeah-check--lib-directory)
                          "-l" feature "--eval" expression)
           :connection-type 'pipe
           :noquery t
           :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                     (with-current-buffer buffer
                       (insert chunk))))
          buffer)))

(defun yeah-check--send (process object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line to PROCESS."
  (process-send-string process (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

(defun yeah-check--await-line (buffer &optional timeout)
  "Return the next complete JSON line in BUFFER, waiting at most TIMEOUT."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (line nil))
    (while (and (null line) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (with-current-buffer buffer
        (goto-char yeah-check--position)
        (when (re-search-forward "^\\(.+\\)\n" nil t)
          (setq line (match-string 1))
          (setq yeah-check--position (match-end 0)))))
    (and line (json-parse-string line :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))))

(let ((failures nil)
      (data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-wire-data" t)))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        ;; --- MCP over stdio ---
        (let* ((started (yeah-check--start-server
                         "yeah-mcp"
                         (format "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) (yeah-mcp-serve))"
                                 data-home)))
               (process (nth 0 started))
               (buffer (nth 1 started)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion "2025-06-18")))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (equal "2025-06-18"
                           (plist-get (plist-get response :result)
                                      :protocolVersion))
              (push (format "MCP initialize did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (yeah-check--send process (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "tools/list"))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (let ((tools (plist-get (plist-get response :result) :tools)))
              (unless (and (listp tools)
                           (cl-some (lambda (tool)
                                       (equal "emacs__buffer_list"
                                              (plist-get tool :name)))
                                     tools))
                (push (format "MCP tools/list did not publish the tools: %S"
                              response)
                      failures))))
          (when (process-live-p process)
            (delete-process process)))

        ;; --- ACP over stdio ---
        (let* ((started (yeah-check--start-server
                         "yeah-acp"
                         (format "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) (yeah-acp-serve))"
                                 data-home)))
               (process (nth 0 started))
               (buffer (nth 1 started)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion 1)))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (equal 1 (plist-get (plist-get response :result)
                                        :protocolVersion))
              (push (format "ACP initialize did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (yeah-check--send
           process
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "session/new"
                 :params (list :cwd data-home :mcpServers nil)))
          (let ((response (yeah-check--await-line buffer)))
            (unless (stringp (plist-get (plist-get response :result) :sessionId))
              (push (format "ACP session/new did not answer: %S" response)
                    failures)))
          (when (process-live-p process)
            (delete-process process))))

    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "wire: %s" failure))
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-wire-speaks-over-stdio.el ends here

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

## Summary of the conversation so far

### The task (from the user's original prompt)

Working in the Yeah repository (`/home/az/Projects/yeah-selfdev-2`, branch `main`), implement the **first half of wave 42** of the owner's plan (`docs/PLAN.md` §18.2):

- **Defect:** the ACP server process outlives the agent — a client that keeps the server's pipe open after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
- **Claim to register:** `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the server process is gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open.
- **Exit criterion:** a server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
- **Explicitly OUT of scope:** the second half (`the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent`) — do not register that claim, do not try to localize the spin.

Required deliverables:
1. Investigate how the server process is started/ended today (real servers, name file and line).
2. Implement a way for the server to end that does not depend on the client closing the pipe.
3. Write end-to-end check `tests/checks/check-the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over.el`; verdict must be decided by construction (deterministic).
4. Register the claim in `spec.json` with a control that breaks the subject; prove the control bites (check fails with exit code 1 and its own words) on a **copy of the tree**.
5. Document: `waves/wave-42.json` (fields: intent, touches, checks, claims, commitment, objection, refuted_by, note), an execution note in `docs/PLAN.md` §18.2, a bullet in `AGENTS.md` next to other wave bullets; state plainly what was not proved.
6. Verify only: `./scripts/dev byte-compile-all`, `./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el`, and the new check file. **Never** run `./scripts/dev run` or the whole `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*` suite (ten minutes; provider drops the connection).

**Hard rule:** the run's journal lives under `sessions/` — never delete it or anything else to make a check pass; any file a check deletes must be one the check itself created in a temp directory.

### Repository rules (from AGENTS.md / system prompt)
- `lib/` is Elisp only, one feature per file; public symbols `yeah-`, internal `yeah--`; domain errors as `user-error`; no telemetry; no global gptel hooks; subprocesses via `make-process`.
- Check the plan section and existing checks, don't read journals of past runs or git history.

### What has been established so far (findings)

**Server start/stop paths (named places):**
- `lib/yeah-service.el:133` `yeah-service-start` — starts the service Emacs via `make-process` with `:connection-type 'pipe`, argv = emacs `-Q --batch -L <lib> -l yeah-acp --eval "(progn ... (yeah-acp-serve-socket <socket> <transport>))"` (local family) or `(yeah-acp-serve-socket <port> nil 'ipv4)` for ipv4. Socket path under `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/yeah` or `/tmp/yeah-<uid>`; `.port` file for ipv4.
- `lib/yeah-service.el:196` `yeah-service-connect` — opens the client connection.
- `lib/yeah-service.el:~205` `yeah-service-stop` — `delete-process` + removes socket/port file. (Client-side stop only.)
- `lib/yeah-acp.el:798` `yeah-acp-serve` — stdio server; loops on `yeah-acp--read-line` (blocking `read-string`), ends only on EOF (`catch 'eof`).
- `lib/yeah-acp.el:825` `yeah-acp-serve-socket` — socket server; delegates to `yeah-wire-socket-serve` with handler and `#'yeah-acp--connection-closed`.
- `lib/yeah-wire-socket.el:57` `yeah-wire-socket-server` (make-network-process server), `:90` `yeah-wire-socket-serve` — loops `(while (process-live-p server) (accept-process-output nil 0.05))` — i.e. the socket server **never exits by itself**; it waits for the server process to die.
- `lib/yeah-acp.el:713` `yeah-acp--connection-closed` — cancels the run when a connection dies; does **not** end the process.
- `lib/yeah-control.el:241` `yeah-control-cancel` → `yeah-turn-cancel` (`lib/yeah-turn.el:1279`) — cancels the turn, marks done `interrupted`, aborts gptel FSM, cancels managed processes; does not exit the process.
- `lib/yeah-client.el` — client side: `yeah-client-connect`, `yeah-client-notify` (line 217), `yeah-client-close` (line 223), `yeah-client-request` (line 208).
- `lib/yeah-wire.el:50` `yeah-wire-pump-until` — pumps with `accept-process-output nil 0.05`.

**Measurements actually made with real servers (previous run, /tmp/measure-server.el, /tmp/measure-server2.el):**
- Idle/quiet ACP server (stdio, fake transport that never answers): `MEASURE pid=… ticks=4 … elapsed=10.04 percent=0.00%`; with a noisy child writing continuously: `ticks=10 … percent=0.00%`. So an ACP server sitting with a pending prompt is cheap; the spin lives on the live-provider path (gptel/url), not localized. `/proc/<pid>/stat` tick reading works (CLK_TCK=100; `string-after` does not exist in this Emacs — use `substring` + `string-match`).
- `json-serialize` in Emacs 30 requires keyword plists / vectors / conses with symbol keys — `:type "text"` inside a plist works, but `(list (cons "type" "text"))` and `(list (list :type "text"))` produce `wrong-type-argument (symbolp …)` / `(json-value-p :text)` errors. Use `:keyword` keys in plists and vectors for arrays.

**External context (out of repo):** Paseo plugin `yeah-provider` at `/home/az/Projects/PaseoPlugins/yeah-provider`; `server/yeah.ts` launches `emacs -Q --batch --eval LAUNCH_FORM` with `(yeah-acp-serve)` (stdio) and its `acpStream` closes the child's stdin when the SDK stream closes ("the process leaves by EOF") — but only when the stream is closed; the plugin does not currently send any "session over" notification. ACP SDK does define `session/close` (`node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/sdk/dist/acp.d.ts:59`) and `session/delete`, `session/set_mode`, `session/set_config_option`, `session/list`, `session/resume`, `session/fork`.

**Docs/context:** `docs/PLAN.md` §18.2 (lines ~2724-2790) and §16.30 item 2; `docs/PASEO-INTEGRATION.md` §2.10.4–2.10.5 records the leftover-process measurement (1,921,354 involuntary context switches, ~25–60% of a core) and states the plugin doesn't close stdin; AGENTS.md line ~162 has the "process of the ACP server outlives the agent" warning bullet; `docs/PASEO-INTEGRATION.md` line 729 mentions Paseo closing a session with `session/close`.

### Current tree state

- `git status`: only `lib/yeah-acp-vocabulary.el` modified (uncommitted) + untracked `sessions/`.

(defun yeah-acp--fresh-id (prefix)
  "Return a fresh id beginning with PREFIX."
  (setq yeah-acp--counter (1+ yeah-acp--counter))
  (format "%s-%d-%x" prefix yeah-acp--counter (random #x1000000)))

(defun yeah-acp--session-state (session-id &optional required)
  "Return the ACP state for SESSION-ID, optionally requiring it to exist."
  (let ((state (gethash session-id yeah-acp--sessions)))
    (when (and required (null state))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "unknown ACP session: %s" session-id))))
    state))

(defun yeah-acp-initialize (handshake)
  "Negotiate an ACP HANDSHAKE and return agent capabilities."
  (unless (and (listp handshake)
               (integerp (plist-get handshake :protocolVersion)))
    (signal 'user-error
            (list "initialize: protocolVersion must be an integer")))
  (yeah-acp--remember-capabilities handshake)
  (list :protocolVersion yeah-acp-protocol-version
        :agentInfo (list :name yeah-acp--agent-name
                         :version yeah-acp--agent-version)
        :agentCapabilities
        (list :loadSession t
              :promptCapabilities (list :image :false
                                        :audio :false
                                        :embeddedContext :false)
              :mcpCapabilities (list :http :false :sse :false))))

(defun yeah-acp--remember-capabilities (handshake)
  "Remember the client capabilities of HANDSHAKE for the current connection.
What the client announced is what it understands of the wire: Yeah's own
events travel to the clients that asked for them and to nobody else."
  (puthash yeah-acp--connection
           (plist-get handshake :clientCapabilities)
           yeah-acp--client-capabilities))

(defun yeah-acp--queue-events-p (state)
  "Return non-nil when the client of STATE asked for Yeah's queue events.
The queue events are Yeah's own vocabulary, not the vocabulary of ACP: a
client that does not know them refuses the whole update.  A client asks
for them in the `_meta' of the capabilities it announced."
  (let* ((capabilities (gethash (plist-get state :connection)
                                yeah-acp--client-capabilities))
         (meta (and (listp capabilities) (plist-get capabilities :_meta))))
    (and (listp meta)
         (eq t (plist-get meta yeah-acp-queue-events-capability)))))

(defun yeah-acp--validate-session-request (request &optional load)
  "Validate a session/new or session/load REQUEST.  LOAD selects its shape."
  (unless (listp request)
    (signal 'user-error (list "session request must be an object")))
  (when load
    (unless (stringp (plist-get request :sessionId))
      (signal 'user-error (list "session/load needs sessionId"))))
  (unless (and (stringp (plist-get request :cwd))
               (file-name-absolute-p (plist-get request :cwd)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "session request needs an absolute cwd")))
  (unless (or (null (plist-get request :mcpServers))
              (eq (plist-get request :mcpServers) :null)
              (listp (plist-get request :mcpServers)))
    (signal 'user-error (list "mcpServers must be an array or null"))))

(defun yeah-acp--send-update (session-id update &optional output)
  "Send a session/update notification for SESSION-ID and UPDATE.
OUTPUT receives the serialized message and defaults to standard output."
  (funcall (or output yeah-acp--output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line)
           (json-serialize
            (list :jsonrpc "2.0"
                  :method "session/update"
                  :params (list :sessionId session-id :update update)))))

(defun yeah-acp--content-chunk (kind text)
  "Return an ACP content chunk of KIND containing TEXT.
The content of an ACP chunk is one content block, not an array of them:
the protocol says so, and a client that checks the wire refuses a chunk
that carries an array."
  (list :sessionUpdate kind
        :content (list :type "text" :text (or text ""))))

(defun yeah-acp--tool-input (args)
  "Return ARGS as a JSON value for the wire.
The journal holds the arguments of a call in their printed form, because the
journal is a log of what happened and not a place for structured data.  A
client that shows the call wants the values themselves, so the printed form
is read back into them.

The arguments come from the model, so the printed form is read as data and
not as code: a form that the reader would evaluate is not read at all, and
the printed form travels to the client as it is."
  (if (stringp args)
      (condition-case nil
          (if (string-match-p "#\\." args)
              args
            (let ((value (car (read-from-string args))))
              (cond
               ((and (listp value) (proper-list-p value))
                (apply #'vector (mapcar #'yeah-result-json-safe value)))
               ((vectorp value) value)
               (t (format "%S" value)))))
        (error args))
    args))

(defun yeah-acp--tool-call (tool-call-id name status &optional input result)
  "Return a tool_call or tool_call_update ACP update for TOOL-CALL-ID.
INPUT is what the tool was called with and RESULT is what it returned.
The protocol has a field for each of them, and a client that shows the call
of a tool shows them: a call without its input is a name."
  (if (eq status 'started)

                           :toolCallId tool-call-id
                           :title name

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:
  smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings
  ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
  bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
  pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
  map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
  run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
  gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
  help                  — this text

Exit codes:
  0 — pass       (Green)
  1 — fail       (Red)
  2 — blocked    (input error)
  3 — unknown    (the method could not tell)

Environment:
  MATHC  — path to the math-coding binary (default: `mathc` on PATH)
  EMACS  — path to the Emacs binary (default: `emacs` on PATH)
EOF
    ;;

  smoke)
    echo "yeah-dev ok ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
    exit 0
    ;;

  byte-compile-all)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -d lib ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: lib/ does not exist" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    out="$("$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -f batch-byte-compile lib/*.el 2>&1)"
    rc=$?
    clean_bytecode
    printf '%s\n' "$out"
    if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation failed" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "Warning:"; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation produced warnings" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;

  ert)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev ert: needs at least one test file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev ert: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    load_args=()
    for f in "$@"; do
      load_args+=(-l "$f")
    done
    "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . "${load_args[@]}" -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
    ;;

  check)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev check: needs at least one check file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev check: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    rc=0
    started="$(now_ms)"
    for f in "$@"; do
      before="$(now_ms)"
      case "$f" in
        *.el)
          "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . -l "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *.sh)
          bash "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev check: unknown kind of check: $f" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
      printf 'check: %6d ms  %s\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - before ))" "$f"
    done
    printf 'check: %6d ms  total for %s file(s)\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - started ))" "$#"
    exit $rc
    ;;

  bench)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev bench: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -f bench/run-bench.el ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev bench: bench/run-bench.el does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    mode="--self-check"
    for arg in "$@"; do
      case "$arg" in
        --run) mode="--run" ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev bench: unknown option: $arg" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
    done
    # The task checks call emacs themselves: EMACS tells them which one.
    # gptel is not part of this repository: YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH names the
    # directory it is installed in, so the Yeah harness can reach a provider.
    clean_bytecode
    gptel_args=()
    if [ -n "${YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH:-}" ]; then
      gptel_args=(-L "$YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH")
    fi
    EMACS="$emacs_bin" "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch "${gptel_args[@]}" -L lib -l bench/run-bench.el -- "$mode"
    exit $?
    ;;

  pixel)
    if [ ! -f tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev pixel: tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    clean_bytecode
    bash tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh
    exit $?
    ;;

  map)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    ;;

  run)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . run
    ;;

  gate)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . run
    rc=$?
    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    exit $rc
    ;;

  *)
    echo "scripts/dev: unknown subcommand: $cmd" >&2
    echo "Run \`scripts/dev help\` for the list of subcommands." >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## Current warnings for every agent

- This is a kernel prototype, not a usable coding product.
- The parity with other harnesses was piloted on 2026-11-15, and the
  difference the pilot found was a defect of the turn, not a difference of
  quality: after the results of the tool calls arrive, the model may answer
  with an empty message, and the turn took that as the end of the work and
  stopped without the effect (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot of the
  parity").  The defect is fixed (the claim
  `an-empty-answer-does-not-end-the-run'), and the pilot on the fixed turn
  moved one task of three; the nudge now carries the state of the work
  (the claim `a-silence-nudge-carries-the-state-of-the-work'), because the
  provider goes silent after every batch of tool results and the model was
  answering the nudge by starting the work over.  With that, Yeah passes
  two tasks of three and pi passes three.  The third task failed in the
  tools: the `read` of a file nobody has edited yet returns no tick, and
  the `edit` refused the tick the model guessed as stale although the file
  has not changed; wave 26 makes a guessed tick ignored rather than
  refused (the claim
  `a-guessed-tick-does-not-refuse-an-unchanged-file'), and that task of the
  pilot passes now.  The provider was overloaded for hours (HTTP 529 to both
  harnesses), so the pilot of 15:02 measured one task of three and two
  blocked runs: the runner records a run the provider stopped as **blocked**,
  neither a pass nor a failure (the claim
  `a-provider-failure-is-not-a-failure-of-the-agent').  The pilot of 15:39, on
  the code of wave 28, measured two tasks of three — Yeah passed both of them
  and pi passed all three — and the third was blocked, because the transport
  to the provider died.  The parity of that run is not measured either.  The
  pilot of 17:06, on the code of waves 30+31, measured one task of three for
  Yeah and two of three for pi: all three runs of Yeah ended `unfinished`,

  failed on the **version token** of the file — the model copied 58 of the 64

  not changed (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot that measured the copy of the

(dolist (callback callbacks)
      (condition-case err
          (funcall callback completion)
        (error
         (message "yeah-control completion listener failed: %s"
                  (error-message-string err)))))
    completion))

(defun yeah-control--start-next (control &optional recovered)
  "Start the oldest pending ask in CONTROL when no turn is active.
A steering is not a task: it belongs to a run, and it is delivered at
a tool-batch boundary, never started on its own.
When RECOVERED is non-nil, the input was started explicitly by the
person and the journal says `input-recovered' instead of `input-taken'.
Return the active turn or nil when the queue holds no ask."
  (let ((active (yeah-control-active-turn control)))
    (when (and active (not (yeah-turn-done active)))
      (user-error "yeah-control: a turn is already active"))
    (let ((input (yeah-input-take (yeah-control-session control) 'ask)))
      (when input
        (yeah-control--write-taken control input recovered)
        (let ((turn
               (yeah-turn-run
                (yeah-control-session control)
                (plist-get input :prompt)
                (yeah-control-transport control)
                (yeah-control-answerer control)
                (or (plist-get (plist-get input :frozen) :budget)
                    (yeah-control-budget control))
                (or (plist-get (plist-get input :frozen) :max-nudges)
                    (yeah-control-max-nudges control))
                (lambda (finished)
                  (setf (yeah-control-active-turn control) nil)
                  (yeah-control--release-steering control)
                  (yeah-control--notify-completion control input finished)
                  (yeah-control--start-next control))
                (lambda (_turn)
                  (yeah-control--deliver-steering control))
                input
                (plist-get (plist-get input :frozen) :deadline-seconds))))
          (unless (yeah-turn-done turn)
            (setf (yeah-control-active-turn control) turn))
          turn)))))

(defun yeah-control-submit (control prompt &optional frozen on-complete)
  "Queue PROMPT with FROZEN data and return its persistent input id.
ON-COMPLETE receives one plist of shape
`:input-id ID :input INPUT :turn TURN-OR-NIL :state STATE'.  It is runtime
state only, never serialized with INPUT.  A queued input has its own completion
notification, and withdrawing it reports state `cancelled' with a nil turn."
  (let ((input (yeah-input-enqueue
                (yeah-control-session control)
                (yeah-control--frozen control 'ask prompt frozen))))
    (yeah-control--write-queued control input)
    (when on-complete
      (yeah-control-add-completion-listener control (plist-get input :id)
                                            on-complete))
    (unless (yeah-control-active-turn control)
      (yeah-control--start-next control))
    (plist-get input :id)))

(defun yeah-control-ask (control prompt &optional frozen)
  "Queue PROMPT as an ordinary ask with FROZEN configuration.
Retain the original return value: CONTROL's active turn, or nil when all work
finished synchronously.  Use `yeah-control-submit' to obtain the input id."
  (yeah-control-submit control prompt frozen)
  (yeah-control-active-turn control))

(defun yeah-control-steer (control prompt &optional frozen)
  "Queue clarification for the active run, or an ordinary ask when idle.
Steering is delivered after the current tool batch, never between tools."
  (let ((active (yeah-control-active-turn control)))
    (if (and active (not (yeah-turn-done active)))
        (let ((input (yeah-input-enqueue
                      (yeah-control-session control)
                      (yeah-control--frozen control 'steering prompt frozen))))
          (yeah-control--write-queued control input)
          input)
      (yeah-control-ask control prompt frozen)))
  (yeah-control-active-turn control))

(defun yeah-control-cancel (control &optional reason)
  "Cancel CONTROL's active turn, leaving pending inputs for subsequent runs."
  (when-let ((active (yeah-control-active-turn control)))
    (yeah-turn-cancel active reason)))

(defun yeah-control-recover-next (control)
  "Explicitly start the oldest pending input after a restart or cancellation.
The journal says `input-recovered': the input was started by the person,
not by the automatic continuation of a run."
  (yeah-control--start-next control t))

(defun yeah-control-pending (control)
  "Return CONTROL's pending inputs without executing them."
  (yeah-input-pending (yeah-control-session control)))

(defun yeah-control-withdraw (control id)
  "Withdraw pending input ID and complete its runtime listeners as cancelled.
The journal records the withdrawal with the id of the input: the pending
list of the editor is a projection of the journal, and a withdrawn input
must leave it."
  (when-let ((input (yeah-input-withdraw (yeah-control-session control) id)))
    (yeah-control--write-withdrawn control input "withdrawn by the person")
    (yeah-control--notify-completion control input nil 'cancelled)
    input))

(defun yeah-control-done-p (control)
  "Return non-nil when CONTROL has no active turn."
  (null (yeah-control-active-turn control)))

(provide 'yeah-control)
;;; yeah-control.el ends here

### 16.29 Проверка провода решает свой вердикт по построению — **сделано 2026-11-18 (волна 50)**

Проверка провода была флаки, и причина была в самой проверке: `yeah-check--raw`
читала части провода через `nreverse`, который разворачивает список на месте и
оставляет переменную на ячейке, бывшей его головой.  Второе чтение провода
находило одну часть, а не провод, а проверка читает провод много раз (рукопожатие,
сессия, ответ агента и байты провода в конце), поэтому её вердикт зависел от
того, сколько раз она читала провод до этого.  Свидетельство, чей вердикт зависит
от порядка собственных чтений, нельзя прочитать.

Первая часть волны починила чтение: список читается, а не разворачивается на
месте, и строки режутся по байтам до декодирования.  Проверка даёт один и тот же
вердикт на двадцати прогонах подряд.  Вторая часть делает это claim'ом, а не
надеждой: новая проверка берёт контроль claim'а о тексте на проводе (декодирование
байтов UTF-8, взятых из провода) и гоняет проверку провода против него двадцать
раз подряд в копии репозитория.  Каждый из двадцати прогонов должен упасть на
утверждении самой проверки, и каждый должен упасть одинаково: один и тот же код
выхода и одни и те же слова.  Прогон, который вешает Emacs, прогон, который
проходит, и прогон, который падает по-другому, — все они проваливают новую
проверку.

Волна переносит ожидание проверки провода с равенства текста на конец хода:
равенство — это утверждение проверки, а не условие ожидания, а ожидание, которое
просит равенства, ждёт весь таймаут на каждом прогоне, который сломал контроль.
Из-за этой одной строки цикл из двадцати прогонов новой проверки стоит
одиннадцать секунд, а не десять минут.

Новая проверка: `tests/checks/check-wire-check-decides-its-verdict-by-construction.el`.
Новый claim: `the-wire-check-decides-its-verdict-by-construction`; его контроль
(момент часов в словах проверки) применён к копии дерева, и новая проверка падает
там с одним отказом: девятнадцать из двадцати прогонов решили не так, как первый.

**Open:** ожидание проверки провода — это ожидание с таймаутом в тридцать секунд:
сервер, который отвечает на prompt и никогда не пишет сообщение агента,
заставляет проверку сообщить об отказе после таймаута — вердикт верен, ожидание
долго.  Новая проверка гоняет проверку провода против одного контроля (контроля
