### 17.1 The open work of the code

**The delegation (Stage 7, after wave 36).**

- Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the audit of wave 35
  proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What is not proven is
  a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live provider.
- The model of the child is the model of the preset, and the preset names it;
  no child of a live provider has run yet on a model other than the model of
  its parent.
- The depth of the tree of the children and the children of a run are in the
  journal since wave 37: the journal of the run holds the short id, the
  session and the depth of every child, and the journal of the child holds
  where the child stands in the tree.  A restart of the harness finds the
  child of a run again and tells what became of it, and a child that the
  journal holds no end of is not reported as a child that still works.
- A child that was running when the Emacs died is not brought back to life: the
  journal says that the child was delegated and what became of it, and the
  work of that child is lost, because nobody restarts it.
- The live checks do not exercise the delegation: the benchmark gives its runs
  a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is not among them.  The live
  evidence of a child that works is the fixed point, and that is one child and
  one task.
- The tools of the delegation are not in `yeah-builtins-specs` (the built-ins
  are the tools of the kernel, and the delegation is a tool of the product),
  so a reader of that list does not see them.

**The turn, and what the provider and the model do.**

- A model can end its turn with a message that announces an action and call no
  tool ("I'll look at the current state of calc.el.").  The harness cannot tell
  a promise of an action from an answer: the completion nudge fires when the
  model is silent and not when the model talks without acting.  Since wave 39 a
  run of the kernel is supervised by default, so such a model is nudged into
  the action; a model that spends the budget without an effect ends the run as
  a failed run, and the ACP route answers `refusal` and not `end_turn`.
- The harness cannot tell the research from the work: a model that reads the
  whole repository, measures a race with experiments of its own and never
  changes a file makes calls of tools like any other model, and the nudge
  names the tools the run has not called yet — among them `edit` and `write`.
  Two live runs of the wave 41 (2026-11-17, 15:45 and 16:16) found that
  shape: 108 calls of tools, no change of the repository.  A guard that asks
  the model for the change after a number of calls of tools without one is
  open work; nothing in the harness does it yet.
- Since wave 47 the model is told what the run has done: every request of a run
  carries the transcript of the run before the prompt, and the transcript is a
  projection of the journal — the tail of the records of the run, cut at twelve
  records and six hundred characters of the result of a tool.  What it is not
  is a context: a long run pays for the tail of its own work in every
  request, and the projection of the context (`lib/yeah-context.el`), the
  compaction and the pruning are still not on the road to the model.  The
  transcript fixes the memory of the model and not the shape of the provider,
  which still answers with a plan instead of an action: the two live runs that
  found the defect of the transcript were made with a model of that shape, and
  the run on the code of wave 47 is the measurement that says whether the two
  together are enough.
- Since wave 48 a request that the provider dropped is asked again: the
  death of the transport is not the death of the run.  The retry is bounded
  (two by default), the journal holds it as a record of its own, and the
  model is asked the same question with the transcript of the run in front of
  it.  A request the provider refused is not asked again.  What the wave does
  not repair is the run that meets a provider that is down: such a run ends
  after the budget of the retries, where it ended before the wave.
- Since wave 49 the compaction of the context waits for the answer of the
  provider: the thinking of a model is the road to the answer and not the end
  of the request, and the outcome of a compaction is delivered once.  What the
  wave does not repair: the wait has no bound of its own, so a provider that
  thinks and then says nothing leaves the run in the state `compacting` until
  the deadline of the run cancels it, and the decision of an answer is the
  decision of the shapes of gptel, so a transport that answers with shapes of
  its own ends the request of a summary without a summary.
- A caller that wants the old behaviour of the kernel (a run that ends as soon
  as the model answers with text) must now say so with an explicit budget of
  zero.  The default changed for every caller at once.
- A message that reports a finished work **and** announces the next step at
  the same time is a plan in part, and the harness does not see that part:
  `yeah-turn-plan-regexp` matches "I'll", "I will", "Let me", "Next I",
  "I'm going to" and "I am going to", so "All 15 tests pass.  Verifying the
  CLI end-to-end from a shell:" reads as a result.  The live coding run of
  wave 45 ended that way: the model announced a verification it never
  performed, and the run was completed.  The task was already done there, so
  the gap cost nothing; a task whose *last* step is the announced one would
  end as a completed run with the step missing.
- A run that ends on a text answer is a completed run even when the task
  asked for the tool `finish`: the live coding run of wave 45 was told to
  finish through `finish` and never called it.  The state of a run is
  therefore not a proof that the instructions of the task were followed; the
  check of the task is the arbiter.  Whether the kernel should require
  `finish` is a decision of the owner (§17.2).
- The budget of a child of a delegation is a separate default and is still
  zero: a child that only talks still ends as a completed child.  Whether a
  child that never calls `finish` is a failed child is a decision of the owner
  (§17.2).
- The provider answers with an empty message after a batch of tool results,
  with the status of a success (HTTP 200, `answer=""`).  Since wave 46 such a
  silence does not spend the budget of the nudges when the model has acted: the
  noise of the provider is not the refusal of the model, and a run that works
  must not be ended by it.  A model that never acts still ends, and the record
  of a run that did not finish says what the run did.
- The budget of the nudges is no longer a bound on the length of a run: it pays
  for the nudges that no effect answered, and a model that acts and then says
  nothing is not charged for the silence (wave 46).  The deadline of the run and
  the deadline of the request still bound it; a caller who wants a bound on the
  length of a run must set a deadline.
- The provider is overloaded for hours: HTTP 529 to both harnesses, a plain
  model call that answers with nothing now and then, and a transport that
  times out ("Curl failed with exit code 28").  A run that the provider stops
  is blocked and not a failure of the agent.
- A run that the provider *silences* and a run that the provider *fails* are
  not told apart by the runner of the benchmark: the silence is not an error
  record of the journal, so the runner records it as a failure of the agent,
  and a run that was never measured counts against the agent.  The pilot of
  wave 36 and the pilot of wave 37 measured the third task of Yeah in that
  shape (the sum was computed, the file was never written).  Whether that
  shape is a failure of the agent or a run that was never measured is a
  decision of the owner (§17.2), because it changes the number of every
  pilot (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the pilot after wave
  37").
- The reason of the row of such a run names the shape of it since wave 38:
  the model answered with an empty message N times, or it described its next
  step N times and called no tool.  The shape is what the journal of the run
  holds, and the verdict of the row is still the verdict.

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)
(require 'yeah-service)
(load (expand-file-name "tests/support/yeah-journal-files.el") nil t)

(defvar yeah-check--buffer nil
  "The buffer collecting the messages the client received.")

(defvar yeah-check--position nil
  "Position in the client buffer after the last line consumed.")

(defun yeah-check--send (connection object)
  "Send OBJECT as one JSON line to CONNECTION."
  (process-send-string connection (concat (json-serialize object) "\n")))

(defun yeah-check--next-message (&optional timeout)
  "Return the next message the client received, or nil."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (message nil))
    (while (and (null message) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
        (goto-char yeah-check--position)
        (when (re-search-forward "^\\(.+\\)\n" nil t)
          (setq message (json-parse-string (match-string 1)
                                          :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))
          (setq yeah-check--position (match-end 0)))))
    message))

(defun yeah-check--response (id)
  "Return a predicate matching the JSON-RPC response with ID."
  (lambda (message)
    (and (equal (plist-get message :id) id)
         (not (plist-get message :method)))))

(defun yeah-check--await (predicate &optional timeout)
  "Return the next message that satisfies PREDICATE."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 5)))
        (message nil))
    (while (and (null message) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (let ((candidate (yeah-check--next-message 1)))
        (when (and candidate (funcall predicate candidate))
          (setq message candidate))))
    message))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "check-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-service-data" t))
      (connection nil))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (setq yeah-check--buffer (generate-new-buffer "*yeah-service-client*"))
        (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
          (setq-local yeah-check--position (point-min)))
        ;; start a service with a fake model
        (yeah-service-start
         name
         (concat "(defvar yeah-check--asked 0) "
                 "(defun yeah-check--transport (prompt callback) "
                 "(setq yeah-check--asked (1+ yeah-check--asked)) "
                 "(if (= yeah-check--asked 1) "
                 "(funcall callback \"the answer\") "
                 "(funcall callback (list 'tool-call "
                 "(list (list :name \"finish\") (list \"done\") "
                 "(lambda (_value) nil)))))) ")
         data-home
         "#'yeah-check--transport")
        (setq connection (yeah-service-connect name 6))
        (unless connection
          (push "the client could not connect to the service" failures))
        (when connection
          (set-process-filter
           connection
           (lambda (_process chunk)
             (with-current-buffer yeah-check--buffer
               (insert chunk))))
          ;; the handshake
          (yeah-check--send
           connection
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 1 :method "initialize"
                 :params (list :protocolVersion 1)))
          (unless (equal 1 (plist-get
                            (plist-get (yeah-check--await
                                        (yeah-check--response 1))
                                       :result)
                            :protocolVersion))
            (push "the service did not answer the handshake" failures))
          ;; a session
          (yeah-check--send
           connection
           (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 2 :method "session/new"
                 :params (list :cwd data-home :mcpServers nil)))
          (let ((session-id (plist-get
                             (plist-get (yeah-check--await
                                         (yeah-check--response 2))
                                        :result)
                             :sessionId)))
            (unless (stringp session-id)
              (push "the service did not create a session" failures))
            (when session-id
              ;; a prompt
              (yeah-check--send
               connection
               (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 3 :method "session/prompt"
                     :params (list :sessionId session-id
                                   :prompt (vector (list :type "text"
                                                         :text "hi")))))
              (let ((answer (yeah-check--await (yeah-check--response 3) 5)))
                (unless (equal "end_turn"
                               (plist-get (plist-get answer :result)
                                          :stopReason))
                  (push (format "the prompt answered with %S"
                                (plist-get (plist-get answer :result)
                                           :stopReason))

              (let ((journal (car (yeah-journal-files--files data-home))))
                (unless (and journal
                             (string-match-p "assistant-message"
                                             (yeah-journal-files--read journal)))
                  (push "the service journal has no assistant message"
                        failures)))))))
    (when connection
      (ignore-errors (delete-process connection)))
    (yeah-service-stop name)
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory data-home t))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "service: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;; runtime dependency; when it is absent the check skips itself.
;;
;; The model is a FAKE that answers with text, so the check needs no

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'json)

(defun yeah-check--acp-client-dir ()
  "Return the directory of the independent acp.el client.
The environment variable wins, then the checkout sibling, then the usual
research checkout in the user's home."
  (let* ((library-dir
          (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-acp") "yeah-acp.el")))
         (candidates
          (delq nil
                (list (getenv "YEAH_ACP_RESEARCH_DIR")
                      (expand-file-name "../../emacs-agents-research/acp.el"
                                        library-dir)
                      (expand-file-name "~/Projects/emacs-agents-research/acp.el")))))
    (or (cl-find-if (lambda (dir)
                      (file-readable-p (expand-file-name "acp.el" dir)))
                    candidates)
        (car candidates))))

(defvar yeah-check--acp-dir (yeah-check--acp-client-dir)
  "The directory of the acp.el research clone.")

(unless (and (file-directory-p yeah-check--acp-dir)
             (file-readable-p (expand-file-name "acp.el" yeah-check--acp-dir)))
  ;; The independent client lives outside this repository.  Its absence is
  ;; a blocked check, not a passed one: exit 2 says "unknown", and a
  ;; check that cannot fail proves nothing.
  (message "third-party: blocked — the acp.el research clone is absent (%s)"
           yeah-check--acp-dir)
  (kill-emacs 2))

(add-to-list 'load-path yeah-check--acp-dir)
(require 'acp)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS")) (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the Yeah server.")

(defvar yeah-check--lib
  (expand-file-name (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-acp")
                                             "yeah-acp.el")))
  "The directory holding Yeah's Elisp modules.")

(defvar yeah-check--data-home (make-temp-file "yeah-acp-3p" t)
  "The data home of the server process.")

(defun yeah-check--await (predicate &optional timeout)
  "Pump the event loop until PREDICATE returns non-nil, at most TIMEOUT."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 10)))
        (done nil))
    (while (and (not done) (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output nil 0.05)
      (setq done (funcall predicate)))
    done))

(let ((failures nil)
      (notifications nil)
      (prompt-answer nil))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (let ((client (acp-make-client
                       :command yeah-check--emacs
                       :command-params
                       (list "-Q" "--batch"
                             "-L" yeah-check--lib
                             "-l" "yeah-acp"
                             "--eval"
                             (format
                              (concat "(progn (setq yeah-data-home %S) "
                                      "(defun yeah-check--transport (prompt callback) "
                                      "(funcall callback (list 'tool-call "
                                      "(list (list :name \"finish\") (list \"done\") "
                                      "(lambda (_value) nil))))) "
                                      "(yeah-acp-serve #'yeah-check--transport))")
                              yeah-check--data-home)))))
          (acp-subscribe-to-notifications
           :client client
           :on-notification (lambda (notification)
                              (push notification notifications)))
          ;; initialize
          (let ((init-result (condition-case err
                                 (acp-send-request
                                  :client client
                                  :request (acp-make-initialize-request
                                            :protocol-version 1)
                                  :sync t)
                               (error (push (format "initialize failed: %S" err)
                                            failures)
                                      nil))))
            (unless (equal 1 (map-elt init-result 'protocolVersion))
              (push (format "initialize answered %S" init-result) failures)))
          ;; a session
          (let* ((session-result (condition-case err
                                     (acp-send-request
                                      :client client
                                      :request (acp-make-session-new-request
                                                :cwd yeah-check--data-home)
                                      :sync t)
                                   (error (push (format "session/new failed: %S" err)
                                                failures)
                                          nil)))
                 (session-id (map-elt session-result 'sessionId)))
            (unless (stringp session-id)
              (push "session/new did not return a session id" failures))
            (when session-id
              ;; a prompt
              (acp-send-request
               :client client
               :request (acp-make-session-prompt-request
                         :session-id session-id
                         :prompt (list (list (cons 'type "text")
                                             (cons 'text "hello"))))
               :on-success (lambda (result)
                             (setq prompt-answer result))
               :on-failure (lambda (err) (push (format "prompt failed: %S" err)
                                               failures)))
              (unless (yeah-check--await (lambda () prompt-answer) 12)
                (push "the prompt was not answered" failures))
              (unless (equal "end_turn" (map-elt (or prompt-answer '())
                                                 'stopReason))
                (push (format "the prompt answered with %S"
                              (map-elt (or prompt-answer '()) 'stopReason))
                      failures))
              ;; the streamed updates arrived
              (unless (cl-some (lambda (notification)
                                 (equal "session/update"
                                        (map-elt notification 'method)))
                               notifications)
                (push "no session/update notification arrived" failures)))
            (acp-shutdown :client client))))

    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "third-party: %s" failure))
    (ignore-errors (delete-directory yeah-check--data-home t))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

bridge; it does not repair the harness and it does not measure the parity of
the harnesses.  The second criterion of the exit (two consecutive runs of the
method that end in `green`) depends on the human review of the plan of the
owner being fresh at the time of the run: that review is a decision of the
owner and not a machine verifier (docs/PLAN.md 17.2), and any later edit of
this plan makes it stale again.  The runs, their verdicts and their dates are
in docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.

(require 'ert)

(defun yeah-acp-test--parse (json-string)
  "Parse JSON-STRING as a plist."
  (json-parse-string json-string :object-type 'plist :array-type 'list))

(defun yeah-acp-test--prompt-request (id session-id text)
  "Return one valid ACP prompt request string for ID, SESSION-ID and TEXT."
  (json-serialize
   (list :jsonrpc "2.0"
         :id id
         :method "session/prompt"
         :params (list :sessionId session-id
                       :prompt (vector (list :type "text" :text text))))))

(defun yeah-acp-test--find-response (emitted id)
  "Return the emitted message answering request ID, or nil."
  (cl-find-if
   (lambda (text)
     (equal id (plist-get (yeah-acp-test--parse text) :id)))
   emitted))

(defun yeah-acp-test--stop-reason (text)
  "Return the stopReason carried by the response TEXT."
  (plist-get (plist-get (yeah-acp-test--parse text) :result) :stopReason))

(defun yeah-acp-test--response (method params)
  "Return the parsed JSON-RPC response of the ACP METHOD with PARAMS.
A notification that answers nothing gives nil."
  (let ((raw (yeah-acp-handle-message
              (json-serialize (list :jsonrpc "2.0" :id 99 :method method
                                    :params params)))))
    (and raw (yeah-acp-test--parse raw))))

(defun yeah-acp-test--result (method params)
  "Return the result object of the response of the ACP METHOD with PARAMS."
  (plist-get (yeah-acp-test--response method params) :result))

(defun yeah-acp-test--update-objects (emitted)
  "Return the update objects of the session/update notifications in EMITTED."
  (mapcar (lambda (text)
            (plist-get (plist-get (yeah-acp-test--parse text) :params) :update))
          (seq-filter
           (lambda (text)
             (equal "session/update"
                    (plist-get (yeah-acp-test--parse text) :method)))
           emitted)))

(defun yeah-acp-test--content-text (content)
  "Return the text of CONTENT, one content block or a list of them."
  (let ((blocks (cond ((vectorp content) (append content nil))
                      ((and (listp content) (consp (car content))) content)
                      (t (list content)))))
    (string-join (mapcar (lambda (block) (or (plist-get block :text) ""))
                         blocks)
                 "")))

(defun yeah-acp-test--pending-input (control id)
  "Return the pending input ID of CONTROL, or nil."
  (seq-find (lambda (input) (equal id (plist-get input :id)))
            (yeah-control-pending control)))

(defun yeah-acp-test--schema-path ()
  "Return the path of the ACP schema, or nil when it cannot be found."
  (seq-find
   (lambda (path) (file-readable-p path))
   (list (expand-file-name
          "../schemas/acp-v1.json"
          (file-name-directory (or (locate-library "yeah-acp") "yeah-acp.el")))
         (expand-file-name "schemas/acp-v1.json" default-directory))))

(defun yeah-acp-test--schema-methods ()
  "Return the names of the methods the ACP schema declares."
  (let ((path (yeah-acp-test--schema-path)))
    (when path
      (with-temp-buffer
        (insert-file-contents path)
        (let* ((schema (json-parse-string (buffer-string) :object-type 'alist))
               (methods (cdr (assoc 'methods schema))))
          (mapcar (lambda (method) (symbol-name (car method))) methods))))))

(defmacro yeah-acp-test--with-server (&rest body)
  "Run BODY with isolated ACP state, model transport and output.
The pending queue of a session lives in the temporary directory too: a test

(ert-deftest yeah-acp-initialize-negotiates-protocol-one ()
  (yeah-acp-test--with-server

                     (list :protocolVersion 1 :clientInfo '(:name "zed")))))
      (should (= 1 (plist-get response :protocolVersion)))
      (should (equal "yeah" (plist-get (plist-get response :agentInfo) :name)))
      (should (eq t (plist-get (plist-get response :agentCapabilities)
                               :loadSession))))))

(ert-deftest yeah-acp-initialize-rejects-string-protocol-version ()
  (yeah-acp-test--with-server
    (should-error (yeah-acp-initialize '(:protocolVersion "1"))
                  :type 'user-error)))

(ert-deftest yeah-acp-session-new-load-and-updates ()
  (yeah-acp-test--with-server
    (let* ((updates nil)
           (session-id (yeah-acp-test--new-session))
           (session (plist-get (yeah-acp--session-state session-id) :session)))
      (setq yeah-acp--output-function (lambda (text) (push text updates)))
      (yeah-events-write session "assistant-message" :payload "hello")
      (should (= 1 (length updates)))
      (let* ((update (yeah-acp-test--parse (car updates)))
             (params (plist-get update :params)))
        (should (equal "session/update" (plist-get update :method)))
        (should (equal session-id (plist-get params :sessionId)))
        (should (equal "agent_message_chunk"
                       (plist-get (plist-get params :update) :sessionUpdate))))
      (let ((loaded (yeah-acp-session-load
                     (list :sessionId session-id :cwd yeah-data-home
                           :mcpServers nil))))
        (should (equal session-id (plist-get loaded :sessionId)))
        (should (yeah-acp--session-state session-id))))))

(ert-deftest yeah-acp-prompt-answers-with-end-turn-stop-reason ()
  (yeah-acp-test--with-server
    (let* ((emitted nil)
           (session-id (yeah-acp-test--new-session
                        (yeah-acp-test--answer-then-finish "the answer"))))
      (setq yeah-acp--output-function (lambda (text) (push text emitted)))
      (should-not
       (yeah-acp-handle-message
        (yeah-acp-test--prompt-request 7 session-id "hello")))
      (let ((response (yeah-acp-test--find-response emitted 7)))
        (should response)
        (should (equal "end_turn" (yeah-acp-test--stop-reason response))))
      (should (cl-some (lambda (text)
                         (string-match-p "agent_message_chunk" text))
                       emitted)))))

(ert-deftest yeah-acp-prompt-answers-refusal-when-the-run-does-not-finish ()
  "A model that only describes its next step does not finish the run.
The wire must not call such a run done: the run is supervised, and a run
that spends its budget without an effect is not a completion."
  (yeah-acp-test--with-server
    (let* ((emitted nil)

;;; yeah-wire.el --- shared stdio plumbing for the wire protocols -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; In batch mode Emacs reads standard input a line at a time with
;; `read-string'; `read-char' does not see it.  A server therefore reads one
;; request, then pumps the event loop until the work it started has settled,
;; so asynchronous answers leave immediately instead of waiting for the next
;; request.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)

(defgroup yeah-wire nil
  "Shared stdio plumbing for Yeah's wire protocols."
  :group 'yeah)

(defun yeah-wire-read-line ()
  "Read one line from standard input.
Return the line without its newline, or nil at end of file."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((line (read-string "")))
        (if (or (null line) (string= line "")) nil line))
    (error nil)))

(defun yeah-wire-print-line (text)
  "Write TEXT and a newline to standard output.
TEXT is one message of a wire protocol, serialized as JSON.  The
serializer returns a unibyte string whose bytes are UTF-8, and printing
such a string as it is makes Emacs read every byte as a character of
Latin-1 and write it back as UTF-8: the client reads the text twice
over, and a Russian answer arrives as mojibake.  The bytes are decoded
as UTF-8 before they are printed, so the client reads what the model
wrote.

A text that is not UTF-8 is printed as it is: a wire that carries
broken bytes is better than a wire that carries nothing."
  (princ (if (and (stringp text) (not (multibyte-string-p text)))
              (condition-case nil
                  (decode-coding-string text 'utf-8)
                (error text))

  "Pump the event loop until PREDICATE returns non-nil or TIMEOUT seconds pass.
TIMEOUT defaults to 600 seconds.  Return non-nil when the predicate held."
  (let* ((deadline (+ (float-time) (or timeout 600)))

;;; yeah-acp.el --- ACP v1 agent over newline JSON-RPC -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Agent-side ACP v1 over newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0.  Sessions are real
;; Yeah sessions; prompt responses are sent when the run reaches a terminal
;; state; session/cancel is a notification; journal events become
;; session/update notifications through `yeah-events-write-functions'.
;;
;; A session is driven by a controller: the same one the attached path uses.
;; The controller owns the session's turn and its persistent pending queue,
;; so the wire can ask, steer, cancel, withdraw a pending input and recover
;; one.  There is no second queue in this module: the pending inputs of a
;; session are the ones the control keeps, and the queue the editor sees is
;; a projection of the journal -- the events that move an input in or out of
;; the queue reach the client as session/update notifications.
;;
;; `session/load' opens a session again and replays its journal: the records
;; of the session become session/update notifications, so that an editor can
;; rebuild the transcript of a session it opens a second time.
;;
;; An answer to a permission that arrives after the run that asked has ended
;; is not applied: the journal shows the question as deferred and the run as
;; ended, and the late answer changes nothing.

(defun yeah-acp--live-turns ()
  "Return the turns that run now, one per session at most.

sessions through their controllers, so the controllers know what runs."
  (let (turns)

(defun yeah-acp-serve (&optional transport answerer output-function)
  "Serve ACP over standard input/output until EOF.
TRANSPORT and ANSWERER configure the agent for this service process.
OUTPUT-FUNCTION receives serialized JSON messages and defaults to stdout.
After each request the server lets the work it started settle, so an
asynchronous prompt answer leaves before the next request is read.
A cancellation that arrives while a prompt runs is therefore read only
after that prompt settled; `yeah-acp-serve-socket' does not have this
limit."
  (setq yeah-acp--transport transport
        yeah-acp--answerer answerer
        yeah-acp--output-function (or output-function #'yeah-acp--print-line))
  (let ((yeah-acp--output yeah-acp--output-function))
    (catch 'eof
      (while t
        (let ((line (yeah-acp--read-line)))
          (unless line
            (throw 'eof nil))
          (unless (string-blank-p line)
            (let ((response (yeah-acp-handle-message line)))
              (when response
                (funcall yeah-acp--output-function response)))
            (yeah-wire-pump-until
             (lambda () (null (yeah-acp--live-turns)))))))))
  nil)

;;;###autoload
(defun yeah-acp-serve-socket (service &optional transport answerer family)
  "Serve ACP on the local socket SERVICE until the server stops.
TRANSPORT and ANSWERER configure the agent for this service process.
FAMILY is `local' for a Unix socket and `ipv4' for a loopback TCP port.
The connection is a process, so the event loop keeps running while the
server waits: a `session/cancel' that arrives during a running prompt is
handled while that prompt is still running, and two connections are
served at the same time."
  (setq yeah-acp--transport transport
        yeah-acp--answerer answerer)
  (yeah-wire-socket-serve
   service
   (lambda (line respond &optional connection)
     (let ((yeah-acp--output respond)
           (yeah-acp--connection connection))
       (let ((response (yeah-acp-handle-message line)))
         (when response
           (funcall respond response)))))
   family
   #'yeah-acp--connection-closed))

(defun yeah-acp--reset-for-test ()
  "Clear ACP sessions, listeners and pending questions for tests."
  (maphash
   (lambda (_id state)
     (when-let ((listener (plist-get state :listener)))
       (setq yeah-events-write-functions
             (delete listener yeah-events-write-functions))))
   yeah-acp--sessions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--sessions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--pending-permissions)
  (clrhash yeah-acp--client-capabilities)
  (setq yeah-acp--counter 0))
